title: fix(checkpoints): dispatch-approved silently ignores a valid approval when an older approval names a superseded draft PR
body:
## What

`pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh dispatch-approved` never launches a valid, unexpired `CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_APPROVED` when the same issue also carries an older approval for a **superseded** draft PR (or another runner). Discovery exits 1 without output and Pulse routes the draft to the stall path instead, where it waits up to the fleet window (`fleet_window_pending:86400s`) even though a maintainer has approved continuation.

## Why

The approval route is how maintainers unblock checkpoint drafts quickly. If an approval is silently ignored, maintainer time is wasted, the draft sits idle for up to 24h, and the approval expires unused. Nothing in the logs explains the failure.

## Evidence (managed private repo; identifiers replaced)

- Issue `#A` has two approvals:
  - an old one (Nov 10) for draft PR `#P1` (closed, superseded), minimised by comment hygiene as `outdated`; GraphQL `lastEditedAt: null`
  - a fresh one (Nov 12 19:33Z) for the current draft PR `#P2`, same runner
- `approval-template` for `#P2` regenerates a line byte-identical to the fresh approval, so the approval itself is valid.
- The Pulse log shows `revision dispatch issue=#A ... attempt_log=<path>`. The attempt log is **empty**. Dispatch then falls through to `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_REARM_BLOCKED ... reason=fleet_window_pending window=86400s` and `blocked:stale_draft_checkpoint`.
- Of 42 open worker drafts in that repo, this is the only one whose approval history names more than one `{pr, runner}` pair. Every issue whose draft is replaced after an approval will reach this state.

## Reproducer

1. On an issue with an open worker draft `#P2`, keep an earlier trusted `CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_APPROVED` line for a closed draft `#P1` (same issue, same runner). Minimise it as `outdated` without editing it, as dispatch comment hygiene does.
2. Publish a fresh approval for `#P2` generated by `approval-template`.
3. Run `pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh dispatch-approved OWNER/REPO REPO_PATH ISSUE LOGIN`, or wait for Pulse.
4. Observed: exit 1 with no output, and Pulse logs `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_REARM_BLOCKED ... fleet_window_pending`. Expected: discovery selects the `#P2` approval and proceeds to full validation and the fenced claim.

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` `_pcc_dispatch_approved` (around line 863):

```jq
[flatten[] | select(trusted) |
 select((.updated_at // .created_at) == .created_at) |
 .body | split("\n")[] | select(startswith("CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_APPROVED ")) |
 ltrimstr("CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_APPROVED ") | fromjson? |
 select(.repo == $repo and .issue == $issue) | {pr,runner}] | unique |
 select(length == 1) | ...
```

`_pcc_issue_comments` runs `_pr_checkpoint_normalise_hidden_unedited` (`pr-checkpoint-target-lib.sh:29`), so the hidden old approval is treated as unedited, which is correct per GH#36529. It therefore remains a candidate. Two unique `{pr, runner}` pairs fail `select(length == 1)`, `jq -e` exits non-zero, and `|| return 1` returns without printing anything.

## How

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-dispatch.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md`

Files to modify:

- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` — `_pcc_dispatch_approved` discovery.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-dispatch.sh` (or the nearest existing dispatch-approved test) — add a case for a superseded-PR approval plus a current approval.
- `.agents/reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md` — one sentence under "Approving a corrected released checkpoint" saying that the newest approval bound to the current open draft owns discovery.

Suggested approach (the worker may refine it):

1. Restrict discovery candidates to approvals whose `.pr` is the issue's **current open worker draft**, or select the newest trusted, unedited approval by `created_at`. Discovery is not authorization: `_pcc_dispatch` → `_pcc_target_row` and the claim helper still perform the full exact-head/brief/expiry/permission validation, so narrowing discovery does not weaken the fence.
2. Keep refusing genuinely ambiguous cases, such as two current approvals naming different runners for the same open PR. On refusal, print a sanitised diagnostic (for example `PR_CHECKPOINT_APPROVAL_DISCOVERY_REJECTED issue=#N reason=<ambiguous|none|unreadable> candidates=<count>`) to the attempt log instead of exiting silently.
3. Do not edit or delete published approvals as a workaround. The reference doc forbids editing them.

Reference pattern: `_pcc_blocked_release_evidence` in the same file already pairs evidence with the newest relevant episode instead of requiring global uniqueness.

## Acceptance criteria

- An issue with an old, hidden, unedited approval for a closed PR plus a fresh valid approval for the current draft dispatches via `dispatch-approved` (in a test with stubbed `gh`).
- Two simultaneous valid approvals for the same current draft that name different runners are still refused, and the refusal is logged.
- Discovery failures always write one diagnostic line. An empty attempt log no longer occurs.
- Existing checkpoint continuation tests pass.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-dispatch.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh
```

After release, the reporting maintainer re-checks the affected draft: the Pulse log should show `PR_CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_DISPATCHED` for it while its approval is still unexpired, or a new approval should be published if it has expired.

title: fix(pulse): REST-reserve serial dispatch mode stays sticky for the whole round after the budget recovers
body:
## What

When the REST-core budget is near its reserve at the start of a dispatch round, `_dispatch_max_compute_parallel` forces `max_parallel=1` (GH#29742). The round then processes **its whole candidate list serially**, even after the REST budget has fully recovered. `_dispatch_floor_loop` checks REST headroom on every iteration, but only to stop. It never returns to parallel mode.

## Why

Serial candidate processing costs 46s per benign dedup block and up to 300s per launch. A 60-candidate round therefore keeps the host far below its worker target for more than an hour after the budget recovers. That directly reduces Pulse throughput, against the policy of maximising throughput and throttling only while the cause persists (`reference/throughput-throttling-policy.md`).

## Reproducer

Evidence from 2026-11-13, one host, worker target 20:

- REST core fell to a few hundred requests remaining around 04:45Z (pulse log: `budget-priority: deferred deferrable stage ... rest=normal:178/5000`).
- 04:49:50Z: the round started with `Dispatch_max: available=20, candidates=60` followed by `Dispatch_max: REST-core reserve-adjacent mode forces serial launch ceremony (GH#29742)`.
- 06:14Z: `gh api rate_limit` reports core `4790/5000`. The same round is still serial at `loop iter=14`, after about 86 minutes, with 5 launches.
- Live host workers at 06:14Z: 3 of 20 (`ps` shows 3 distinct `headless-runtime-helper.sh run --session-key ...`).
- Blocked-candidate cost in this log: 18 `dispatch_with_dedup returned rc=1` attempts, 825s total, 46s on average.

## How

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh`

Suggested approach (the worker may refine it):

1. Record why the round is serial: REST reserve, throttle file, or slot budget. Only the REST-reserve cause can be revisited mid-round.
2. In `_dispatch_floor_loop` (around line 968), when the cause was REST reserve, re-evaluate `_dispatch_rest_core_requires_serial` every N iterations (for example 3) or every M seconds. Once it returns false, hand the **remaining** candidates to the existing parallel path (`_dispatch_max_compute_parallel` / the parallel loop used when `max_parallel > 1`) and log `Dispatch_max: REST-core recovered; resuming parallel launch ceremony at iter=<n>`.
3. Keep every existing fence: GraphQL circuit breaker, `_dispatch_rest_core_progress_allows_next`, stop flag, cooperative drain (GH#37907), the throttle-file serial escape hatch, and the effective slot cap.

Reference pattern: the existing mid-round restoration `effective_slots="$available_slots"` after `_DISPATCH_THROTTLE_CLEARED` in the same loop shows how to relax a round-start constraint mid-round.

## Acceptance criteria

- A round that starts serial because of the REST reserve resumes parallel processing within N iterations of the budget recovering. A stubbed test covers this.
- A round that is serial because of the throttle file stays serial, as it does today.
- No change to behaviour when the REST budget stays near the reserve for the whole round.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh
```

After release, check the reporting host's pulse log: after a low-REST start, a `resuming parallel launch ceremony` line should appear once `rate_limit` core is healthy again.

title: Make finished-worktree reclaim unconditional and fast enough for the pulse budget
body:
## Problem

The finished-worktree reclaim pass added in #37903 is gated behind
`AIDEVOPS_WORKTREE_RECLAIM_FINISHED=1`. The flag is set on no host, so the pass has
never run in the pulse cleanup stage: `~/.aidevops/logs/cleanup_worktrees.log`
contains zero `Finished-worktree reclaim` lines even though the stage itself runs
on cadence (`cleanup_worktrees.last-run` is current, budget 900s under
`reason=disk-headroom`). Every reclaim so far has been started by hand.

The flag was an interim concession while the removal path was unproven. It is now
proven: 22 removals, 0 failures, 98 GB reclaimed, and 73 refusals that each name a
real reason. Leaving it off means worktrees accumulate until a person notices the
disk filling, which is the failure this work set out to remove.

## Required change

Remove the flag and its conditional. The reclaim pass becomes a normal third pass
of the cleanup stage, taking an equal share of the stage budget.

An always-on pass is budget-bound in a way a manual run is not, and the current
pass is far slower than its checks need to be. Measured per candidate:

| Step | Cost |
|------|------|
| `process_census()` | 0.03s once per pass |
| `git status --untracked-files=all` | 0.2–0.3s, including 5 GB trees |
| `git rev-list --count` | 0.14s |
| `gh issue view` per reference | 1.05s |
| `directory_size()` per authorized tree | 4.3s on a 5 GB tree |

A 95-candidate scan took 442s. Two steps account for nearly all of it, and both
are avoidable:

1. **Per-reference GitHub queries**: ~93s for 89 candidates. One batched GraphQL
   query per repository resolves 20 references in 1.14s. A batch containing a
   nonexistent number exits non-zero but still returns the resolved aliases on
   stdout, so partial results must be parsed regardless of exit code and absent
   aliases left to the existing per-reference fallback.

2. **Per-tree directory walks**: ~110s, purely to report bytes. The pass-level
   total is available from the free-space delta on the base directory at two
   `statvfs` calls, so the per-tree walk buys nothing the receipt needs.

With both fixed, the GitHub resolution becomes effectively free and the local state
checks run only for the candidates whose work has finished — 22 of 89 today, not
all 89, because `evidence()` already asks GitHub before touching local state.
Projected full scan: 15–20s, comfortably inside a 300s share.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup-worktree-removal.sh`: drop `reclaim_enabled` and
  the `AIDEVOPS_WORKTREE_RECLAIM_FINISHED` conditional; always split the budget
  three ways and always call `_cleanup_reclaim_finished_worktrees`. The stage
  minimum budget rises from 2 to 3.
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_reclaim_evidence.py`: add a batched prefetch that
  fills the same cache `reference_finished` reads, so a failed batch degrades to
  today's per-reference behaviour.
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_reclaim_host.py`: replace `directory_size` with
  `free_bytes`.
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-reclaim-finished.py`: prefetch before judging, and
  report `reclaimed_bytes` from the free-space delta.
- `.agents/reference/worktree-registry.md`: replace the opt-in section with the
  always-on contract, keeping the stated residual gaps.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-reclaim-finished.py`: cover batch
  population, degradation when a batch fails, and the free-space accounting.

## Reference pattern

The budget split and pass invocation already exist in `cleanup_worktrees()`; this
removes a branch rather than adding one.

## Verification

- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-reclaim-finished.py` — all pass.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup-worktree-removal.sh` — zero findings.
- `rg -n "AIDEVOPS_WORKTREE_RECLAIM_FINISHED" .` — no matches outside history.
- A live dry run completes in well under 60s and reports the same verdicts as the
  pre-change run for unchanged trees.
- After deployment, `~/.aidevops/logs/cleanup_worktrees.log` shows a
  `Finished-worktree reclaim:` line from a pulse-driven run nobody started.

## Out of scope

The six-proof evidence collector that `cleanup_policy.decide_cleanup` still lacks.
This pass continues to supply none of those proofs and claims no cleanup
authorization.

title: fix(pulse): stale-blocked stage starves the partial-continuation revisit on large repos, stranding merged For-#N partials in status:in-review
body:
## What

On a large managed repository, the GH#34432 partial-continuation revisit (`_pm_reconcile_partial_continuations`) has not run for about 20 hours, and has not completed a traversal for 11 days. Every cycle the stale-blocked stage defers it with:

```text
[pulse-wrapper] stale-blocked sweep: partial-continuation pass deferred for <repo>: sweep deadline reached (GH#36041)
```

Issues whose worker partial PR (`For #N`) merged while the merge-time hook could not restore them stay `status:in-review` with no open PR. The dispatcher never sees them, and their phase dependants stay `status:blocked`.

## Why

This is a throughput blocker. On the affected repository, 50 open issues were stranded in `status:in-review`. Each had a merged `For #N` PR, no open PR and a finished worker release. The oldest had been stranded since 2026-10-15.

Running the canonical restore by hand, unchanged and with all its guards, returned them to `status:available` with `auto-dispatch` (see Reproducer). The guards therefore accept these issues, and the fault is only in scheduling.

## Reproducer

Evidence from 2026-11-13, one runner, v3.39.187:

- Each sweep logs `stale-blocked reconciliation completed failures=0 partial_repos=70 repos=70 fresh_repos=0 cadence=1800s`: no repository ever completes inside the 60s stage (`PULSE_STALE_BLOCKED_RECONCILE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` default, minus the 15s margin).
- On the large repository, each stale pass logs `candidates=337 pending=189 visited=1 checked=1 complete=false`. Listing the candidates consumes the share, so one blocked issue is visited per cycle. Cycles on this host currently take more than an hour.
- `_pulse_stale_blocked_run_and_measure` passes `DER_STALE_BLOCKED_STOP_EPOCH=$sweep_deadline` to the stale pass. A pass that overruns its own `stale_deadline` can therefore consume the reserve that GH#36041 holds for the later passes. Both optional passes then defer at the `pass_now >= sweep_deadline` check in `_pulse_stale_blocked_optional_pass`.
- `~/.aidevops/cache/partial-continuation/<repo>` was last written 2026-11-12T10:52Z (page 3). `~/.aidevops/cache/partial-continuation-complete/<repo>` is dated 2026-11-02.
- The revisit lists **all** open issues, 10 per page, and does several REST reads for each one: issue, comments, timeline, PR view, and every open-PR page through `_pmpc_other_open_pr_owns_issue`. Only `status:in-review` issues (restore) and unassigned `status:available` worker issues (`_pmpc_restore_available_dispatch`) can change. On this repository (about 390 open issues, 57 in review) about 85% of the reads cannot lead to an action.
- Manual canonical run (sourcing the deployed `pulse-merge.sh` chain and calling `_pm_restore_partial_continuation <pr> <repo> "" "" <issue>`): returned `#N to status:available (auto-dispatch added, released: <runner>) after partial PR #M (GH#34312)` for each eligible stranded issue. Unlabeled PRs without the worker body marker were correctly refused by `_pmpc_unlabeled_worker_provenance`.

## How

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh` (`_pm_reconcile_partial_continuations`)
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh` (`_pulse_stale_blocked_sweep_repo`, `_pulse_stale_blocked_run_and_measure`, `_pulse_stale_blocked_optional_pass`)
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-blocked-reconcile.sh`

Suggested approach (the worker may refine it):

1. **Narrow the revisit to candidates.** List `issues?state=open&labels=status:in-review` for the restore path, and unassigned `status:available` `origin:worker` issues without `auto-dispatch` for `_pmpc_restore_available_dispatch`, instead of every open issue. Keep the per-repo cursor and the persist-before-process ordering (GH#34432).
2. **Stop starvation.** Give the stale pass a hard stop at its own `stale_deadline`, or `sweep_deadline - later_reserve`, rather than `sweep_deadline`, so the GH#36041 reserve is actually kept. Alternatively, when an optional pass's complete stamp is older than a bound (for example `4 * interval`), run it **before** the stale pass for that repository.
3. Add a log line or a `pulse-health.json` counter for the age of each pass's complete stamp, so starvation shows up in `pulse-health`.

Reference pattern: GH#36041 already reserves time for later passes (`_pulse_stale_blocked_later_reserve`). The fix is to make that reserve binding when the stale pass overruns.

## Acceptance criteria

- On a repository where the stale pass cannot finish in its share, the partial-continuation pass still runs every sweep. A stubbed test makes the stale pass overrun and asserts that the optional pass is invoked with a non-expired deadline.
- `_pm_reconcile_partial_continuations` visits only label-filtered candidates. A test asserts that a non-candidate open issue causes no timeline or comment read.
- A merged worker `For #N` partial whose merge-time hook was skipped is returned to `status:available` within one sweep cadence on a repository with more than 300 open issues.
- The existing GH#34312, GH#34432 and GH#37043 guards and tests are unchanged.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-blocked-reconcile.sh
```

After release, the reporting host's pulse log should show no `partial-continuation pass deferred ... sweep deadline reached` lines for consecutive sweeps. The `partial-continuation-complete/<repo>` stamp should refresh at least daily.

title: Promote ruff and mypy configs to the repository root so onboarding a package costs one line
body:
## Problem

`ruff` and `mypy` are configured only inside one component. CI runs
`ruff check --no-cache .agents/worker-lifecycle` and
`mypy --config-file .agents/worker-lifecycle/mypy.ini`, so every other Python file
in the repository is linted by neither. That includes the three reclaim modules in
`.agents/scripts/` added by #37903 and #38037, which carry a destructive code path
and have never been type-checked.

Adding a second component the same way would create a second pair of config files
and a third CI step, which is the duplication this change exists to prevent. The
existing config already prescribes the alternative in its own comment: "Initial
strict scope; legacy Python keeps its existing pyflakes/lizard checks. Extend
include as other packages are migrated, rather than masking violations."

## Required change

Promote both configs to the repository root and express per-package scope inside
them, so onboarding a package costs one line per config instead of two new files.

- Root `ruff.toml`: keep `required-version`, `target-version` and the current
  `select`; replace the implicit component scope with an explicit `include` list
  naming migrated packages. Unmigrated Python stays outside `include`, so nothing
  is masked by ignores.
- Root `mypy.ini`: set `mypy_path` to the component roots so top-level packages in
  different directories both resolve, list migrated packages in `files`, and use
  per-module sections for any package-specific strictness.
- `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml`: invoke `ruff check --no-cache` and
  `mypy --config-file mypy.ini --platform linux|darwin` without component paths.

## Scope decision

`.agents/scripts/*.py` is NOT added to `include` in this change. Those files have
never been checked, so adding them here would mix a config move with an unknown
volume of fixes. They are onboarded when the reclaim modules move into their own
component, which is the next piece of work.

## Files to modify

- `ruff.toml` (new, at repository root; moved from `.agents/worker-lifecycle/`)
- `mypy.ini` (new, at repository root; moved from `.agents/worker-lifecycle/`)
- `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml`: the lint and typecheck steps

## Risk to control

A root config that CI does not reference is worse than no config: it reads as
configured while checking nothing. The config move and the workflow edit must land
in the same commit, and the PR must show the new invocations passing in CI rather
than being skipped.

## Verification

- `ruff check --no-cache` from the repository root reports the same findings for
  the worker-lifecycle package as `ruff check --no-cache .agents/worker-lifecycle`
  does today.
- `mypy --config-file mypy.ini --platform linux` and the darwin variant both pass.
- `rg -n "worker-lifecycle/(ruff.toml|mypy.ini)" .github/` returns nothing.
- CI shows the lint and typecheck steps executing, not skipped.

title: fix(worker): headless worker PRs still created and merged without origin labels; marker-less partials strand targets in status:in-review
body:
## What

Headless worker PRs are still being created and merged with **no `origin:*` label**. GH#37859 (GH#37204) assumed creation-time enforcement (`_gh_create_pr_enforce_origin_postcondition`, `_reconcile_pr_origin_label`) prevents this, and it only added recovery for label-less PRs that still carry the `<!-- aidevops:origin:worker -->` body marker.

Most of the affected PRs carry no marker and no signature either. Their worker partial PRs (`For #N`) therefore strand the target issue in `status:in-review`: `_pmpc_unlabeled_worker_provenance` correctly refuses them, and nothing returns the issue to the queue.

## Why

On one managed repository, 8 issues were stranded this way (worker partials merged 2026-11-12 to 2026-11-13). Phase dependants stay blocked until an operator intervenes. Missing provenance also weakens every origin-based gate (merge policy, partial continuation, attribution).

## Reproducer

Evidence from 2026-11-13. Runners are on v3.39.185 to v3.39.187 (versions taken from the `DISPATCH_CLAIM version=` fields).

**Symptom command:**

```bash
gh pr list --repo <owner>/<repo> --state merged --limit 120 \
  --json number,author,headRefName,labels,body \
  --jq '.[] | select(.headRefName | test("^feature/auto-"))
        | select(([.labels[].name | select(startswith("origin:"))] | length) == 0)
        | "\(.number) \(.author.login) marker=\(.body | contains("aidevops:origin:worker")) sig=\(.body | contains("aidevops:sig"))"'
```

**Actual output** (excerpt, logins replaced):

```text
23288 runner-a marker=true sig=true
23195 runner-a marker=false sig=false
23101 runner-b marker=false sig=false
23083 runner-a marker=false sig=false
... (21 rows in total)
```

**Expected output:** no rows. Every `feature/auto-*` worker PR should carry `origin:worker` or `origin:worker-takeover`.

- Of the last 120 merged PRs on that repository, 113 are on `feature/auto-*` branches. One runner authored 102 of them, and 20 of those have no `origin:*` label. Another runner authored 11, and 1 of those has no label. A third runner authored 4, and all 4 are labelled.
- **Class A, raw creation (13 PRs):** no label, no `aidevops:origin:worker` marker, no `aidevops:sig` footer. The timeline shows no `labeled` event at all. Example: a draft created at 01:58:49Z, renamed and marked ready at 02:07:05Z, then merged by the authoring runner at 02:36:52Z. The body is free-form agent prose that ends in `For #N` with no signature. This matches a worker calling `gh pr create`, or the REST pulls API, outside `gh_create_pr`.
- **Class B, wrapper body without a label (8 PRs, including two created at 06:55Z today):** marker and signature are present, but there is no `labeled` event. So `gh_create_pr` ran, but the origin postcondition either returned `_GH_PR_CREATE_PARTIAL_RC` and the worker continued, or the label write never happened. These PRs were still merged.
- **Independent provenance is available for both classes.** For each stranded PR, the target issue has a `DISPATCH_CLAIM ... runner=<PR author> ... session=issue-<N>` comment whose `ts=` is 14 to 29 seconds before the `feature/auto-<YYYYMMDD>-<HHMMSS>-gh<N>` branch timestamp. The PR author also has admin access. After an operator added `origin:worker` on that evidence, the canonical `_pm_restore_partial_continuation` (all other guards unchanged) returned the issues to the queue.

## How

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh` (`_pmpc_unlabeled_worker_provenance`)
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh` or `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` (pre-merge origin reconciliation for worker-branch PRs)
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh` (`_reconcile_pr_origin_label`, and the worker merge path's handling of `_GH_PR_CREATE_PARTIAL_RC`)
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`
- Unknown: the exact worker path that creates class A PRs. Inspect the headless worker transcripts for `gh pr create` or `gh api ... /pulls` calls that are not routed through the `gh` shim. Start with whether `PATH` in the worker sandbox keeps `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts` first.

Suggested approach (the worker may refine it):

1. **Recovery:** in `_pmpc_unlabeled_worker_provenance`, accept a second, independent proof as an alternative to the body marker. A trusted `DISPATCH_CLAIM` comment on the target issue must have `runner=` equal to the PR author and `session=issue-<N>`, where `<N>` equals the branch's `gh<N>`, and a `ts=` within 10 minutes of the branch timestamp. Keep the write-access check (`#aidevops:trust-boundary`) and the rule that conflicting `origin:*` labels are never overridden.
2. **Prevention at merge:** before a pulse or full-loop merge of a `feature/auto-*` PR, reconcile the missing origin label using the same claim-matched proof, and fail closed (do not merge) when it cannot be proven.
3. **Prevention at creation:** make the worker PR path treat `_GH_PR_CREATE_PARTIAL_RC` as blocking until the label is reconciled, and find and route the class A raw-creation path through `gh_create_pr`.

## Acceptance criteria

- A merged label-less, marker-less worker partial whose target issue has a matching `DISPATCH_CLAIM` from the PR author is restored by `_pm_restore_partial_continuation`. A test covers this.
- A claim from a different login, a different session or issue, a timestamp more than 10 minutes away, or an author without write access is refused. Tests cover each case.
- A `feature/auto-*` PR without a provable origin is not merged by the pulse merge pass. A test covers this.
- Existing GH#34312, GH#37043 and GH#37204 tests pass unchanged.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-commit-and-pr-partial-success.sh
```

After release, recently merged `feature/auto-*` PRs on the reporting repository should all carry `origin:worker` (or `origin:worker-takeover`).

title: bounded_operation: cancelling an ssh operation leaves the remote command running
body:
## What

`aidevops_bounded_operation` cancellation of an `ssh <host> "<remote command>"` operation ends only the local ssh client. The remote non-TTY shell keeps running, so a cancelled remote timer still fires later. The tool's description and `reference/` guidance should say so and give the safe pattern.

## Evidence (13 November 2026, a project's Hostinger rollout)

- Operation A: `["ssh","host","sleep 3600; rm -f <dir>/PAUSE; echo pause-removed"]` with a `restoration_command` that also removed `PAUSE`. Cancelled after 30 minutes: restoration ran and removed `PAUSE` as expected.
- The remote `bash -c "sleep 3600; rm -f …"` kept running (parent PID 1). It fired at the original deadline and removed a later, separately created `PAUSE` that another session's deploy depended on.
- A second cancelled operation of the same shape left another orphan (`ps -o pid,ppid,etimes,args -C sleep` showed PPID 1), which had to be killed by PID.
- Cleaning up with `ssh host 'pkill -f "sleep 2700; rm -f …"'` matched and killed its own remote `bash -c`, so that call printed nothing.

## How

- EDIT: the `aidevops_bounded_operation` tool description (OpenCode plugin) and the matching reference doc for bounded operations: note that cancelling ends the local process group only. A remote command started through ssh keeps running unless ssh allocates a TTY (`-tt`, so the remote side gets SIGHUP) or the restoration command kills it remotely.
- Suggested pattern: run timers locally (`["bash","-c","sleep N"]` and then a separate ssh call), or use `ssh -tt` for remote long-running commands that must die on cancel. For remote cleanup, kill by PID found with `ps`, never with `pkill -f` on a pattern your own command line contains.
- Files: exact paths not checked (plugin tool description and its reference doc); find them with `rg -n "bounded_operation" ~/Git/aidevops/.agents`.

## Verification

Start `["ssh","-tt","<host>","sleep 120"]`, cancel it, and confirm with `ssh <host> 'ps -o pid,ppid,args -C sleep'` that no orphan is left. Without `-tt`, the orphan remains (the reproduction above).

title: fix(scratch-worktree): clear inherited Git repository-location variables for every Git call in the scratch worktree helper
body:
## What

`.agents/scripts/scratch-worktree-helper.sh` runs every Git command as `git -C <path> ...` with the caller's environment. Git resolves an exported `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_COMMON_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE` or `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY` before `-C` applies. If a caller has any of these set (for example when the helper is reached from a Git hook), the helper's Git calls act on a different repository than the one named by `-C`.

Make every Git call in the helper ignore those inherited variables.

## Why it matters

`scratch_worktree_fetch` (added in PR #38038 for GH#38031) fetches a PR branch from a linked-worktree context so CI repair can start. With an inherited `GIT_DIR`, the fetch would update refs in the wrong repository and the borrowed-context probes would select a worktree from it. The CI-repair caller then fails closed on its exact-head check, so the result is a misleading `pr_head_fetch_failed` or `pr_head_moved` lease instead of a repair. The lock, unlock, remove and stale-reap calls in the same helper have the same exposure.

No current caller is known to export these variables: Pulse does not run inside a Git hook. This is hardening, raised by a review bot on PR #38038 and deferred there because the fix belongs to the whole helper, not one function.

## Reproducer

Not observed in production. It follows from Git's documented precedence and can be shown with two temporary repositories:

1. Create repository A with a remote that has a branch A does not hold, and an unrelated repository B.
2. `export GIT_DIR=<B>/.git`, source the helper, and call `scratch_worktree_fetch` for A with that branch.
3. Expected: A's remote-tracking ref is updated. Actual: Git operates on B, so A's ref is not created and the caller's exact-head check fails.

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/scratch-worktree-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-scratch-worktree-helper.sh`

Steps:

1. The helper is a sourced library, so do not `unset` the variables at file scope: that would change the caller's shell. Clear them per call with `env -u GIT_DIR -u GIT_WORK_TREE -u GIT_INDEX_FILE -u GIT_COMMON_DIR -u GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY git ...`. Define the variable list once.
2. A private shell function (for example `_scratch_wt_git()`) is fine for the plain calls. The fetch path also runs Git through `timeout_sec "$fetch_seconds" git -C ...`; check how `timeout_sec` runs its arguments before passing it a shell function, and use the `env -u ... git` form there if it executes an external command.
3. Apply it to every direct `git` invocation. Find them with `rg -n '\bgit ' .agents/scripts/scratch-worktree-helper.sh`. At the time of filing they are in `_scratch_wt_current_reason`, `_scratch_wt_unlock_and_remove`, `scratch_worktree_add`, `_scratch_wt_context_is_usable`, `_scratch_wt_borrowable_context`, `scratch_worktree_fetch` and `scratch_worktree_reap_stale`.
4. Keep the variable list identical to the reference pattern so the two helpers do not drift.

Reference pattern: `.agents/scripts/worktree-rescue-helper.sh` line 28 clears the same variables with `unset`. That file is an executable script, which is why it can unset at file scope.

## Acceptance criteria

- With `GIT_DIR` exported and pointing at an unrelated repository, `scratch_worktree_fetch` against the intended repository updates that repository's remote-tracking ref and leaves the unrelated repository's refs unchanged.
- With the same export, `scratch_worktree_add` and `scratch_worktree_remove` still create and remove the scratch worktree in the intended repository.
- The caller's `GIT_DIR` value is unchanged after each helper call.
- No direct `git` invocation in the helper inherits the listed variables.

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-scratch-worktree-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-ci-repair-routing.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/scratch-worktree-helper.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-scratch-worktree-helper.sh
```

Add one case to `test-scratch-worktree-helper.sh` for the first acceptance criterion. The file already creates a temporary repository under `$ROOT`; add a second repository as the unrelated `GIT_DIR` target, and a local bare remote if the fetch case needs one.

## Context

- Source: review comment on PR #38038 by @coderabbitai (thread on `.agents/scripts/scratch-worktree-helper.sh`).
- Related: GH#38031. The helper functions named above reach `main` when PR #38038 merges.

title: fix(pulse): reconcile pass starved by stale prefetch cache — fallback issue list lacks author trust metadata, so stage 0b blocks every lifecycle repair
body:
## What

When the legacy prefetch cache is stale, `reconcile_issues_single_pass` falls back to an issue list that carries no author trust metadata. Once a small per-process lookup budget is spent, stage 0b (`_action_reconcile_external_issue_gate`) fails closed on each remaining row, which skips stages 1 to 5. Both passes in the reporting host's current log window completed **zero actions**. Open `status:done` issues are not healed, issues whose PR already merged are not closed, and parent, close and objective repairs are skipped.

## Why

The pass is the only pulse path that heals `open + status:done` (GH#33374, `_action_rsd_single`). On one managed repository, 7 open issues currently carry `status:done`, all authored by a `MEMBER`; they were last updated between 2026-11-12T14:55Z and 2026-11-13T05:40Z. The dispatcher skips `status:done`, so reopened phase work, such as a completion phase that found an unpublished source class, never resumes.

## Reproducer

Evidence from 2026-11-13, one runner, runtime bundle `3.39.187-7e64721d5a`.

**Symptom command:**

```bash
rg -n 'reconcile_issues_single_pass: |cache author metadata missing' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log
jq -r 'to_entries | map(select(.value | type == "object") | .value.last_prefetch // "none") | sort | "oldest=\(.[0]) newest=\(.[-1]) n=\(length)"' \
  ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-prefetch-cache.json
```

**Actual output** (excerpt):

```text
External issue trust reconcile: <repo> cache author metadata missing; bounded live fallback budget exhausted (25/25); failing closed (further misses this cycle suppressed)   # 6 repos in one pass
reconcile_issues_single_pass: time-budget abort at 361s (budget=360s) — actions completed: persistent_repaired=0 external_gated=0 ciw_closed=0 rsd_closed=0 rsd_reset=0 oimp_closed=0 cpt_closed=0 ...
reconcile_issues_single_pass: time-budget abort at 367s (budget=360s) — actions completed: persistent_repaired=0 external_gated=0 ciw_closed=0 rsd_closed=0 rsd_reset=0 oimp_closed=0 cpt_closed=0 ...
oldest=2026-10-31T13:14:18Z newest=2026-11-13T06:52:03Z n=72
```

At 07:38Z, all 72 entries were outside the 600s window that `_read_cache_issues_for_slug` accepts, and 55 of 72 had a `last_prefetch` before 2026-11-13T00:00Z. The large product repository's entry was dated 2026-11-12T10:58:57Z, even though `pulse-batch-prefetch` logged a conditional-REST refresh of that repository at 07:31:44Z. The log window contains no `Reconcile done: healed` lines.

**Expected:** open `status:done` issues are healed (`Reconcile done: healed open + status:done ...`) within one pass.

### Mechanism

1. `_read_cache_issues_for_slug` (`pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`) only accepts a `pulse-prefetch-cache.json` entry younger than 600s. On this host the legacy prefetch (`preflight_prefetch_and_scope`) was deferred by budget priority 4 times in the current log window (`budget-priority: deferred deferrable stage 'preflight_prefetch_and_scope'`). The newer `pulse-batch-prefetch` conditional-REST refresh did not advance this file's `last_prefetch`.
2. On a miss, `_pir_reconcile_slug` falls back to `gh_issue_list --json number,title,labels,body`, which has no `authorAssociation` or `author` fields.
3. Every row therefore reaches `_action_reconcile_external_issue_gate` with an empty association. `_pir_recover_external_issue_author_metadata` allows 25 live lookups **per process across all repositories** (`PULSE_EXTERNAL_TRUST_FALLBACK_MAX`), and the first repository in the pass spends them. The first miss diagnostic already reported `budget exhausted (25/25)`. After that, every row returns 0 ("block remaining stages"), so `_pir_reconcile_issue_stages` skips stages 1 to 5 for that issue. The time-budget abort at 360s also means later repositories in the cursor order are not reached in a pass.

## How

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` (`_pir_reconcile_slug` fallback list, `_read_cache_issues_for_slug`)
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-actions.sh` (`_action_reconcile_external_issue_gate` / `_pir_recover_external_issue_author_metadata`)
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-external-issue-trust-reconcile.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-reconcile-budget-isolation.sh`

Prior art: #30792 added the bounded live fallback and one aggregated diagnostic per repository. It left the fallback list without metadata, and `gh issue list --json` offers no `authorAssociation` field. At this scale, 25 lookups per process do not cover even one repository.

Suggested approach (the worker may refine it):

1. **Carry trust metadata on the fallback path.** List open issues through REST (`repos/{slug}/issues?state=open&per_page=100`, skipping pull requests). REST returns `author_association` and `user{login,type}` in the same call. Map them to `authorAssociation` and `author` so stage 0b gets real metadata at no extra request cost. Alternatively, read the fresh `pulse-batch-prefetch` canonical snapshot when it carries trust metadata.
2. Keep fail-closed behaviour for genuinely unknown associations (`#aidevops:trust-boundary`). The fix is to supply the metadata, not to relax the gate.
3. Add a one-line summary per pass that counts rows blocked for missing metadata, so a no-op pass is visible in `pulse-health`.

## Acceptance criteria

- With a stale `pulse-prefetch-cache.json`, a reconcile pass reaches stage 2 for an open `status:done` issue authored by an `OWNER`/`MEMBER`. `_action_rsd_single` then closes or resets it according to its existing rules. A stubbed test covers this.
- An issue from an external, non-collaborator author is still gated exactly as today. A test covers this.
- The fallback adds no per-issue REST calls: one paginated list per repository.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-actions.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-external-issue-trust-reconcile.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-reconcile-budget-isolation.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-open-done-nonclosing-regression.sh
```

After release, the reporting host's pulse log should show non-zero `rsd_reset`, `ciw_closed` or `oimp_closed` counts when such issues exist, and no `cache author metadata missing ... failing closed` lines for repositories whose issues are maintainer-authored.

title: perf(pulse): cooperative bundle drain discards a completed full census — 130 ranked candidates, 19 free slots, 0 launches
body:
## What

A cooperative bundle drain (GH#37907) discards a completed **full** dispatch census. The drained cycle stops at the first candidate boundary, and the activated bundle's first cycle cannot reuse the census because the full-census snapshot is cycle-scoped. The runner then dispatches nothing for the length of one census plus the restart, even with free slots and a large ranked backlog.

## Why

On a 20-slot runner, a 915-second census produced 130 ranked candidates with 19 slots free. Zero workers launched, and active workers fell from 1 to 0. Runtime bundles activated 6 times between 03:37Z and 07:18Z (03:37, 04:47, 05:56, 06:07, 06:39, 07:18), roughly every 45 minutes. A full census on this host takes 450 to 915 seconds, so a large share of censuses overlap an activation.

## Reproducer

Evidence from 2026-11-13, one runner. Drained bundle `3.39.187-7e64721d5a37`; activated bundle `3.39.187-cfadea127845-1794554317` (activated 07:18:37Z). The 915-second census completed shortly before the 07:33:41Z drain line, so it started within about a minute of the activation.

**Symptom command:**

```bash
rg -n 'candidate enumeration timing|Dispatch_max: available=|cooperative drain requested|Dispatch path=max complete|drain_(started|completed)' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log
```

**Actual output** (excerpt):

```text
[pulse-wrapper] Dispatch_max: candidate enumeration timing census=full outcome=ok elapsed=915s sample=recorded estimate=300s->454s (GH#37623)
[pulse-wrapper] Dispatch_max: available=19, candidates=130
[pulse-wrapper] Dispatch_max stopping early: cooperative drain requested for activated bundle 3.39.187-cfadea127845-1794554317-75702.4LXePN during parallel loop (GH#37907)   # logged 4 times
[pulse-wrapper] PRIORITY_RESERVATION requested=12 product_launched=0 held=12 discovery_complete=false launched=0
[pulse-wrapper] Dispatch path=max complete: implementation_dispatched=0 triage_attempted=0 triage_infrastructure_failed=0 processed=0/130 simultaneous_worker_slots_targeted=19
[pulse-wrapper] Minimum worker floor refill stopped: cooperative drain requested for activated bundle 3.39.187-cfadea127845-1794554317-75702.4LXePN (GH#37907)
[2026-11-13T07:33:41Z] [pulse-event-refill] action=drain_started source=cycle-final pass=1
[pulse-wrapper] pulse-health.json written: workers=0/20 merged=0 closed_conflicting=0 dispatched=0 ...
```

**Expected:** the 130 ranked candidates still feed dispatch. The drained cycle should either hand them to the activated bundle's first cycle, or avoid spending the census at all.

### Mechanism

1. `_pulse_drain_requested_bundle` (`pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`) documents "In-flight candidates finish; no new census starts", but it is only consulted at candidate boundaries and in `_dispatch_compute_capacity`. A census that started before the marker appeared runs to completion.
2. `_dispatch_candidate_snapshot_path` (`pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh`) gives the full census a cycle-keyed path (`_dispatch_cycle_cache_path` uses `_PULSE_CYCLE_ID`), and `_dispatch_cleanup_cycle_cache` removes it. Only the first-wave **partial** census uses a durable path ("Partial censuses survive cooperative bundle drains/cycle rollover").
3. The activated bundle's first cycle therefore starts discovery from scratch.

## How

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh` (`_dispatch_candidate_snapshot_path`, `_dispatch_ranked_candidates_json`, `_dispatch_cleanup_cycle_cache`)
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh` (`_pulse_drain_requested_bundle` contract comment)
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-candidate-snapshot.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh` (extend the GH#37907 drain case near line 968)

Suggested approach (the worker may refine it):

1. **Hand a completed full census across a drain.** If a drain is requested, or always, write the completed full-census snapshot to a durable, bundle-independent path, mirroring the first-wave partial. Keep its existing `captured_at`/`census_seconds` TTL and `.consumed` filtering. Add a snapshot schema/version field so a bundle with a changed candidate format discards it. Every candidate is still revalidated by the existing dispatch-time gates (dedup guard, claim, labels, approvals), so reuse does not widen trust.
2. **Optional:** check `_pulse_drain_requested_bundle` at repository boundaries inside the census. If the census is less than half done when the marker appears, abort it so the activated bundle starts sooner. If it is further along, finish it and hand it over per step 1.
3. Keep GH#37907's guarantee that a drained cycle starts no new worker launches.

## Acceptance criteria

- A full census that completes after a drain request is consumed by the next cycle (`dispatch_candidate_snapshot_hit`), with consumed candidates filtered out. A test covers this.
- A snapshot older than its TTL, or with a mismatched schema version, is ignored. A test covers this.
- The drained cycle still launches no workers (existing GH#37907 test stays green).

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-candidate-snapshot.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh
```

After release, a drain during a census should be followed by a `dispatch_candidate_snapshot_hit` in the first cycle of the activated bundle, and that cycle should launch workers without a fresh `census=full` line.

title: Reclaim: replace observation-era worktree cleanup with one fail-closed reclaim path in worker_lifecycle
body:
## Goal

Replace the temporary observation-era worktree cleanup with **Reclaim**: one
fail-closed, budget-bounded reclaim path inside `worker_lifecycle`, built on the
lifecycle primitives that already exist rather than beside them.

## Why

On a busy host the observation-era pass (`worker-legacy-cleanup.py`) retired
nothing in 866 of 934 logged runs. Its documented rule "Automatic passes retain
sources with missing owner records" means every worktree older than admission
control is held forever, and it has no positive evidence that work has finished:
only age and owner records. The finished-worktree reclaim pass added in #37903 and
#38037 does retire trees, because it proves completion (issue CLOSED / PR MERGED,
one GraphQL batch per repository), but it lives in `.agents/scripts/` as a
parallel implementation and reintroduces a global `/proc` cwd census that the
legacy design explicitly rejects ("There is no global process-cwd scan or
descendant census"), and that census is Linux-only.

## What already exists and must be reused

| Need | Existing module |
|---|---|
| process identity, "unknown" vs "absent" | `worker_lifecycle/process.py`: `ProcessAdapter`, `ProcessIdentity`, `ObservationUnavailable` |
| platform adapters | `linux.py: LinuxProcesses`, `macos.py: MacOSProcesses` |
| refusal codes | `refusal.py`: `refusal_code`, `failure_category` |
| append-only, idempotent receipts | `journal.py`: `append_event` (dedup by `event_id`) |
| repeat-refusal quarantine | `cleanup_quarantine.py`: `CleanupQuarantine` |
| retirement proof | `retirement_proof.py`: `verify_retirement` |

Note: `cleanup_plan.enrolled_only_authorized` is NOT an automatic path; it requires
an event with `"operator_confirmed": True`. Reclaim needs its own evidence-backed
authorization event type in the same journal.

## Phases (children to be filed one at a time)

1. Move reference evidence (`worktree_reclaim_evidence.py`: batch GraphQL,
   `reference_finished`, `nothing_to_lose`) into `worker_lifecycle/reclaim/`,
   behaviour-preserving, under the existing 33 tests. Package is then covered by
   the existing ruff/mypy scope.
2. Replace the `/proc` census with an owner check through `ProcessAdapter`, plus
   an explicitly named residual-risk field for unregistered trees, so macOS works
   and the rejected global scan is gone.
3. Record each decision as a journal event keyed by (generation/path, evidence
   fingerprint); commit-time recheck compares the fingerprint (CAS).
4. Route repeat unreadable refusals to `CleanupQuarantine`; persist a cursor so a
   slow pass cannot silently starve the tail.
5. Delete `worker-legacy-cleanup.py`, the nine `legacy_*` modules and the
   observation-era pass in `pulse-cleanup-worktree-removal.sh` once the backlog
   is drained (the pulse comment already marks it "Temporary backlog pass").

## Non-goals

Consensus, replication or leader election: single host, single writer.
Idempotency and CAS are sufficient.

## Verification (per phase)

Existing `test-worktree-reclaim-finished.py` and worker-lifecycle CI contract pass;
`cleanup_worktrees.log` shows `Finished-worktree reclaim` receipts with refusal
histograms; free space on `/home` does not regress across a day of worker load.

title: perf(dispatch): footprint rebuild fetches open PR list once per claimed issue (dedup.footprint avg 93s)
body:
## What

`dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh` fetches the repository's open-PR list once **per stale `status:claimed` issue** while rebuilding the in-flight footprint cache. Fetch it at most once per cache rebuild and evaluate every claimed issue against that one list.

## Why

GH#36817 (PR #36835) correctly made every `status:claimed` issue prove implementation evidence before its Files Scope blocks dispatch. Evidence 2 in `_footprint_claimed_coordinator_has_evidence` runs:

```bash
gh pr list --repo "$repo_slug" --state open --json number,headRefName,body --limit 100
```

`_footprint_refresh_inflight_cache` calls that function inside its per-issue loop, so a repository with N claimed issues that lack ledger/stamp evidence pays N identical `gh pr list` calls. Parallel dispatch candidates run in separate processes, so the in-shell cache does not help them; every candidate that reaches the footprint stage pays the whole cost.

This is now one of the largest serialized dispatch-ceremony costs and keeps worker slots idle (GH#33616 targets ceremony latency).

## Evidence

One maintainer runner (macOS, v3.39.187), `~/.aidevops/logs/dispatch-stages.tsv`, 2026-11-13 05:00–08:30 UTC, completed stages:

| Stage | n | avg | max |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `dedup.ceremony_total` | 13 | 415s | 627s |
| `dedup.footprint` | 19 | 93s | 263s |
| `dedup.claim_consensus` | 16 | 62s | 115s |

GH#33616's baseline for `dedup.footprint` was 19–32s before GH#36817.

- One footprint rebuild logs `event=footprint_stale_coordinator` for 22 distinct issues in the same repository (each one passed through Evidence 2 and found no PR).
- `gh pr list --repo <repo> --state open --json number,headRefName,body --limit 100` takes about 11.8s on that runner (56 open PRs).
- 22 × ~5–12s matches the observed 93s average and 263s maximum.
- Two candidates were killed at their per-candidate stage timeout (`reason=launch_error`, rc=124) after spending 154s in `dedup.footprint`.

## Reproducer

1. In a repository with several open issues labelled `status:claimed` whose bodies declare a Files Scope, and with no dispatch-ledger entry, interactive-claim stamp or linked open PR for them.
2. Dispatch any candidate in that repository (or call `_footprint_get_inflight <repo>` from a fresh shell).
3. Observe one `event=footprint_stale_coordinator` log line per claimed issue, and one `gh pr list ... --limit 100` call per line (for example with a `gh` wrapper that logs argv, or `gh-api-calls.log`).

## How

Files to modify:

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh`
  - In `_footprint_refresh_inflight_cache`, reset a per-rebuild memo (for example `_FOOTPRINT_OPEN_PRS_REPO` / `_FOOTPRINT_OPEN_PRS_JSON`) before the loop.
  - In `_footprint_claimed_coordinator_has_evidence`, keep Evidence 1 (ledger) and Evidence 3 (stamp) before Evidence 2, unchanged. For Evidence 2, fetch the open-PR list lazily only when the memo is not set for this repo, then match against the memoized JSON.
  - Keep fail-safe behaviour: a failed fetch is treated as `[]` (as today). Do not memoize a failed fetch as an empty success across rebuilds; retrying once on the next rebuild is fine.
  - Do not change the evidence rules, the cache TTL or the log lines.
- Reference pattern: the existing `_FOOTPRINT_CACHE_*` variables in the same file.
- Test: extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh` (the existing stale-coordinator case around `event=footprint_stale_coordinator issue=#404`) so that a rebuild with several claimed issues without evidence calls the stubbed `gh pr list` exactly once, and that an issue with a matching open PR branch still keeps its reservation.

## Acceptance

- [ ] One footprint cache rebuild performs at most one open-PR list fetch per repository, regardless of how many claimed issues need Evidence 2.
- [ ] Claimed issues with a linked open PR (closing keyword or `gh<N>` branch) still reserve their footprint; those without evidence still log `footprint_stale_coordinator` and are skipped.
- [ ] `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh` passes; ShellCheck is clean for the modified file.
- [ ] After deploy, `dedup.footprint` average in `dispatch-stages.tsv` returns to roughly the pre-GH#36817 range (≤ ~30s) on a runner with many claimed issues.

## Context

- Regression source: GH#36817 / PR #36835 (2026-11-05).
- Ceremony-latency parent context: GH#33616.

title: Lifecycle retirement stalls forever after squash merge deletes the branch (published-head-not-on-remote)
body:
## Problem

Lifecycle retirement can stall permanently after a squash merge deletes the PR
branch. On one host, 8 `.lifecycle-retire-*` containers accumulated (two still
holding full trees, 4.9 GB and 505 MB); every one had `wip-preserved` and
`retirement-planned` journal events and no `retirement-removing` / `worktree-retired`.

Resuming one with `retire-worktree` fails in `_finish` → `_preserved` →
`verify_preservation` → `worktree-archive-helper.sh verify-local`:

```
archive-local:published-head-not-on-remote; source retained
```

## Root cause

`worker_lifecycle/retirement.py:_finish` re-verifies the WIP archive before
removal (`_preserved`, line ~263). `worktree_archive_local_verify.py:require_published_head`
(line ~106) requires the archive's head dependency to be reachable from a remote.
The archive was verified at preservation time, but `full-loop-helper.sh merge`
squash-merges with branch deletion, so the head commit stops being on any remote.
Any retirement planned before the merge and resumed after it fails the second
verification forever. The CLI collapses the error to
`{"reason": "CalledProcessError", "status": "unavailable"}`, so the cause is not
visible in logs.

Additionally, when the planned source is removed by another path, the empty
container is never removed: `_finish` only calls `container.rmdir()` on success,
and nothing sweeps orphaned containers (`container_cleanup_pending` is reported but
not acted on).

## Required change

1. Re-verification at `_finish` must not depend on remote state that the merge
   workflow deletes. Options: accept a head already recorded as published at
   preservation time (journal holds the preservation receipt), or accept a head
   whose PR is MERGED as content-preserved via the squash commit. Pick the one
   that keeps the fail-closed guarantee; document the choice.
2. Surface the failing helper and its error code in the CLI refusal instead of
   bare `CalledProcessError` (`refusal.py` already maps codes).
3. Sweep orphaned containers: a `.lifecycle-retire-*` whose plan's source path is
   gone and which is empty may be `rmdir`ed; one with `tree/` follows the resumed
   retirement path.

Scope narrowed by maintainer comments (items 1 and 3 are out of scope; only item 2 remains).

## Files

- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/retirement.py` (`_finish`, `_preserved`)
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/preservation.py` (`verify_preservation`)
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_local_verify.py` (`require_published_head`)
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/refusal.py`

### Files Scope

- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/refusal.py`
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/cli_errors.py`
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/cleanup_failure.py`

## Verification

- A retirement planned before a squash merge with branch deletion and resumed
  after it completes (`worktree-retired` event written, container removed).
- A tree with unpushed, unmerged commits still refuses.
- `fd -H -d 1 -t d '^\.lifecycle-retire-' "$AIDEVOPS_WORKTREE_BASE_DIR"` stays empty across a
  day of worker load, except containers of in-progress retirements.

title: Reclaim refuses worktrees whose only change is the full-loop cleanup-deferred marker
body:
## Problem

The finished-worktree reclaim pass refuses exactly the worktrees that ask to be
cleaned up. On one host, 7 of 8 finished-but-refused worktrees were "dirty" only
because of one untracked file: `.agents/.full-loop-cleanup-deferred`, the marker
`full-loop-helper-merge-cleanup.sh:573` writes to hand cleanup to a supervisor.
`nothing_to_lose` runs `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all`, sees `??`
for the marker and returns `uncommitted-changes`.

Every other consumer already treats the marker as framework state, not work:

- `.agents/scripts/worktree_recovery_cache_identity.py:23` — `FRAMEWORK_STATE_FILES`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh:83` — exclude pathspec
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-clean-lib.sh:36` — `_WT_CLEAN_DEFERRED_MARKER`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-risk.sh:12` — runtime paths

In `nothing_to_lose` (currently `.agents/scripts/worktree_reclaim_evidence.py`; if
#38054 has merged, `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/reclaim/evidence.py`),
exclude the marker from the dirty check with the same literal pathspec the worker
uses: `:(top,exclude,literal).agents/.full-loop-cleanup-deferred`.

Constraints:

- Exclude only that exact literal path, and only as untracked. A *tracked*
  modification of a file with that name must still refuse.
- Keep `--untracked-files=all` and `--ignore-submodules=none`.
- Prefer one shared constant over a fifth copy of the literal if a Python source
  for it already exists (`FRAMEWORK_STATE_FILES` above); otherwise define it once

## Verification

- A finished worktree whose only change is the untracked marker is authorized
  (`reason: work-finished`) in a dry run.
- A worktree with the marker plus any other untracked file still refuses

The previous worker's PR #38063 (`GH#38059: fix: reclaim ignores untracked cleanup-deferred marker`) developed merge conflicts with
`main` that could not be resolved by `gh pr update-branch` (server-side fast-forward).

```
.agents/scripts/worktree_reclaim_host.py
```

The prior PR's head commit is `6b17f0224422206fea523e35bfe4f9afb92bfb8c`. Choose the cheapest path that works:

   ```bash
   git fetch origin pull/38063/head:recovered-38063
   # Explicit base on origin/main — NOT canonical HEAD (t2802).
   git worktree add -b fresh-branch ../fresh-worktree origin/main
   cd ../fresh-worktree

   # run tests — if clean, proceed to PR
   ```

2. **If cherry-pick surfaces conflicts**, resolve them. The conflict surface IS the semantic overlap between the two branches — resolve those specific hunks rather than rewriting untouched logic.

title: fix(worktree): concurrent base-ref fetch race aborts worker launch after the claim is won (incorrect old value provided)
body:
## What

`worktree-helper-add.sh` refreshes the base branch with one `git fetch` and treats any failure as a stale base. When two processes fetch the same remote-tracking ref at the same moment, Git rejects one ref update with `incorrect old value provided`. The other fetch has just written the ref, so a repeated fetch would succeed, but the helper aborts worktree creation on the first failure. Retry the fetch a bounded number of times when Git reports this ref-update race.

## Why

Dispatch pre-creates the worker worktree **after** the candidate has passed every dedup gate and won its claim. On this runner that ceremony takes about 7 minutes (`dedup.ceremony_total` p50 419s). A lost fetch race throws that away: the claim comment is already posted, no worker starts, and the issue waits for the next cycle.

Parallel dispatch makes the race routine. Several candidates for the same repository reach `precreate.base_fetch` together, and the repository refresh, routines and running workers also fetch the same ref.

## Evidence

One maintainer runner (macOS, Git 2.53.0), `pulse.log` from 2026-11-05T06:58Z to 2026-11-13T02:59Z:

| Signal | Count |
|---|---:|
| `error: fetching ref refs/remotes/origin/<base> failed: incorrect old value provided` | 66 |
| Worktree pre-creation failed with `could not refresh origin/<base>; refusing stale worktree base` | 15 |
| `PRE_RUNTIME_FAILURE ... reason=worktree_precreation_failed` (all causes) | 59 |
| Workers spawned in the same period (`dedup.worker_spawn`) | 275 |

So about a quarter of worktree pre-creation failures (15 of 59), and roughly 5% of would-be launches, come from this one race. It recurred once more in the current log on 2026-11-13, after 08:12Z.

Log shape of one failure:

```text
[dispatch_with_dedup] Warning: worktree pre-creation failed for #<N> — dispatch will be skipped this cycle (helper_rc=1, extracted: '<empty>', helper_reason: 'Error: could not refresh origin/develop; refusing stale worktree base', wt_helper stdout head: 'error: fetching ref refs/remotes/origin/develop failed: incorrect old value provided
[dispatch_with_dedup] PRE_RUNTIME_FAILURE issue=<N> repo=<owner/repo> reason=worktree_precreation_failed
```

The same error line also appears next to 43 routine-script exits in a product repository's log lines. Adjacency is not proof of cause, and those call sites live outside this repository, so they are out of scope here.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:**

```bash
rg -c 'incorrect old value provided' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log
rg -n 'refusing stale worktree base' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log
```

**Actual output** (current log since 2026-11-13T02:59Z; issue number and repository replaced):

```text
1
[dispatch_with_dedup] Warning: worktree pre-creation failed for #<N> — dispatch will be skipped this cycle (helper_rc=1, extracted: '<empty>', helper_reason: 'Error: could not refresh origin/develop; refusing stale worktree base', wt_helper stdout head: 'error: fetching ref refs/remotes/origin/develop failed: incorrect old value provided
```

**Expected:** the helper repeats the fetch, resolves the base and creates the worktree.

The underlying race, reproduced in throwaway repositories (Git 2.53.0, macOS, local file remote):

1. Advance `main` on a bare remote.
2. From one clone, start 6 fetches at once: `git fetch --quiet --no-tags origin '+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main'`.
3. Repeat for 40 rounds.

Result over 240 fetches:

| Observation | Count |
|---|---:|
| Fetches that exited 1 with `error: fetching ref refs/remotes/origin/main failed: incorrect old value provided` | 200 |
| Fetches that succeeded (one per round) | 40 |
| Failed fetches with any other message | 0 |
| One repeat fetch after a failure: exit 0, local `origin/main` equal to the remote tip | 200 of 200 |

So every concurrent fetch but one loses, and one repeat is enough when the remote has not moved again. A local file remote makes the timing window wide; over the network the loss rate per collision is not measured.

In the helper, the same failure makes `_resolve_worktree_base_ref` print `could not refresh origin/<base>; refusing stale worktree base` and return 1.

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-fresh-base.sh`
- `.agents/reference/dispatch-timing.md`

Changes:

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh`
  - In `_worktree_fetch_origin_branch`, after the first fetch fails, classify the captured stderr. If it reports a ref-update race, run the same fetch again, at most 2 more times with a short pause between attempts, before falling through to the existing SSH-auth retry and error return.
  - Add a small classifier next to `_worktree_is_ssh_auth_failure` (for example `_worktree_is_ref_update_race`) that matches `incorrect old value provided`, the only message the reproduction produced. Do not match the broader `cannot lock ref`: it also covers conflicts that a repeat cannot fix.
  - Record each repeat as a `precreate.base_fetch_retry` sub-stage and add that row to `.agents/reference/dispatch-timing.md`. A recovered race no longer reaches `pulse.log`, so the stage log is the only place to count it.
  - A retry must be a real fetch. Do not accept the local ref without a successful fetch: the fresh-base rule (the worktree base is the server tip observed at creation time) stays as it is.
  - Leave the SSH-to-HTTPS retry, the error messages and the exit codes for every other failure unchanged.
- Reference pattern: `_worktree_is_ssh_auth_failure` and the existing retry branch in the same function.
- Test: extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-fresh-base.sh` with a stubbed `git` whose first `fetch` fails with the race message and whose second succeeds. Assert that `_worktree_fetch_origin_branch` returns 0, and that a failure with a different message still returns non-zero after one attempt.
- Test fixture: resolve `$ROOT` to its physical path (`pwd -P`). On macOS `mktemp -d` returns a path under the `/var` symlink, and the file's existing recreated-path section failed there before this change because its receipt was written with a path the helper never uses.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A fetch that fails once with `incorrect old value provided` and then succeeds makes `_worktree_fetch_origin_branch` return 0.
- [ ] A fetch that keeps failing with the race message returns non-zero after the bounded retries, and the caller still prints `refusing stale worktree base`.

title: fix(cleanup): bound the shared Turborepo cache in canonical checkouts (80 GiB, closes disk gate on shared runner host)
body:
## What

Bound the Turborepo local cache that linked worker worktrees share with the canonical checkout (`<canonical>/.turbo/cache`). Add an age/size-bounded prune to the existing asynchronous cleanup pass so it cannot fill the filesystem and close the disk-capacity admission gate.

## Why

On a shared Linux runner host, `/home` (984 GiB) sits at 95% used with about 48 GiB free. The disk-capacity gate (`disk-capacity-lib.sh`, 5% floor) therefore blocks dispatch for both maintainer runners on that host (`reason=below-minimum-percent`): 66 and 109 blocked attempts in their current pulse logs, with almost all slots idle.

The largest current growth source is one operator's canonical checkout of the product monorepo:

| Path (relative to that operator's home) | Size |
|---|---:|
| `Git/<product-repo>/.turbo` | 80 GiB |
| `Git/<product-repo>/.git` | 9 GiB |
| `Git/<product-repo>/node_modules` | 3.7 GiB |

- 35,991 cache files, all written since 2026-11-03: about 8 GiB/day, with 2,400–6,100 new files per day. 190 files (189 MB) were written in the last 2 hours while workers ran.
- Of 239 linked worktrees, only 1 has its own `.turbo` directory. Worker builds write into the canonical cache.
- Age profile: 62 GiB older than 1 day, 45 GiB older than 3 days, 21 GiB older than 7 days.
- Nothing in the framework prunes it. `worktree-artefact-reclaim.sh` and `worktree_recovery_cache_policy_common.py` handle `.turbo` inside idle linked worktrees only. `storage-cleanup-helper.sh` is interactive and moves to Trash, which frees nothing on the same filesystem (GH#37617).

Cache entries are content-addressed and regenerable. Deleting old ones only causes cache misses.

## Reproducer

1. Run several workers that execute `turbo` tasks in linked worktrees of a Turborepo repository on one host.
2. Watch `du -sk <canonical>/.turbo/cache` grow daily. No aidevops routine reduces it.
3. Once the filesystem falls below 5% free, every candidate fails at `local_capacity_gate`.

**Symptom command:** `grep -c 'disk space critical' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` and `find <canonical>/.turbo/cache -type f -printf '%TY-%Tm-%Td\n' | sort | uniq -c`

**Actual output:** 66 and 109 blocked attempts on the two runner accounts, for example `Dispatch blocked for #N in <repo>: disk space critical (reason=below-minimum-percent, available=50203044KB/4%, require at least 5242880KB and 5%)`. The cache shows 2,400–6,100 new files per day from 2026-11-03 to 2026-11-13, totalling 80 GiB.

**Expected:** The shared regenerable cache stays bounded, so free space does not fall to the admission floor.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worktree-artefact-reclaim.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/throughput-throttling-policy.md`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cleanup-worktrees-async.sh`

## How

Files to modify:

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh`: after the existing worktree cleanup, and under the same lock and bounded runner (see `_maintain_compact_archives` for the pattern), call a new bounded prune for each registered repository path (`_missing_metadata_repo_paths` shows how to iterate canonical plus repos.json paths).
- NEW or EDIT: a small helper (for example in `worktree-artefact-reclaim.sh` or a new `turbo-cache-prune-helper.sh`) that:
  - only touches `<repo>/.turbo/cache` when `<repo>/turbo.json` exists and `.turbo` is git-ignored (`git check-ignore`);
  - deletes regular files older than `AIDEVOPS_TURBO_CACHE_MAX_AGE_DAYS` (default 3), then, if the cache still exceeds `AIDEVOPS_TURBO_CACHE_MAX_SIZE` (default 20G), deletes oldest-first until under the cap;
  - deletes directly, never to Trash, since this is a regenerable cache (GH#37617);
  - never follows symlinks, stays within the cache directory and runs under a time budget;
  - logs `turbo-cache-prune repo=<slug> removed_files=N freed_kb=N` to the cleanup log.
- Before implementing, check whether the pinned Turborepo version (2.9.x) has built-in local-cache eviction. Prefer configuring it if it exists, and keep the prune as the fallback.
- Docs: add one line to `.agents/reference/throughput-throttling-policy.md` "Defaults" naming the turbo cache bound as part of the disk-capacity guard's reclaim path.
- Test: extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cleanup-worktrees-async.sh` with a fixture cache (old and new files, one symlink, a non-ignored `.turbo`) that asserts only old regular files in an ignored cache are removed and the size cap is honoured.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A cleanup pass on a host with a large shared turbo cache removes entries older than the configured age and enforces the size cap. A repo without `turbo.json`, or with a tracked `.turbo`, is untouched.
- [ ] Free space is reclaimed immediately (no same-filesystem Trash move).
- [ ] The prune is bounded in time and logged, and a failure never blocks the rest of cleanup.
- [ ] `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-cleanup-worktrees-async.sh` passes, and ShellCheck is clean.

## Context

- Disk gate: `.agents/scripts/disk-capacity-lib.sh` (`aidevops_worktree_capacity_check`).
- Related throttle report: GH#38026 (same gate on macOS APFS).
- Related: GH#35242 (worktree build artefacts), GH#37617 (same-filesystem Trash frees nothing).

title: fix(worktree-deps): provisioning reports os-error-ENOENT for stale pnpm _tmp_ dirs and dangling .bin links; skip walk when source exceeds budget
body:
## What

Worktree dependency provisioning reports `dependency-provision-rejected reason=os-error-ENOENT` for every worker launch in a large pnpm monorepo. Report specific reasons for these refusals, and skip the full walk when the source cannot fit the budget.

## Why

The ENOENT code is misleading. It sends diagnosis after a missing file when the real causes are ordinary `node_modules` layout plus a budget the source can never fit.

Traced on this host with the deployed validator. The pulse log shows 16 launches today, each `dependency-provision-rejected reason=os-error-ENOENT` followed by `Dependency provisioning unavailable; no external permission granted`.

Two independent causes, in walk order:

1. **Stale pnpm staging directories.** `node_modules/<name>_tmp_<pid>` directories are left behind by an interrupted install. Four were dated 2026-07-07, with no `package.json`. `Snapshot.check_package_root` treats each as a package root, and `regular_bytes(.../package.json)` raises `FileNotFoundError`.
2. **Dangling `.bin` links.** In a hoisted pnpm layout, nested `node_modules/.bin/*` links can point at packages that were hoisted elsewhere. There are 18 in this checkout, for example `@types/babel__template/node_modules/.bin/parser -> ../@babel/parser/bin/babel-parser.js`. `Snapshot.copy_link` → `resolved_inside` → `Path.resolve(strict=True)` raises `FileNotFoundError`.

Even without both causes, provisioning could not succeed here. The source `node_modules` is several GiB with far more than 20,000 entries, while the defaults are `--max-bytes 64 MiB` and `--max-entries 20000`. The walk would end in `byte-budget-exceeded` or `entry-budget-exceeded` after spending its time. Workers then install dependencies themselves, so throughput loss is small: `precreate.helper_deps` takes about 8 s per launch. The real cost is the wrong diagnostic and repeated wasted walks.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `python3 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/worktree-dependency-provision.py <canonical-repo> <linked-worktree> . --max-bytes 67108864`

**Actual output:** `dependency-provision-rejected reason=os-error-ENOENT`. A debug trace shows `FileNotFoundError` first at `node_modules/expo-router_tmp_40024/package.json`. After those stale directories moved to Trash, it shows the next one at `realpath` of `node_modules/@types/babel__template/node_modules/.bin/parser`.

**Expected:** A specific, path-free reason (`stale-package-staging`, `dangling-dependency-link` or `source-exceeds-budget`), and no full walk when the source obviously exceeds the budget.

## How

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/_worktree_dependency_snapshot.py`:
  - In `check_package_root`, skip or refuse with `Rejected("stale-package-staging")` for top-level entries matching pnpm's `^.+_tmp_\d+$` staging pattern. Skipping is preferred because these entries are not part of the inventory.
  - In `copy_link`, catch `FileNotFoundError` from `resolved_inside` and raise `Rejected("dangling-dependency-link")`. Decide whether dangling links under `node_modules/.bin` (non-resolution entries) can be copied as-is, since they are dangling in the source too. Keep the escape check for links that do resolve.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh` (`_provision_worktree_node_modules`, around line 476): before the first validator call, take a cheap bounded pre-check (for example top-level entry count, or `du -sk` with a timeout) and record `source-exceeds-budget` without walking when it clearly exceeds `WORKTREE_NODE_MODULES_RESTORE_MAX_BYTES`.
- Keep every safety property: no path or exception text in logs, `O_NOFOLLOW`, containment checks, and no permission widening.
- Test: extend the existing dependency provisioning test (find with `git ls-files '.agents/scripts/tests/*dependency*'`) with a fixture containing a `<pkg>_tmp_123` directory and a dangling `.bin` link, and assert the new reason codes.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/_worktree_dependency_snapshot.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh`

## Acceptance

- [ ] A fixture with a stale `<pkg>_tmp_<pid>` directory no longer yields `os-error-ENOENT`.
- [ ] A dangling dependency link yields a specific reason code, or is copied as-is under `.bin`. It never yields `os-error-ENOENT`.
- [ ] A source far over budget is refused as `source-exceeds-budget` without a full walk.
- [ ] The existing provisioning tests and ShellCheck pass.
