title: fix(tests): test-worktree-fresh-base.sh fails at a stale registration-failure section and uses the caller's lifecycle registry
body:
## What

`.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-fresh-base.sh` does not pass. Its "registration failure" section expects behaviour the worktree helper no longer has, so the file exits 1 there and the sections after it never run. Bring that section in line with the current helper, get the rest of the file passing, and stop the file from using the live lifecycle registry of the session that runs it.

## Why

No workflow under `.github/workflows` runs this file and no other script refers to it, so it only runs when a worker or a maintainer starts it by hand. Briefs that change `worktree-helper-add.sh` name it as their verification (GH#38060 does). A worker that follows such a brief gets a failure that its own change did not cause.

## Evidence

Observed on macOS with Git 2.53.0, on the GH#38060 branch (`main` at `05450cb617` plus that fix). Not run on Linux.

### 1. Registration-failure section (lines 278-310) is stale

After the temp-path fix described under Context, the file gets this far and stops:

```text
PASS recreated path supersedes terminal receipt with explicit lifecycle disposition
FAIL registration failure did not preserve unverifiable path recreation: rc=1 output=Creating worktree for existing branch 'test/recreated-registration-failure'...
Worktree ownership transaction unavailable
WORKTREE_OWNERSHIP_ERROR_STAGE=lifecycle:begin-create
WORKTREE_OWNERSHIP_ERROR_TYPE=OperationalError
```

The section breaks the ownership registry by creating a directory at `<HOME>/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/worktree-registry.db`. It then expects the helper to create the worktree, fail at registration, keep the tree and print `AIDEVOPS_WORKTREE_LIFECYCLE_DISPOSITION=REGISTRATION_FAILED`.

`worktree_create_registered` in `shared-worktree-create.sh` now runs `shared-worktree-registry-owner.py begin-create` against the registry before `git worktree add`, and returns 1 when that fails. With a registry that is broken from the start, no tree is created and the `REGISTRATION_FAILED` branch in `worktree-helper-add.sh` is not reached.

The test file was last changed on 2026-10-09 (`c3fd429742`). The `Worktree ownership transaction unavailable` message entered the scripts in commits dated 2026-10-13 and 2026-10-22 (`1db16570f5`, `845999a7bf`), and the `precreate.registry_begin_create` stage on 2026-10-24 (`bdc76d5d7e`). Which commit first put `begin-create` ahead of creation was not traced.

The failure was the same in 2 of 2 runs: one with the session environment, one with `AIDEVOPS_WORKSPACE_DIR`, `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_RUNTIME_PID` and `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_SESSION_ID` unset. Nothing in this cause depends on the platform, so Linux is expected to fail the same way.

### 2. Sections after line 310 have not run

The active-receipt section and everything after it are unreached. Whether they pass is unknown.

### 3. The file uses the live lifecycle registry when run from a session

The test overrides `HOME` only. The interactive session that ran it also exports `AIDEVOPS_WORKSPACE_DIR` (the real workspace), `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_RUNTIME_PID` and `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_SESSION_ID`; worker sessions were not checked. `worker_lifecycle_state_dir` (`worker-lifecycle-state.sh`) uses `AIDEVOPS_WORKSPACE_DIR` before `HOME`, and `_worktree_create_native` (`shared-worktree-create.sh`) calls `worker-registry.py create-worktree` when the runtime PID and session ID are set. So, from such a session, each worktree the fixture creates goes through the live registry. This follows from reading those two functions. Whether rows for the fixture paths remain in the live registry afterwards was not checked.

Two failures appeared, lasted about 8 minutes and then stopped, with no change to the code. One replica run before them had exited 0.

| Observation | During those 8 minutes | Afterwards |
|---|---|---|
| Whole file stops at its first step with `Could not create an owned scratch worktree for the fresh-base fetch.` | 3 of 3 runs | 0 of 4 runs |
| A replica of the recreated-path section (one receipt, one `worktree-helper.sh add`) exits 1 | 6 of 7 runs | 0 of 6 runs |

The 5 replica failures whose output was captured printed `Native worktree creation refused; partial results retained: {"cleanup_authorized": false, "mode": "observe-only", "reason": "FileNotFoundError", "status": "unavailable"}`.

A `worker-legacy-cleanup.py` process was running against the live state directory part-way through the first period (5 minutes elapsed when seen) and had exited when checked after it. That makes the live registry a lead, not a finding: one of the three whole-file failures had all three variables unset. The cause of these failures is not established.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:**

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-fresh-base.sh
```

**Actual output** (last lines, after the temp-path fix from GH#38060 is merged): the `FAIL registration failure did not preserve unverifiable path recreation` block shown above, exit 1.

**Expected:** every section prints `PASS` and the file exits 0.

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-fresh-base.sh`

Changes:

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-fresh-base.sh`
  - Registration-failure section: decide which contract it should cover, then make it test that.
    - A registry that is unusable before creation: assert the non-zero exit, that no tree exists at the path, that the output carries `WORKTREE_OWNERSHIP_ERROR_STAGE=lifecycle:begin-create`, and that the terminal receipt is unchanged and still selectable (the two `jq`/`full_loop_cleanup_receipt_for_worktree` checks already there).
    - A registration that fails after `begin-create` succeeded (the `REGISTRATION_FAILED` branch): keep it covered only if the failure can be injected without a new test-only interface in the helper. If it cannot, say so in the PR and leave that branch uncovered.
  - Isolate the lifecycle state: give the fixture its own state directory (`AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_STATE_DIR` under `$ROOT`) or unset the three inherited variables before the first `worktree-helper.sh` call. Other tests under `.agents/scripts/tests/` already set these variables; `rg -l 'AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_STATE_DIR' .agents/scripts/tests` lists them. Follow one of those.
  - Fix whatever the sections after line 310 turn out to need, if the cause is in the test. A failure caused by the helper is a separate issue: file it with the output and leave the helper alone here.
- Do not change `shared-worktree-create.sh`, `worktree-helper-add.sh` or the registry scripts in this issue.
- Do not add the file to a workflow in this issue. A new CI gate is a maintainer decision (`reference/ci-gate-policy.md`).

## Acceptance

- [ ] `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-fresh-base.sh` exits 0 on macOS, run from a session that exports the three lifecycle variables.
- [ ] The same command exits 0 with those three variables unset.
- [ ] The run does not use the caller's lifecycle registry: with `AIDEVOPS_WORKSPACE_DIR` pointing at an empty directory outside `$ROOT`, no `worker-lifecycle` directory exists there after the run.
- [ ] The PR states which of the two registration-failure contracts the section now covers.
- [ ] ShellCheck is clean for the file.

## Context

- Found while verifying GH#38060.
- The file also failed earlier, at the recreated-path section, on macOS only: `mktemp -d` returns a path under `/var/folders`, which is a symlink to `/private/var/folders`. The helper resolves worktree paths to the physical form, and cleanup receipts are matched by path string, so the receipt written with the logical path was never superseded. The GH#38060 PR resolves `$ROOT` with `pwd -P`. With that line the section passed in 2 of 2 runs.

title: fix(pulse-merge): public-repo auto-approvals are logged as failed although GitHub records them
body:
## What

Every pulse auto-approval on a public repository is logged as a failure, although GitHub records the approval. Two defects combine:

1. `privacy_scan_secret_material_text` (`.agents/scripts/privacy-guard-helper.sh`, lines 919-926) prints `[privacy-scan][ALLOW] aidevops script file reference` to stderr for text that contains no script reference. It compares the input with `$(_privacy_redact_aidevops_script_references ...)`; command substitution strips trailing newlines, and the `gh` shim always appends a newline to the body it scans (`.agents/scripts/gh`, `_shim_privacy_scan`). So any public write with a body prints the advisory.
2. `_pulse_approve_pr_at_head` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-gates.sh`, lines 861-866) captures `gh api -X POST .../reviews ... 2>&1` and parses the combined text with `jq`. The advisory line comes first, `jq` fails, and the function returns 1 after the review has been created.

`approve_collaborator_pr` then logs `failed to approve PR #N in <repo> — ` with an empty reason. `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh` classifies that line as `pw-approve-fail`.

## Why

The approval itself works, and the caller in `pulse-merge.sh` (`approve_collaborator_pr ... || true`) ignores the return, so merges still happen. The cost is false failure evidence. Pulse logs and PR diagnostics say approval failed when it succeeded, which sends triage (human or worker) after a problem that does not exist. Any other caller that merges `2>&1` from a public `gh` write and parses JSON can break the same way.

## Evidence

One maintainer runner (macOS), `pulse.log` on 2026-11-13:

| Repository | Visibility | `approved PR #` | `failed to approve PR #` |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| marcusquinn/aidevops | public | 0 | 4 |
| a private product repository | private (privacy scan skipped) | 11 | 0 |

For all four "failed" PRs (#38019, #38037, #38057, #38050), `gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/pulls/<N>/reviews` shows the pulse runner's `APPROVED` review on the exact head with the auto-approval body, submitted at the time of the failure line.

## Reproducer

Without any GitHub write (a stub stands in for the native `gh`, answers the review POST with `{"state":"APPROVED","commit_id":"<head>"}` and passes other calls through):

- The shim exits 0, the stub receives the POST, stdout is the review JSON, and stderr is `[privacy-scan][ALLOW] aidevops script file reference`.
- With stdout and stderr merged as `_pulse_approve_pr_at_head` does, `jq -r '.state'` exits 5 and the state is empty.

Minimal check of defect 1, sourcing `privacy-guard-helper.sh`:

| Input to `privacy_scan_secret_material_text` | stderr |
|---|---|
| `hello` | empty |
| `hello` + newline | `[privacy-scan][ALLOW] aidevops script file reference` |

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/privacy-guard-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-gates.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-approve-collaborator-guard.sh` (existing; run it, extend only if a case is needed)

Changes:

- EDIT `.agents/scripts/privacy-guard-helper.sh`, `privacy_scan_secret_material_text`: preserve trailing newlines when capturing the redacted text (for example, append a sentinel inside the command substitution and strip it afterwards), so the advisory prints only when a script reference was actually redacted. Apply the same to the per-line comparison near line 1091 if it can see trailing newlines. Do not change what is redacted or what is blocked.
- EDIT `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-gates.sh`, `_pulse_approve_pr_at_head`: capture only stdout for the JSON parse and let stderr pass through to the caller, which already captures `2>&1` for its log line. On a real failure the log then carries the `gh` error text instead of an empty reason. Keep the exact-head check (`state == APPROVED` and `commit_id == expected head`) unchanged. This function carries `#aidevops:trust-boundary`; the change must not weaken it.
- Reference pattern: other `gh api` JSON reads in `pulse-merge-gates.sh` capture stdout only (for example `_trusted_existing_approver`).

## Acceptance

- [ ] `privacy_scan_secret_material_text` prints no advisory for text that ends with a newline and has no script reference, and still prints it for text with a real reference.
- [ ] With the shim and a stub native `gh` that returns the approved review JSON, `_pulse_approve_pr_at_head` returns 0 for a public target.
- [ ] A mismatched or failed approval still returns 1 (existing Case S in `test-pulse-merge-approve-collaborator-guard.sh` passes), and the failure log line now includes `gh`'s error text when there is one.
- [ ] `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-approve-collaborator-guard.sh` and the existing privacy tests (`test-gh-public-privacy-guard.sh`, `test-gh-write-privacy-reporting.sh`) pass; ShellCheck is clean for the modified files.
- [ ] After deploy, `pulse.log` records `approved PR #N in marcusquinn/aidevops` for pulse approvals, and no `failed to approve` line appears for a PR whose reviews show the pulse runner's approval on that head.

title: feat(opencode-restart): restart heartbeat-less tmux TUI holders (pre-heartbeat sessions block DB archive indefinitely)
body:
## What

Let `opencode-session-restart-helper.sh` restart interactive TUI holders that have no activity heartbeat and no session-bus presence. These are TUIs started before the heartbeat plugin shipped. They are exactly the long-lived holders that keep `opencode-db-archive` deferred indefinitely.

## Why

On a shared Linux runner host, the async archive had not completed since 2026-10-23 on two runner accounts. Each run logged `Archive deferred — N process(es) hold the active DB open (holder PID <pid> has no activity heartbeat)`, followed by `last-run NOT updated`.

The restart helper (GH#37663) could not help:

- `inventory` (default, DB holders) listed 1 of 9 holders on one account and 7 of 11 on the other. Every heartbeat-less holder was missing: 12 TUIs aged 5–28 days, all in tmux panes.
- `inventory --all` listed even fewer: `_inventory_rows` returns before the heartbeat fallback when `holders='*'`, so `--all` drops heartbeat rows entirely.
- The archive `blocked-notice` names only one holder at a time. An owner who restarts it simply finds the next one.

I restarted these by hand, and the method worked. It is reusable:

1. **Busy detection without a heartbeat.** `tmux capture-pane -p -t <pane>` contains `esc interrupt` while the agent is working. A positive control (a heartbeat-busy TUI) showed the marker, and every idle TUI showed none. Combine this with `#{window_activity}` older than a quiet period (I used 1 h). One TUI with window activity under 5 minutes was left alone.
2. **Session ID without a heartbeat.** After SIGTERM, OpenCode prints `Continue  opencode -s <id>` in the pane. That ID is the session the TUI was actually showing. In one case it differed from the launch `-s` argument, because the user had switched sessions inside the TUI. Parse the last such line from `capture-pane -S -80`.
3. **Resume.** Send `cd -- <cwd> && opencode -s <id>` to the pane with send-keys, as `_resume_one` already does. If no Continue line appears (the TUI was on its home screen), relaunch plain `opencode` in the original cwd.

Result: 10 of 12 TUIs were restarted and resumed in their own panes, and their new PIDs write heartbeats. One was relaunched on its home screen, and one was skipped as recently active. The archive's deferral reason changed from `has no activity heartbeat` to `holder ... was active 62s ago (need 900s)`, which is a normal, self-clearing wait.

## How

Files to modify:

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/opencode-session-restart-helper.sh`
  - `_inventory_rows`: for DB holders with no presence row and no single-session heartbeat, emit a `source=tmux` row when `_pane_locate` finds a tmux pane. Its status comes from the pane busy marker plus `window_activity` quiet time, and its session ID is `unknown`.
  - `_inventory_rows` with `--all`: also include these rows and heartbeat rows, rather than returning early.
  - `_stop_one` / resume: for `sid=unknown`, record the manifest with the pane and cwd; after the exit, read the `Continue  opencode -s <id>` line from the pane; resume with that ID or fall back to plain `opencode`.
  - Keep existing authority (`--yes` or terminal), never signal a busy pane, and never print pane text. Only parse the marker and session-ID tokens.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-async-helper.sh`: the blocked notice should list every heartbeat-less holder (PID, age, pane if known), not just the first.
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/session.md` ("Interactive TUI Restart for Maintenance"): document the tmux fallback and its evidence limits.
- Test: extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-session-restart.sh` with a fake tmux (`OPENCODE_RESTART_TMUX_BIN`) whose capture-pane returns a busy footer, an idle screen, and a post-exit `Continue  opencode -s ses_x` line.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/opencode-session-restart-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-async-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/session.md`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-session-restart.sh`

## Acceptance

- [ ] `inventory` lists heartbeat-less tmux TUI holders, and `--all` is a superset of the default.
- [ ] `stop --yes` stops only heartbeat-less panes that are idle and quiet past the threshold, and skips any pane showing the busy marker.
- [ ] `resume` relaunches the exact session from the exit `Continue` line, or plain `opencode` when there is none, in the original pane and cwd.
- [ ] The archive blocked notice lists every heartbeat-less holder.
- [ ] `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-session-restart.sh` passes, and ShellCheck is clean.

title: fix(worker-lifecycle): enroll and admit-session fail on registry writer contention instead of waiting
body:
## What

`worker-registry.py enroll` and `admit-session` try once and fail on registry writer contention (`database-locked`). Every Pulse worktree pre-creation goes through them (`shared-worktree-create.sh` → `_worktree_enroll_generation`). When the registry writer is busy for more than the 2 s SQLite busy timeout, the worktree is created but not enrolled, the dispatch is skipped for that cycle, and the new tree is left on disk unenrolled.

Admitted launches already wait out this contention (`launch.py` `run_admitted` → `within_contention_deadline`, 30 s, GH#36921), and the OpenCode session helper retries it briefly (GH#37346). The enrollment CLI path does neither.

## Why

- Dispatch loses a cycle for an issue that was ready to run.
- The skipped attempt leaves a created but unenrolled tree, which legacy cleanup later has to archive and retire. That retirement holds the registry writer, which causes more contention.
- The writer is held for long stretches on purpose: legacy cleanup keeps it across the destructive `git worktree move`/`remove --force` and revalidation steps (`legacy_cleanup.py` `finish`), so waiting is the intended consumer behaviour.

## Evidence

One maintainer runner (macOS), 2026-11-13:

- `pulse.log`: 3 pre-creation failures, all `Generation enrollment refused: {"category": "contention", "detail": "database-locked", ...}`, each followed by `dispatch will be skipped this cycle`. One of the three trees was still on disk hours later.
- `~/.aidevops/logs/lifecycle-admission/2026-11-13.jsonl`: 7 `database-locked` refusals out of 1,642 OpenCode tool admissions (plugin path, which has its own short retry).
- A writer probe (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE` with a 0.5 s timeout, rolled back at once, every 2 s for 7.5 minutes) found the writer held in 8 stretches of up to about 10 s (47 s in total), all while `worker-legacy-cleanup.py` was running. The writer was free for the rest of the probe.
- `storage.py` connects with `timeout=2`. In the `worker_lifecycle` package, `within_contention_deadline` is used only by `launch.py`.

## Reproducer

Fully isolated: a temporary registry (`--state-dir` under the agent workspace), a temporary Git repository with one linked worktree, and a second SQLite connection holding `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` on that registry for 5 s while `worker-registry.py --state-dir <tmp> enroll --path <tree>` runs. Deployed runtime v3.39.187:

```text
hold_s=5 enroll_exit=2 elapsed_s=3
stdout={"category": "contention", "cleanup_authorized": false, "detail": "database-locked", "mode": "observe-only", "reason": "OperationalError", "status": "unavailable"}
stderr_retry_lines=0
```

This is the same payload Pulse logged. No retry is attempted.

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/registry.py`
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/creation.py`
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/REGISTRY.md`

Changes:

- EDIT `registry.py` `execute_operation`: run `enroll` and `admit-session` inside `within_contention_deadline(..., ContentionWait(contention_deadline(), <retry logger>))`, after the existing `upgrade_registry` call. Both operations are documented as safe to repeat: `GenerationEnrollment._resolve` ("A crash after marker publication is recovered by repeating create=True") and `admit_session` ("Retry the same owner's admission"). Their journal events use deterministic IDs, and `append_event` deduplicates them. Log retries on stderr with fixed reason codes only, matching `launch.py` `_contention_retry`.
- EDIT `creation.py` `create_worktree`: apply the same wait to the `admit_session` call and the `created-worktree` event write that follow `git worktree add`. Do not retry `git worktree add` itself.
- EDIT `REGISTRY.md` (the paragraph documenting the 30 s admission wait): say that enrollment and session admission use the same bound and variable (`AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_ADMISSION_WAIT_SECONDS`).
- Reference pattern: `launch.py` `run_admitted` (lines ~134-139) and `admission.py` `within_contention_deadline`.
- Out of scope: the OpenCode plugin helper's retry window (bounded by its synchronous 10 s helper timeout) and how long legacy cleanup holds the writer (a deliberate safety design). Each needs its own issue if the residual refusals matter.

## Acceptance

- [ ] With another connection holding `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` on the registry for about 5 s, `worker-registry.py enroll --path <fresh linked worktree>` succeeds after logging at least one retry; before the change it fails with `database-locked`.
- [ ] Contention lasting longer than `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_ADMISSION_WAIT_SECONDS` still fails with `database-locked`, and `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_ADMISSION_WAIT_SECONDS=0` restores a single attempt.
- [ ] Non-contention refusals (for example `generation-not-open`, `session-owner-already-ended`) still fail immediately.
- [ ] `python3 -m unittest discover -s .agents/worker-lifecycle/tests` passes.
- [ ] After deploy, `pulse.log` has no `Generation enrollment refused` with `detail: database-locked` across a legacy-cleanup run.

title: perf(dispatch): single-pass jq extraction in footprint in-flight rebuild (O(n²) JSON parsing)
body:
## What

`_footprint_refresh_inflight_cache` should extract each in-flight issue's number, `parent-task` flag, `status:claimed` flag and body in one `jq` pass, instead of re-parsing the whole in-flight JSON array 4 times per issue.

## Why

`dedup.footprint` is still the slowest pre-launch dispatch stage after GH#38055 (PR #38058), which removed the per-claimed-issue `gh pr list`. Measured on the dispatching Mac on 2026-11-13, in `~/.aidevops/logs/dispatch-stages.tsv`: 50–76 s per candidate (#23489 50.8 s, #23498 53.1 s, #23500 76.0 s, #23499 71.0 s, #23230 57.6 s, #23053 66.7 s).

Profile of one rebuild for a repo with 82 in-flight issues (1.2 MB JSON, mostly enrichment briefs), on an idle shell:

| Phase | ms |
|---|---|
| `_footprint_fetch_active_issues` (4 parallel `gh issue list`) | 1361 |
| per-issue extraction loop (4 × `jq` over the full array per issue) | 5698 |
| claimed-issue evidence checks (26 issues, memoized PR list) | 1471 |
| full `_footprint_refresh_inflight_cache` | 9927 |

The loop is O(n²) in bytes: 82 issues × 4 parses × 1.2 MB ≈ 394 MB of JSON parsed per rebuild. The cost multiplies because:

- The cache TTL is 30 s, which is shorter than a rebuild under load, so a candidate almost never hits a warm cache.
- Each dispatch candidate runs in its own stage subshell, so concurrent candidates each rebuild (38 `footprint_stale_coordinator` events in one 25 s window = 2 rebuilds × 19 claimed issues).
- The host was at load average 113 on 16 cores during the measurement, which amplifies CPU-bound loops about 10×.

A prototype single-pass extraction produced **byte-identical `path|issue` output** in 2324 ms vs 6228 ms for the current loop (81 issues).

## How

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh` — in `_footprint_refresh_inflight_cache` (the `while [[ "$i" -lt "$issue_count" ]]` loop, around line 992), replace the per-index `jq` calls with one `jq -r '.[] | [(.number|tostring), (parent-task flag), (status:claimed flag), ((.body // "")|@base64)] | @tsv'` stream read by `while IFS=$'\t' read -r ...`. Decode the body with `base64` before `_footprint_extract_paths`. Keep the GH#36817 claimed-evidence check, the GH#38055 PR memo, the parent-task skip and the cache variables unchanged. Bash 3.2 compatible; process substitution is already used in this module.
- Out of scope: changing `_FOOTPRINT_CACHE_TTL` or sharing the cache across candidate subshells. Both change staleness semantics relative to the GH#32977 reservation design; revisit with stage telemetry after this lands.
- Reference pattern: the GH#38055 memo in the same function; `_footprint_reservation_entries` "one jq per record" (GH#33998).

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh`

## Acceptance

- [ ] One `jq` invocation per rebuild for per-issue field extraction; output `path|issue` lines are unchanged for the same input.
- [ ] `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh` passes.
- [ ] `shellcheck .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh` is clean.
- [ ] Post-deploy: `dedup.footprint` `complete` durations in `dispatch-stages.tsv` drop relative to the 50–76 s baseline above.

title: fix(pulse): closed-issue dispatch skip is classified unclassified_signal (missing structured issue_closed reason)
body:
## What

When `dispatch_with_dedup` skips a candidate because the issue is already CLOSED, it should emit a structured `DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=issue_closed` line that includes the repo slug. The pre-launch classifier would then record the benign `issue_closed` reason instead of `unclassified_signal`.

## Why

`_dispatch_load_and_validate_metadata` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh`, around line 918) logs only:

```
[dispatch] Skipping #23239: state=CLOSED
```

`_dispatch_candidate_recent_lines` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh`, around line 515) keeps only lines that contain both `#<issue>` and the exact repo slug. This line has no repo slug, so the classifier never sees it and falls through to `unclassified_signal`. The result, in `pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh` (around lines 1915–1938):

- The candidate is logged as `pre-launch failure ... reason=unclassified_signal` and counted in `dispatch_candidate_failed_reason_unclassified_signal`. The benign path (`issue_closed` is already listed in `_dispatch_candidate_benign_block_reason`) and `_dispatch_mark_benign_blocked_candidate` are never reached.
- Genuine unclassified failures are buried. Measured from runner `pulse.log` files on 2026-11-13:

| Runner | `state=CLOSED` skips | `unclassified_signal` total |
|---|---|---|
| Linux runner A | 137 (137 distinct issues) | 163 |
| Linux runner B | 94 (94 distinct issues) | 122 |
| macOS runner | 27 | 28 |

So about 85% of `unclassified_signal` entries are closed-issue skips.

## Reproducer

Observed sequence in a runner `pulse.log` for one candidate, 2026-11-13T13:38:55Z (excerpt, consecutive lines):

```
[pulse-wrapper] DISPATCH_CANDIDATE_ATTEMPT #NNNNN (owner/private-repo)
[pulse-wrapper] Stage start: dispatch_candidate_NNNNN (timeout 600s)
[dispatch] Skipping #NNNNN: state=CLOSED
[pulse-wrapper] Stage failed: dispatch_candidate_NNNNN exited with 1 (6s)
[pulse-wrapper] Dispatch_max: dispatch_with_dedup returned rc=1 for #NNNNN elapsed_ms=6127 timeout_used_ms=600000
[pulse-wrapper] Dispatch_max: #NNNNN (owner/private-repo) pre-launch failure stage=dispatch_with_dedup rc=1 reason=unclassified_signal
```

The result is `unclassified_signal`, because `_dispatch_candidate_recent_lines` drops the slug-less line.

Count on any runner: `grep -c 'Skipping #[0-9]*: state=CLOSED' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` vs `grep -c 'reason=unclassified_signal' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`.

## How

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh`: in `_dispatch_load_and_validate_metadata`, the `issue_state == CLOSED` branch keeps the existing log line and eviction, and adds `echo "[dispatch_with_dedup] DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=issue_closed signal=state-closed issue=#${issue_number} repo=${repo_slug}" >>"$LOGFILE"`. Use the same format as the neighbouring `needs_maintainer_permissions` and `permission_grant_unverified` markers in the same function. Keep `return 1`.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons.sh`, or the nearest existing classifier test: assert that a candidate whose recent lines contain the new marker classifies as `issue_closed`, and that `_dispatch_candidate_benign_block_reason issue_closed` returns 0. That predicate is already covered by `test-pulse-current-state-guardrails.sh` around line 512.

### Files Scope

title: perf(opencode-db-archive): fixed per-run overhead (held-size expiry pass + full archive integrity_check) caps scheduled archive at ~10 sessions/hour
body:
## What

Make the scheduled OpenCode DB archive keep up with session accrual on busy runners. Today each hourly run (`OPENCODE_DB_ARCHIVE_ASYNC_BUDGET_SEC=60`) spends almost all of its budget on two fixed per-run costs and archives about one batch (10 sessions) per hour. That is less than a 20-worker runner creates, so the active DB grows without bound even when the holder gate passes.

## Why

Measured on a shared Linux runner on 2026-11-13. Two runner accounts had active DBs of 68 GB and 50 GB, with 4808 and 1529 eligible sessions. The archive had not completed since 2026-10-23.

| Run budget | Expiry pass | Session batches committed | Where the rest went |
|---|---|---|---|
| 60 s (timer) | ran | 1 (eligible 1529 → 1519) | `PRAGMA integrity_check` on the archive DB, killed by the deadline |
| 300 s (manual) | 5719 events | 42 (420 sessions) | integrity check after batch 1, then about 1.4 sessions/s |
| 120 s (manual) | 281262 events, about 90 s | 1 | integrity check started at t≈100 s, killed |

Process sampling during the 120 s run showed a stream of short-lived `sqlite3 ... opencode-archive.db DELETE FROM event WHERE rowid IN (... LIMIT 10)` calls for about 90 s, then `sqlite3 .../opencode-archive.db PRAGMA integrity_check;` until the deadline.

Root causes in `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh`:

1. **The expiry pass uses the held-DB batch size on the archive DB.** `_archive_expire_events` (around line 1122) deletes `LIMIT $ARCHIVE_BATCH_SIZE` per `sqlite3` process. The idle gate (around lines 290–291) lowers `ARCHIVE_BATCH_SIZE` globally to `DEFAULT_HELD_BATCH_SIZE=10` when the active DB is held. The expiry pass operates only on the archive DB and already requires zero archive holders (around line 1105), so the active-DB lock-friendliness limit does not apply to it. Each iteration also re-runs the `event JOIN session` scan from the start.
2. **The expiry pass shares, and can exhaust, the whole per-DB budget before any session is archived.** It receives the same `max_duration` and runs first.
3. **A full `PRAGMA integrity_check` runs on the entire archive DB on every run.** `_archive_report_batch` (around line 1605) runs it after the first batch of each process. Its cost is O(archive size) (21 GB here), not O(batch). Each batch is already verified before any active delete by the `archive_copy_guard` `EXCEPT` comparison in `_archive_write_batch` / `_archive_execute_batch`.
4. **Unheld batches are a fixed 500 sessions, with no byte or time bound, so a large batch can livelock.** Added 2026-11-13: on the 68 GB runner DB (unheld, so batch = 500), a 600 s run spent about 170 s on expiry. Batch 1 then committed its archive copy (archive DB 4.8 → 11.1 GB, plus a 10.6 GB archive WAL), but the deadline killed it during verify/delete after about 430 s. The active DB was unchanged. Every later run repeats the same copy (`INSERT OR IGNORE`) and verify and is killed again, so the oldest sessions never leave the active DB. `_archive_run_batches` (around line 1421) only checks the budget *before* starting a batch.
5. **The copy-guard `EXCEPT` verify spills to temp storage in proportion to the batch payload.** The single killed batch's `sqlite3` process had about 44 GB `write_bytes` (in `/proc/<pid>/io`), about 70 MB/s, while neither DB file grew. That fits `EXCEPT` building temp b-trees over full `part`/`message` rows. A primary-key-correlated check is just as strict and streams through the index without a temp sort, for example `SELECT NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM part p WHERE <filter> AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM archive.part a WHERE a.id = p.id AND a.col1 IS p.col1 AND ...))`.

Side observation, not required: the expiry cutoff equals worker retention (7 days), so a just-archived worker session's events are copied into the archive and expired on the next pass.

## How

Files to modify:

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh`
  - `_archive_expire_events`: use its own batch size (for example `OPENCODE_ARCHIVE_EVENT_EXPIRY_BATCH_SIZE`, default `DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE` 500), independent of the held active-DB batch size. Give it a bounded share of the budget (for example at most 25% of `max_duration`), or run it after session batches, so session archiving always gets time.
  - `_archive_report_batch`: do not run a full `PRAGMA integrity_check` on every run. Options, in order of preference: (a) run it only when the archive DB was created in this run; (b) record the last successful check (archive DB path + inode + size class + timestamp) under the archive state dir and re-check at most daily; (c) use `PRAGMA quick_check`, still O(N), so only as a fallback. Keep the abort-on-failure semantics when it does run.
  - `_archive_run_batches`: bound each batch by payload as well as count. For example, pick the session prefix whose `SUM(LENGTH(part.data)) + SUM(LENGTH(message.data))` stays under a byte cap (env-tunable, for example 256 MB). Halve the next batch when the last one took more than about a third of the remaining budget, and do not start a batch whose estimated time exceeds the remaining budget. A batch must always contain at least one session, so oversized single sessions still progress.
  - `_archive_write_batch` verify SQL: replace the `EXCEPT` full-row comparison with a primary-key-correlated `NOT EXISTS ... IS`-per-column check (same strictness, no temp b-tree). Keep the commit-archive → verify → delete-active ordering and the abort-on-mismatch semantics.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-async-helper.sh`: no budget change is required if the above lands. Optionally log the per-phase seconds (expiry, batches, integrity) so stalls are diagnosable from the log.
- Test: extend the existing archive tests (`rg -l 'opencode-db-archive' .agents/scripts/tests`) with a held-gate case asserting that the expiry pass deletes more than 10 rows per statement and that a second run on an existing archive does not invoke `integrity_check`.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-async-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh`

Integration evidence: the requested held-gate expiry and integrity regressions belong in the existing archive test suite. Verify with `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh` and ShellCheck.

## Acceptance

- [ ] With the active DB held (idle gate passed, batches of 10), a 60 s run archives well over one batch on a DB with thousands of eligible sessions (log shows multiple `Archived N/M sessions [batch K]` lines).
- [ ] The expiry pass cannot consume the whole per-DB budget before session archiving.
- [ ] A full `integrity_check` does not run on every scheduled run of an existing archive DB.
- [ ] An unheld run on a DB whose oldest sessions are multi-GB in total commits at least one batch within a 60 s budget (no repeated copy-then-kill), and the copy guard still aborts on any column mismatch.
- [ ] Existing archive tests pass, and ShellCheck is clean.

title: perf(git-shim): cut ~127 ms per-call canonical Git guard overhead without changing verdicts
body:
## What

Cut the mechanical per-call overhead of the aidevops canonical Git shim (`.agents/scripts/git` → `canonical-git-command-guard.py`) **without changing a single policy verdict**. Every `git` call made by pulse, workers, lifecycle cleanup and interactive sessions goes through it, because `~/.aidevops/bin/git` precedes the native `git` on the launchd service PATH (`aidevops_service_path` in `.agents/scripts/runtime-env.sh:78-88`).

## Why

Measured on a maintainer macOS runner on 2026-11-13 (15–20 sequential calls each, `git rev-parse HEAD` inside a linked worktree):

| Stage | Mean (ms) |
|---|---|
| native `git rev-parse HEAD` | 13 |
| `bash -c true` | 6 |
| `bash` + source `runtime-env.sh` + `aidevops_resolve_native_git` | 11 |
| `python3 -c pass` | 17 |
| `canonical-git-command-guard.py` alone | 93 |
| **full shim** | **140–234** |

Attribution inside the guard (`python3 -X importtime`):

- About 20 ms is imports. `canonical_git_policy.py:10` imports `tempfile` at module load (6.7 ms, which pulls in `shutil`, `random` and the compression modules), but it is only used at `:106` and `:141`. `argparse` costs 4.2 ms and `__future__` 2.3 ms.
- About 52 ms is four sequential native-git spawns in `is_canonical` (`canonical_git_repository.py:50-85`): `rev-parse --git-dir`, `rev-parse --git-common-dir`, `rev-parse --show-toplevel` and `config --get core.worktree`.
- The shim itself spawns a second `python3` only to JSON-encode argv (`.agents/scripts/git:34`, about 17 ms).

Volume (system-wide sampling of guard processes over 180 s, a lower bound): **571 shimmed calls (190/min)**. Pulse made 77/min, OpenCode sessions and workers 83/min, full-loop 14/min and the worker-lifecycle registry 13/min. At about 127 ms added per call, pulse alone loses about 10 s of every minute.

There is also a secondary symptom. On macOS with the shim on PATH, the worker-lifecycle `test_retirement` module stalled for more than 400 s, inside `preservation._run` waiting on `worktree-archive-helper.sh` (120 s helper timeout). With a clean PATH (`/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/bin:/bin`), the same module ran 47 tests in 196 s. CI on Linux has no shim and runs the full 475-test contract suite in 224 s.

## How

Precedent: #33062 / PR #33063 cut the `gh` shim's overhead with the same discipline, removing mechanical cost while keeping policy.

1. `.agents/scripts/git`: remove the argv-encoding `python3 -c` spawn. Pass the original argv to the guard positionally after `--`, and keep `--argv-json` accepted for existing callers.
2. `.agents/scripts/canonical-git-command-guard.py`: accept argv after `--`, using `argparse.REMAINDER` or equivalent. If `argparse` dominates, a minimal hand parser is acceptable.
3. `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_repository.py` `is_canonical`: replace the three `rev-parse` spawns with one `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir --git-common-dir --show-toplevel`. Parse the three lines in order. When that call fails (bare repo or outside a work tree, where `--show-toplevel` errors), fall back to the current individual calls so every existing edge case yields the same values. Keep the `core.worktree` read unless you can prove it is unnecessary for a given branch of the decision.
4. `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_policy.py`: import `tempfile` lazily inside the two functions that use it. Audit other module-level imports pulled in only for rare paths (clone or snapshot) and defer them the same way.

## Hard boundaries

- **No verdict changes.** Do not add bash-side fast paths that skip the Python policy engine, and do not exempt daemons, pulse or particular subcommands. This is a trust boundary: a regression here lets agents mutate canonical checkouts.
- Keep the existing `GIT_*` environment handling and `-C`, `--git-dir` and `--work-tree` prefix semantics exactly.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/git`
- `.agents/scripts/canonical-git-command-guard.py`
- `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_repository.py`
- `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_policy.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh`

## Acceptance

1. `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh` passes. Existing classification cases stay unchanged; only add cases for the new `--` argv transport and the combined `rev-parse` fallback, which covers a bare repo and a non-repository cwd.
2. `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-git-safety-gate.mjs` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-command-policy-helper.sh` still pass.
3. The measured mean full-shim overhead over native `git rev-parse HEAD` drops by at least 40% on the same host. Record before and after numbers in the PR. Measure with 20 sequential `subprocess.run` calls of `<worktree>/.agents/scripts/git -C <worktree> rev-parse HEAD` against native `git`.
4. Blocked canonical mutations, such as `git checkout` in a registered canonical checkout, still exit with the same block message.

Planning note: paths and line numbers were verified on `main` at `c1529ade32`.

title: fix(pulse-dispatch): surface why cleanup-receipt reconciliation refused worktree pre-creation
body:
## What

Make worktree pre-creation's `RECONCILIATION_FAILED` skips self-explaining in pulse.log, and name the process holding the cleanup-receipt lock when a wait times out.

## Why

On 2026-11-13, between 15:14:31Z and 15:15:09Z, pulse skipped dispatch for three issues in a private managed repository. The only recorded cause was:

```
helper_reason: 'AIDEVOPS_WORKTREE_LIFECYCLE_DISPOSITION=RECONCILIATION_FAILED branch=feature/auto-... head=fe95298... status=1'
```

The specific cause is lost in two places:

1. `full_loop_supersede_cleaned_receipts_for_recreated_worktree` (`.agents/scripts/full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh:1076-1078`) reports a lock failure only as "could not acquire the receipt lock for <dir>". It drops `_FULL_LOOP_RECEIPT_LOCK_FAILURE`, which already carries the holder PID and hold age.
2. `_dlw_precreate_helper_reason` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh:1023-1034`) matches only `managed-worktree:`, `Generation enrollment refused:` and the generic disposition. The helper's own `Cleanup-receipt reconciliation refused: <reason>` stderr line never reaches pulse.log.

The same lock also failed a merge's cleanup-receipt write (`cleanup-receipt-failure: receipt-lock-timeout (holder 51312, held 85s)` on PR #38084). By the time anyone looked, that PID had exited, and the holder's identity was unrecoverable. The receipt scans themselves are fast (three passes over 5,107 receipts take about 0.16 s each), so a long holder must exist elsewhere, but nothing records which process it is.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh`: on lock timeout with a live holder, capture a bounded, single-line, quote-stripped `ps -o command=` of the holder in `_FULL_LOOP_RECEIPT_LOCK_HOLDER_CMD`. Keep the `_FULL_LOOP_RECEIPT_LOCK_FAILURE` format unchanged; `test-full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh:121` pins it, and merge-cleanup retries on its prefix. Include both values in the supersede refusal reason and in the `cleanup-receipt-failure:` line from `full_loop_write_cleanup_deferred`.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`: rank `Cleanup-receipt reconciliation refused:` above the generic disposition, as GH#36142 did for enrollment refusals.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`

## Acceptance

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-add-managed-symlink-base.sh` pass, and ShellCheck reports nothing new.
- A lock timeout against a live holder yields a supersede reason that names the holder PID, hold age and command. Feeding that output to `_dlw_precreate_helper_reason` returns the refusal line rather than the generic disposition.

title: feat(pulse): auto-run native macOS verification for trusted needs-macos-verification PRs on a Darwin maintainer host
body:
## What

On a Darwin pulse host whose GitHub login is the repository's registered macOS maintainer, pulse should run the existing `macos-local-checks.sh verify-pr` for trusted open PRs labelled `needs-macos-verification`. Currently a human has to do this by hand, and in practice nobody does.

## Why

GH#36691 (PR #36701) routes macOS-sensitive PRs from non-Mac hosts to the registered macOS maintainer. Its direction was "that person's local run clears the label". The local run never happens:

- 17 PRs carried `needs-macos-verification` between 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-13, most from the Linux worker hosts.
- 6 of 6 sampled merged PRs (#37946, #37801, #37507, #37332, #37320, #36701) merged with the label still present and no native macOS evidence in Runtime Testing. No unlabel event exists on any of them.
- The sensitive paths include the canonical Git shim (`.agents/scripts/git`, `canonical*git*.py`). That shim runs every git call on the maintainer's Mac, which is also the host that runs pulse.

When run manually, the check works and is cheap. On 2026-11-13 an interactive session ran it for PR #38096 (the shim performance change): a detached clean worktree at the exact PR head, then `bash .agents/scripts/macos-local-checks.sh verify-pr 38096 marcusquinn/aidevops`. The same session measured the shim A/B on macOS: per-call overhead dropped from about 130 ms to about 80 ms. A Linux sandbox cannot produce that macOS-only evidence.

## How

Add a bounded pulse stage in a new `.agents/scripts/pulse-macos-verification.sh`. Source it from `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` in the same way as the neighbouring sub-libraries (`rg -n 'source "\$\{_PULSE_DISPATCH_ENGINE_SCRIPT_DIR\}/pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh"' .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`). Register it in `_run_preflight_stages()` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:1491`) after `preflight_early_dispatch`, using the existing asynchronous launch pattern (`rg -n '_preflight_start_async_cleanups' .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh`) so it never consumes dispatch budget. `pulse-wrapper.sh` only calls `_run_preflight_stages`; do not edit it. It is over the large-file threshold, which would hold this issue from dispatch. The stage does nothing unless every condition holds:

1. `macos_checks_host` (`.agents/scripts/macos-local-checks.sh`) prints `Darwin`.
2. The authenticated `gh` login equals the repo's registered `macos_maintainer`, falling back to `maintainer`. Resolve the login exactly as `macos_checks_route` does from `repos.json`.
3. PR candidates: open, non-draft, labelled `needs-macos-verification`, head repository equal to base repository (no forks), and required checks terminal-success at the current head.
4. `#aidevops:trust-boundary`: the PR author has `write`, `maintain` or `admin` permission on the repository. This stage executes PR code locally, so fail closed when the permission is unknown.

For at most one PR per cycle, with a hard budget (default 20 min, env-overridable):

- Fetch the PR head ref explicitly. Create a controlled linked worktree at the exact `headRefOid` through the sanctioned creation path, never canonical `git worktree add` or `reset --hard`, which the command policy refuses. Run `bash .agents/scripts/macos-local-checks.sh verify-pr <PR> <slug>` from that worktree, then remove the worktree through the guarded cleanup path.
- Persist the attempt keyed by `(slug, PR, headRefOid)` under `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/state/`, so one head is attempted only once per outcome.
- On failure, post one deduplicated PR comment (keyed by head SHA) naming the failing suite with the last ≤40 lines of its output, so the PR repair loop can act. Keep the label.
- Run in the background relative to dispatch, so a long suite never delays issue dispatch.

Limit `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` changes to one `source` line and one stage registration. Touch `macos-local-checks.sh` only if a small reusable hook is needed, such as exposing maintainer resolution. In `platform-support.md`, update the CI/CD section to describe the automatic Darwin path.

### Files Scope

- NEW: `.agents/scripts/pulse-macos-verification.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/macos-local-checks.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/platform-support.md`

## Acceptance

- On a non-Darwin host, or when the `gh` login is not the registered macOS maintainer, the stage exits immediately with no GitHub reads beyond what pulse already does.
- PRs from authors without write access, and fork PRs, are skipped and logged as `macos-verify skipped: untrusted-author` or `fork`.
- On Darwin with a trusted labelled PR, the stage runs `verify-pr` at the exact head. On success the existing helper records Runtime Testing evidence and removes the label. On failure, exactly one comment is posted per head SHA and the label stays.
- No more than one verification per cycle, and the stage respects its budget.
- ShellCheck is clean. Extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-macos-local-checks.sh` only if needed to cover candidate selection, using its existing `gh` stub pattern.

title: fix(worktree-helper): add <open-PR-branch> silently branches from origin/main when the PR ref was never fetched
body:
## What

`worktree-helper.sh add <branch>` should check out an open PR's remote branch (GH#33194) even when that branch has never been fetched into `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>`. Today it silently creates a same-named local branch from `origin/main`.

## Why

GH#33194 added this path to `_cmd_add_create_worktree` (`.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh:1376-1389`): "an unmerged remote branch (e.g. an open PR head) must be checked out directly rather than diverging from origin/<default>". Its detector, `check_stale_remote_branch` (`.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-git.sh:261-290`), consults only local remote-tracking refs via `_remote_refs_for_branch`.

## Reproducer

On 2026-11-13, an interactive session ran `worktree-helper.sh add feature/auto-20261113-152231-gh38094 <path>` to verify open PR #38096. The PR branch had been pushed by a worker on another host and was not yet fetched locally. Output:

```
Creating worktree with new branch 'feature/auto-20261113-152231-gh38094' based on 'origin/main'...
```

The worktree was on `origin/main`, not the PR head `a6c8d9d7`. Committing there and pushing would be rejected as non-fast-forward, and a reviewer running checks there would silently test `main` instead of the PR. Recovery needed a manual fetch plus a detached switch, because the command policy correctly forbids `reset --hard`.

## How

In `_cmd_add_create_worktree`, when no local branch exists and no explicit `--base` was given, refresh that one origin branch before the stale or unmerged checks. Use the existing `_worktree_refresh_origin_branch "$_branch"` (`.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh:1227`), which already fetches from linked-worktree context so the canonical Git guard holds. Treat a fetch failure because the branch is absent as "new branch" and keep today's path.

To avoid a network round trip on every pulse pre-creation, skip the refresh for pulse auto-branch names (`feature/auto-<timestamp>-gh<N>` created under `AIDEVOPS_WORKTREE_MANAGER`) unless an existing PR head is expected. Alternatively, limit the refresh to non-pulse callers. Choose whichever is simpler and keeps pulse latency unchanged.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh`

## Acceptance

- In a fixture repo with a bare `origin`, push branch `topic` from a second clone. In the first clone, without fetching, `worktree-helper.sh add topic <path>` yields a worktree whose `HEAD` equals the pushed `topic` commit and prints the "on unmerged remote" message.
- `worktree-helper.sh add brand-new-branch` behaves as before: based on `origin/<default>`, no error.
- The pulse pre-creation path adds no extra fetch for new auto branches; confirm with the existing `precreate.*` substage timing in the dispatch stage log.
- ShellCheck is clean, and existing `test-worktree-helper*.sh` suites that cover `add` still pass.

title: perf(dispatch): instrument and cut dedup layer-4 PR-evidence latency (p50 10s, p90 47s, 138 min/day)
body:
## What

Cut the per-candidate latency of dispatch dedup layer 4 (`has_open_pr`). Instrument its six parallel checks, then serve the dominant one from the per-cycle prefetched PR snapshot, without weakening any block or uncertainty verdict.

## Why

`~/.aidevops/logs/dispatch-stages.tsv` on the maintainer host for 2026-11-13 00:00–15:40Z (aggregated with a read-only script):

| substage | n | total | p50 | p90 | max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dedup.layer4_pr_evidence` | 420 | 137.8 min | 10.4 s | 46.8 s | 388 s |
| `dedup.ceremony_total` (launched workers) | 62 | 391 min | 349 s | 621 s | 748 s |

Layer 4 runs for every candidate, including the many that are later skipped. It is the largest single per-candidate cost after the footprint rebuild, which #38055 and #38089 already address. The full pre-launch ceremony now takes a median of about 6 minutes per worker, longer than many workers take to solve their issue (for example, #38094 took 4 minutes). On the same day, 11 dispatch candidates hit the 600 s stage timeout (`[pulse-wrapper] Stage timeout: dispatch_candidate_<N> exceeded 600s`) after spending their budget across serial gates.

`has_open_pr` (`.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh:1089-1189`) already runs six checks in parallel: healthy sibling, open commits, open body keyword, merged keywords, task-ID title, and superseded-issue PR. Its latency is therefore that of the slowest check. Search-API pacing or transport queueing is the likely tail (compare #37888), but this is unmeasured.

## How

1. Wrap each of the six background checks so it records its own substage through the existing `_ds_substage_*` helpers, named `dedup.layer4.<check>` (for example `dedup.layer4.merged_keywords`). This makes the dominant check visible in `dispatch-stages.tsv`. Follow the pattern used for `precreate.base_fetch_retry` (`.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh:1189-1195`).
2. Using the measured dominant check(s), serve the open-PR lookups from the per-cycle prefetched open-PR snapshot when it is fresh. The footprint path did the same in #38055: `rg -n 'prefetch' .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-footprint*.sh`. Fall back to the live query when the snapshot is missing or stale. Keep `PR_LOOKUP_RESULT=uncertain` precedence exactly as it is.
3. Do not change any block, allow or uncertainty verdict. Optimise transport only.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-dedup-layers.sh`

## Acceptance

- `dispatch-stages.tsv` records the six `dedup.layer4.<check>` substages for a real dispatch cycle.
- Existing suites pass: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh`, `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-stale-no-worker.sh`, and any `test-dispatch-dedup-pr*.sh`.
- The PR body reports before/after p50 and p90 for `dedup.layer4_pr_evidence` from at least one live pulse cycle, or names the dominant check and why it could not be served from the snapshot.
- ShellCheck is clean.

title: consolidation-task: merge thread on #20781 into single spec
body:
## Consolidation target: #20781

**Parent issue:** #20781 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** file-size-debt: .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh exceeds 2000 lines
**Parent labels:** `status:available,auto-dispatch,tier:thinking,origin:worker,consolidation-in-progress,file-size-debt,model:opus-4-7`

> Sources are inlined below unless explicitly listed as omitted. Fetch omitted references before consolidating.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below, fetching any explicitly omitted sources first.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `### Files Scope` — the successor's write surface, one repo-relative path per line and nothing else on the line (`- EDIT: path/to/file` or `- NEW: path/to/file`). Carry over the parent's scope when present. Read-only references belong in `## How`, not here. The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.
     Preserve every wildcard scope entry verbatim from every superseded issue, including tool-generated paths such as `- NEW: todo/<area>/log/*/*/<slug>-*.jsonl`. Never invent a concrete machine, date, timestamp or filename in place of a pattern. Never change an existing `EDIT:` entry to `NEW:`.
     Check each path against the current default branch before copying its scope marker: use `git ls-files` in an up-to-date default-branch checkout or `gh api` for that branch's contents. Use `EDIT:` when the path already exists on the default branch; use `NEW:` only after confirming it is absent. A stale checkout or failed API lookup is not proof of absence.
   - **Runner prerequisites** — copy verbatim every line matching `^requires-secrets:` and its runner-prerequisite paragraph from every superseded issue. Keep all source lines (do not replace them with a summary): the runner capability gate unions comma/space-separated names across these lines. Never drop a prerequisite because this consolidation runner lacks the named secret; consolidation itself does not need those credentials.
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #20781 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`
   That marker must be a line by itself, exactly as shown (no extra text, no trailing whitespace); the dispatch gate refuses consolidated successors without it. Put any further lineage (for example "#20781 itself superseded #M") on a separate line, and add one exact marker line per additional superseded issue.

3. **Validate before filing the new consolidated issue.** Save the parent body (inlined or explicitly fetched) verbatim to a local file, plus a separate body file for each additional superseded issue. Validate the merged body against ALL sources; a failed check stops publication and parent closure until the merged body is repaired:

```bash
python3 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/consolidation-contract-validator.py \
  --parent 20781 \
  --source "<file containing the verbatim parent body>" \
  --successor "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
# Repeat --source for each additional superseded issue body.
# Repeat --parent for each additional superseded issue number.
```

The validator must pass before running the signed creation command below. It checks the exact marker line for every `--parent`, verbatim secret lines and prerequisite paragraphs, wildcard scope preservation, and EDIT-to-NEW regressions. Also run `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check` on the merged body for ordinary scope syntax validation.

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,status:available,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding all status:* labels, needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body-file "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Use the signed wrapper above rather than the raw GitHub CLI so the successor retains the managed signature and origin metadata.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` and `status:available` are also mandatory. Keep exactly one `status:*` label on the successor: `status:available` — never the parent's ownership status (`status:queued`, `status:claimed`, `status:in-progress`, `status:in-review`). Immediately before creating the successor, re-read the parent's labels; if it now carries `status:blocked`, use `status:blocked` instead, because that label records an unresolved dependency or hold rather than ownership. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch; the fill-floor enumerator also needs the available status, and the pre-claim gate holds a `status:blocked` successor until its blocker is released.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close every superseded parent and verify each handoff.** Run all five commands below for #20781, then repeat them for every additional issue passed as `--parent` in step 3, substituting that issue number in every command (including dependency repointing and the state check). Every command must succeed:

```bash
gh issue comment 20781 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 20781 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 20781 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
# Repoint open dependants' blockedBy edges and Blocked-by lines at the successor (GH#35130):
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dependency-supersession-repoint-helper.sh repoint "marcusquinn/aidevops" 20781 $NEW_NUM
# Re-read the parent (GH#37600); this must print exactly: closed not_planned
gh api "repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/20781" --jq '.state + " " + (.state_reason // "")'
```

   **Handoff verification (GH#37600):** a parent that still reads `open` keeps the `consolidated` label while the dispatch gate rejects it, so it consumes dispatch attempts every cycle. If any command above fails or refuses the write (for example a worker target-scope guard on a non-target issue), or any parent re-read is not `closed not_planned`, this task has FAILED: do not run step 5 and do not report success. Leave this consolidation task open, record the parent number, the failing command and its output in one comment here, and exit `BLOCKED`. Report a reopen observed after your close as evidence, with its event time; do not guess its cause.

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** only after every parent passed the step 4 verification, with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #20781 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- Read only explicitly omitted source references when the packet size limit prevents inlining them; otherwise do NOT re-read #20781.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Checkpoint recovery is never an unconditional requirement** (GH#35871). Name a checkpoint commit or branch as binding only after verifying it is reachable from a remote ref (`gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/commits/<sha>`), recording the full SHA and ref. Otherwise write: "Best-effort recovery: reuse if reachable; the functional spec is the source of truth; re-implement if unrecoverable." Never forbid re-implementing work that exists only as local commits on one runner.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn

title: fix(checkpoints): idle worker drafts stranded after a failed continuation launch, worker_failed/ready-transition releases, or unanswered blocked attention
body:
## What

Give every idle, unassigned worker draft checkpoint an automatic, bounded recovery route. Today three failure paths leave the draft and its issue idle with no recovery route:

- Fresh dispatch is blocked (`worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked`).
- Stalled continuation is skipped (`STALLED_CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_SKIPPED: ... has no current stall release`).
- `approval-template` refuses to generate an approval.

The dispatcher still re-evaluates each held issue every few hours, at 25–400 s per evaluation (observed `dispatch_with_dedup ... elapsed_ms=402277`).

## Why

Observed 2026-11-13 on one managed product repo with a 3-runner fleet on v3.39.188. 16 unassigned issues were held by idle worker drafts, idle from a few hours up to 6 days:

| Pattern | Drafts | Current route |
|---|---|---|
| A. Stall-class release (`worker_draft_checkpoint` / `worker_complete`), then **one continuation launch failed before the worker started** | 3 | none: stranded permanently |
| B. `worker_failed` release | 5 (3 with a prior approval) | none: not stall-class; `approval-template` → `open_at_end` / not trusted release |
| C. `worker_claim_ready_transition_failed` release | 1 | attention posted once, then nothing |
| D. `blocked` release (worker decision) | 7 | attention posted once, then nothing |

Over 13 h, the local runner logged 39 `has no current stall release` skips and 101 `worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked`/`stale_draft_checkpoint` dispatch blocks for this set.

### Root cause A (most severe): a failed continuation launch permanently hides the stall release

Sequence (example: draft head `b4f2689`, 2026-11-13):

1. 14:47: the worker releases `reason=worker_draft_checkpoint` (stall-class per `_PCC_STALL_RELEASE_PATTERN`).
2. 15:01: a runner's `_pcc_dispatch_stalled` emits `STALE_PR_CONTINUATION`, posts its continuation `DISPATCH_CLAIM` and starts the guarded launch.
3. The ownership transfer in `_prrts_prepare_worker_ownership` fails (`set_issue_status ... in-progress`). `PRRTS_WORKTREE_FAILURE_REASON=checkpoint_ownership_transfer_failed`, the scanner returns `PRRTS_RC_RETRYABLE_FAILURE` (13), and the helper logs `launch failed rc=13`.
4. 15:04: the episode closes with a terminal `DISPATCH_LEASE`. Both the claim and the terminal lease comments are edited afterwards.
5. From then on, `_pcc_stall_release_evidence` takes the newest ownership event, which is the edited terminal lease. `closes_earlier_lease` requires `unedited`, so the lease counts as ownership. `$release | unedited and stall_release` then fails, and the draft gets `has no current stall release` on every cycle, permanently.
6. The local scanner state records `blocked_by=code maintainer_attention=true blocker_reason=checkpoint_ownership_transfer_failed`, but **nothing is posted to GitHub**, so no maintainer can see it.

Two other drafts show the same event shape: an older stall-class release, then an edited continuation `DISPATCH_CLAIM` plus an edited terminal lease within 2 minutes.

So the failure is classified as retryable, but the evidence model makes it unrecoverable. The ownership-transfer failure (a GitHub label/assignment write) is also classified as `code` instead of infrastructure.

### Root cause B/C: non-decision failure releases are not continuation evidence

- `_PCC_STALL_RELEASE_PATTERN` (`pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` line 66) and `STALL_RELEASE_REASONS` (`pr_checkpoint_events.py` around lines 106–116) exclude `worker_failed` and `worker_claim_ready_transition_failed`. Neither is a worker decision.
- GH#37984 / PR #37995 fixed only *new* watchdog hard-kill releases. Older `worker_failed` episodes and non-hard-kill failures still strand the draft.
- For approval-bound episodes, `approval-template` (`pr-checkpoint-revision.py` `template()`, around lines 188–230) treats a `worker_failed` successor without a terminal lease as `open_at_end`. Only the owning device can post that terminal (`close-expired-pr-checkpoint-lease`). For non-approval continuation claims, that command denies with `not_checkpoint_claim`. When the owning device is another machine, no maintainer can recover the draft.

### Root cause D: unanswered `blocked` attention never escalates

One attention record is posted per head and release. If nobody acts, nothing escalates or expires. The dispatch cost of re-evaluating these drafts is already bounded by the existing negative cache (see How 5); the missing piece, automatic resolution of decision blockers, is outside this issue.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `rg -o 'PR #[0-9]+ in [^ ]+ has no current stall release issue=#[0-9]+' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | sort -u | wc -l`

**Actual output:** a stable set of drafts skipped on every cycle (16 unique on 2026-11-13). For pattern A, the continuation runner logs `PR_CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_BLOCKED: ... launch failed rc=13`, and its local state has `blocker_reason=checkpoint_ownership_transfer_failed maintainer_attention=true` with nothing posted to the issue.

**Expected:** each draft gets a bounded continuation or a visible maintainer-attention record.

Full steps:

```bash
# Unique stranded drafts on a runner
rg -o 'PR #[0-9]+ in [^ ]+ has no current stall release issue=#[0-9]+' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | sort -u
# Pattern A: on the runner that attempted the continuation
rg -n 'launch failed rc=13' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log
rg -n 'blocker_reason' ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/pr-checkpoint-continuation/OWNER-REPO-PR.state
#   -> blocker_reason=checkpoint_ownership_transfer_failed, maintainer_attention=true (local only)
# Then list the issue's coordination comments: the newest ownership events are an
# edited continuation DISPATCH_CLAIM and an edited DISPATCH_LEASE phase=terminal after the stall release.
# Pattern B (approval-bound worker_failed episode):
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh approval-template OWNER/REPO PR ISSUE PREVIOUS_RELEASE_ID attempt:PREVIOUS_ATTEMPT
#   -> "intervening coordination is not fully released ... reason=open_at_end"
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-helper.sh close-expired-pr-checkpoint-lease ISSUE OWNER/REPO CLAIM_ID SESSION
#   -> PR_CHECKPOINT_LEASE_CLOSE_DENIED reason=not_checkpoint_claim   (non-approval continuation claim)
```

## How

1. **Pattern A.** In `_pcc_stall_release_evidence`, treat a *never-launched* continuation episode for the same PR head as transparent: the runner's own `pr-checkpoint-continuation-<repo>-<pr>` session, closed by a terminal lease, with no `Dispatching worker` and no `phase=ready` lease. The prior stall release then stays current evidence. Count each such episode toward the existing per-head stall fuse (`stalls >= 2` → attention) so retries stay bounded. Do not weaken the "edited coordination is a fence" rule for any other event.
2. **Pattern A.** In the ownership-transfer step, classify `set_issue_status`/assignment write failures as infrastructure (retryable), not `code`. Whenever the scanner state records `maintainer_attention=true` for a checkpoint continuation, post one deduplicated attention record to the issue, so the decision is never stored only in a runner's local state.
3. **Patterns B/C.** Treat `worker_failed` and `worker_claim_ready_transition_failed` as stall-class for continuation, in both the shell pattern and `STALL_RELEASE_REASONS`, so they get one bounded exact-head continuation per head under the existing fuse and `_PCC_MAX_PR_RELEASES`. Keep `blocked` decision-class.
4. **Pattern B, approvals.** In the `approval-template` successor walk, accept an intervening episode as closed when it has a trusted release from its own runner, its lease expired more than 60 min ago, and no live executor exists for its session. Record it in `released_successors` with `outcome` set to the release reason. Do not require the owning device's terminal lease.
5. **Pattern D: no new label (brief-owner decision, 2026-11-13).** Do not add a label hold or a candidate-selection filter. The existing dispatch negative cache already supplies the cheap hold: in `pulse-dispatch-lib.sh` `_dispatch_negative_cache_reason`, the `worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked | stale_draft_checkpoint` branch skips the dispatch ceremony for an unassigned draft for up to the 6 h quiet TTL. It is keyed to the issue's `updatedAt`, the exact PR fingerprint and the attention re-arm boundary. An approval comment or a brief edit bumps `updatedAt`, so the hold clears at once and `dispatch-approved` / `blocked-attention` stay reachable. A label filtered before `dispatch_with_dedup` would hide exactly those routes (the continuation worker's finding), so it would be a regression. No code change is needed for this item.

### Decision record (brief owner, 2026-11-13)

This answers the `CONTINUATION_BLOCKER_FINDING` on draft PR #38133 at head `fa38fab557` (`ttl_hold_design_choice`):

- **Criterion 5:** resolved as "no new label"; see How 5. PR #38133 needs no further code for it.
- **Remaining scope for PR #38133:** criteria 1–4 as already implemented on the draft. Fix the failing required checks at that head (`Qlty Smell Regression`, `Qlty Regression Gate`, `CodeFactor`): reduce the added complexity in the changed functions rather than suppressing the findings. Then run the verification below and mark the PR ready.
- **Out of scope for PR #38133:** the 2026-11-13 19:01 comment (an approved revision launch fails after the ownership transfer and leaves the issue assigned). Its root cause, the prelaunch lease expiring during transfer and worktree preparation, is #38145 (PR #38148). Any restore gap that remains after that fix gets its own issue.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh:1436-1468` (`_pcc_stall_release_evidence`; the shared jq defs are at lines 94–128)
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh:1776-1830` (`_pcc_dispatch_stalled`)
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh:180-209` (ownership transfer failure classification)
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pr_checkpoint_events.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-revision.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-draft-checkpoint-unblock.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-attention.sh`

Line ranges are from `main` at filing time; re-locate them by function name if they have drifted. The continuation helper itself is about 2,000 lines, so read only these ranges plus the jq defs. The draft PR #38133 also touches `pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh`, `pr_checkpoint_episodes.py`, `pr_checkpoint_history.py` and related tests; those edits are accepted as part of criteria 1–4.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A stall-class release followed by one never-launched continuation episode on the same head still yields exactly one more bounded continuation; a second failure posts attention instead of looping.
- [ ] An ownership-transfer write failure is reported as infrastructure/retryable, and any checkpoint `maintainer_attention` is visible on the issue.
- [ ] An unassigned draft whose last release is `worker_failed` or `worker_claim_ready_transition_failed` gets one bounded continuation per head under the existing fuse.
- [ ] `approval-template` produces an approval when the only intervening episode is an expired, released, executor-less episode from another device of the same runner.
- [ ] No new label or candidate filter for `blocked` drafts; the existing `worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked` negative cache stays the only hold before the ceremony (no diff to `pulse-dispatch-lib.sh` for this item).
- [ ] Existing continuation/attention tests pass, ShellCheck/ruff are clean, and the required Qlty/CodeFactor checks pass at the final head.
