title: perf(dispatch-claim): expired checkpoint-claim sweep starves on loaded runners — sweep own claims from a device-local ledger first
body:
## What

Make the owner-device expired checkpoint-claim sweep (GH#38028 / PR #38078) reach this device's own stranded claims every cycle, even on a loaded runner. Today it rotates across all pulse repos inside half of the remaining stale-blocked sweep stage. On a busy runner, the repo holding the claims is rarely reached.

## Why

Observed 2026-11-13 on a shared Linux runner (24 cores, load average 57–68) running v3.39.188, which includes PR #38078:

- The per-repo sweep cursor for the product repo with about 45 open worker drafts advanced once at deploy and not again for over 70 minutes. The stale-blocked `draft-checkpoint-unblock` pass for that repo logged `deferred ... sweep deadline reached (GH#36041)` on every cycle in the sampled log. `reap_orphan_workers` was also deferred with `cycle budget exhausted`.
- One approval-bound prelaunch claim had expired about 15 h earlier and still held its maintainer approval (`open_at_end`). Running `dispatch-claim-helper.sh sweep-pr-checkpoint-claim <issue> <repo> 0` by hand as the runner user released it immediately (`CLAIM_RELEASED reason=claim_only_no_worker`). A fresh approval was then published.

Root cause: `_pdcu_sweep_expired_claims` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-draft-checkpoint-unblock.sh`, around lines 362–386) discovers candidates by listing every open worker draft in a repo (GitHub reads, capped at 10 visits per call). `pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh` (around lines 940–961) visits repos one at a time from a persisted cursor, with a deadline of half the remaining stale-blocked stage. Cost scales with fleet-wide drafts × repos, but the work that matters is only *this device's own* open prelaunch claims, which the device already knows about because it posted them.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `rg -n 'draft-checkpoint-unblock pass deferred' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | tail -n 3` on a loaded runner, plus the mtime of the product repo's file under `~/.aidevops/cache/checkpoint-claim-sweep/`

**Actual output:** `... draft-checkpoint-unblock pass deferred for OWNER/REPO: sweep deadline reached (GH#36041)` on every sampled cycle; the cursor file did not advance for 70+ minutes; an own expired prelaunch claim stayed unreleased for about 15 h.

**Expected:** own expired prelaunch claims are released within one cycle.

Full steps, on a runner whose pulse cycle is budget-constrained (stale-blocked passes deferred):

```bash
# Sweep cursor staleness per repo (mtime should advance each cycle the repo is visited)
ls -l --time-style=+%FT%T ~/.aidevops/cache/checkpoint-claim-sweep/
rg -n 'draft-checkpoint-unblock pass deferred|reap_orphan_workers cycle budget exhausted' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | tail -n 5
# An issue with this device's own expired DISPATCH_CLAIM phase=prelaunch checkpoint_mode=revision and no later release:
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-helper.sh sweep-pr-checkpoint-claim ISSUE OWNER/REPO 0
# -> posts CLAIM_RELEASED reason=claim_only_no_worker immediately; the scheduled sweep had not reached it for hours
```

## How

- EDIT `.agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-checkpoint.sh` / `.agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-helper.sh`: when posting a checkpoint `DISPATCH_CLAIM` (`phase=prelaunch`, `checkpoint_mode=revision`), append `{repo, issue, claim_id, session, expires_at}` to a device-local ledger (for example `~/.aidevops/state/checkpoint-claims.jsonl`, 0600). Remove the entry on ready transition, release or terminal.
- EDIT `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh`: before the repo rotation, run `sweep-pr-checkpoint-claim` for every ledger entry whose `expires_at` has passed. Cost is O(own expired claims), with no repo scan and no dependency on the shared stage deadline beyond a small floor. Keep the existing rotation as the fallback for claims posted before the ledger existed.
- All existing fences stay unchanged: identity, device, session, live executor and final timeline revalidation in `cmd_sweep_pr_checkpoint_claim`.
- Test: add a new focused suite `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-claim-ledger.sh` with a ledger-driven sweep case (expired entry → release posted; live/ready entry → untouched; ledger entry pruned after release). Reuse the stub setup pattern from the existing claim-helper suite, but do not grow that suite: it is over the 2,000-line large-file threshold (simplification is tracked in #38030).

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-checkpoint.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh`
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-claim-ledger.sh`

## Acceptance

- [ ] An expired own prelaunch checkpoint claim is released within one pulse cycle, even when the stale-blocked stage defers every repo pass.
- [ ] The sweep makes no GitHub reads when the ledger has no expired entries.
- [ ] Existing claim-helper tests pass, and ShellCheck is clean.

title: t18980: Reclaim phase 2: observe worktree owners through the lifecycle registry and ProcessAdapter, not a /proc scan
body:
<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## Goal

Phase 2 of #38051 (Reclaim). Decide "does anyone still own this worktree?" from the
worker-lifecycle registry, observed through `ProcessAdapter`, instead of a global
`/proc` scan. The lifecycle registry already records, per worktree generation, the
runs (process identities) admitted to it; Reclaim should ask it rather than keep a
parallel, weaker mechanism.

## Evidence (2026-11-13, this host, read-only probe)

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Linked worktrees under the base dir | 67 |
| Enrolled in the lifecycle registry | 65 |
| Trees with a live registered owner (`ProcessAdapter.observe`) | 6 |
| ...of which the `/proc` census also saw | 2 |
| Trees the census held but the registry did not | 0 |
| Not enrolled / generation unreadable | 1 / 1 |

The census misses owners whose working directory is elsewhere (it matches only cwd
and argv substrings), while the registry knows them by identity, including PID-reuse
protection. Nothing the census caught is lost by switching.

## Required change

1. New `worker_lifecycle/reclaim/owners.py`:
   - Resolve the state directory exactly as `worker-lifecycle-state.sh`
     `worker_lifecycle_state_dir` does (`AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_STATE_DIR`, then
     `~/.config/aidevops/lifecycle-state-dir`, then
     `${AIDEVOPS_WORKSPACE_DIR:-~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace}/worker-lifecycle`).
   - Open `LifecycleRegistry`, build `runtime.adapter_for(installation_id)` and run
     `runtime.require_ready` once per pass. Any failure → pass-level
     `owner-observation-unavailable`, every candidate refused (fail closed, as today's
     `process-inventory-unavailable`).
   - `owner(path) -> str | None`: `GenerationEnrollment.inspect(path)` → generation;
     for each non-ended run from `cleanup_plan._runs`, `adapter.observe(identity)`.
     `alive` → `owner-alive`; `unknown` → `owner-unobservable`; not enrolled →
     `not-enrolled`; any other registry error → `owner-registry-unreadable`.
     Read-only: never write observations or events.
2. `reclaim/evidence.py`: replace the `Census` parameter with the owner observer;
   `_unsafe_to_remove` returns its reason before `nothing_to_lose`. Order unchanged:
   GitHub first, so the registry is read only for finished candidates.
3. `reclaim/host.py`: delete `Census`, `process_census`, `_arguments`,
   `_live_same_user`; `remove()` re-checks the owner immediately before deletion
   (`owners-appeared`).
4. `reclaim/sweep.py`: receipt drops `unplaceable_processes`, adds
   `"residual_risk": "unregistered-processes-unobserved"` (stated, not hidden:
   orphaned descendants of a dead run are not observed; removal still requires
   finished work, a clean tree and zero unpushed commits).
5. `.agents/reference/worktree-registry.md`: replace the census description with the
   registry contract and the residual risk.
6. `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_reclaim.py`: adjust existing tests to the new
   parameter (no new test infrastructure).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/reclaim/owners.py`
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/reclaim/evidence.py`
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/reclaim/host.py`
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/reclaim/sweep.py`
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_reclaim.py`
- `.agents/reference/worktree-registry.md`

## Out of scope

Decision journal / CAS / `remove|archive|refuse` classification (phase 3), archive
stage (later), removing `legacy_*` (phase 5), any change to `decide_cleanup` or
`cleanup_authorized`.

## Verification

- `uvx ruff check --no-cache`, `uvx mypy --config-file mypy.ini --platform linux|darwin` clean.
- `PYTHONPATH=.agents/worker-lifecycle python3 -m unittest test_reclaim` passes.
- `rg -n "process_census|Census" .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/reclaim` → none.
- Live dry run `worktree-reclaim.py --budget-seconds 120` finishes inside budget and
  refuses every tree with a live registered owner.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Brief workflow contract</summary>

## Brief Workflow

This issue body is composed under `.agents/workflows/brief.md`. Newly queued auto-dispatch work must pass its `Dispatch Readiness Contract (brief schema v2)`: complete write surface, hazards and compatibility, executable verification mapped to affected surfaces, and positive plus negative/regression acceptance criteria.

body:
## What

Two stale-recovery assertions fail on `main` (`c87f35c4f5`, 2026-11-13). Neither test runs in CI, so nothing has flagged them. Bring both suites back to all-pass by fixing whichever side drifted: the production rule or the test expectation.

## Reproducer

From any linked worktree at `main` `c87f35c4f5` or later:

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-stale-recovery-escalation.sh | rg 'FAIL|failed'
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-stale-no-worker.sh | rg 'FAIL|failed'
```

Observed: `1 / 38 tests failed` and `Tests run: 11 failed: 1`. Expected: 0 failures in both.

## Why

Both failures reproduce identically on unchanged `main` and in an unrelated worktree (found while verifying PR #38109):

1. `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-stale-recovery-escalation.sh`: 37/38. Failure:
   `FAIL recovery_bare cannot authorize stale PR continuation (got: 'STALE_PR_CONTINUATION: issue #99999 in owner/repo — PR #86 preserved for exact-head continuation assignee=stale-runner')`
   The fixture (`test-stale-recovery-escalation.sh:184`) is an `origin:worker-takeover` same-repo draft with no closing refs and body `Recovered work for #99999`, which has no `For #N` line.
2. `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-stale-no-worker.sh`: 10/11. Failure: `FAIL remote branch liveness and recovery evidence` with an empty result. One of the bare `exit 1` guards in the subshell at `test-dispatch-dedup-stale-no-worker.sh:437-484` fires before `printf 'ok'`.

Likely cause of (1): GH#37915 (#37916, 2026-11-12, `d174341873`) changed `worker_checkpoint_draft_links` in `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-target-lib.sh` to accept `For #N` / `Ref(s) #N` "anywhere in the body, word-bounded, case-insensitive" (header comment, lines 80-90). Prose such as `work for #99999` now links. The same file's GH#34008 comment (lines 71-78) still says "Bare mentions ... never match". The two contracts disagree. This is unverified; confirm it with `git log -p` and by re-running the test at `d174341873^`.

Likely cause of (2): unknown. Candidate commits touching the stale path: `1820a832da` (#37819, 2026-11-12) and `d174341873`.

## How

1. For (1), decide which contract is intended. The safer reading, and the one the GH#34008 comment and the test both state, is that a takeover draft links only through an explicit reference, not prose. If you keep case-insensitive matching, require the keyword to start a line or be followed only by the issue reference: `(?mi)^\s*(For|Refs?)\s+#N\b`, so mid-sentence prose like `work for #99999` no longer links. Then keep both header comments consistent. If you conclude prose links are intended, update the `recovery_bare` fixture and the GH#34008 comment instead, and say why in the PR.
2. For (2), add a distinct `printf` label before each `exit 1` in that subshell (or run it with `bash -x`) to find the failing guard, then fix the drifted side the same way.
3. Do not weaken any other fixture in either suite: `recovery_for_ready`, `recovery_for_cross`, `recovery_for_protected`, and `recovery_for_other_closing` must still refuse continuation.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-target-lib.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-stale-recovery-escalation.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-stale-no-worker.sh`

Edit the library or the fixture, depending on the decision in How step 1. The stale-assignment source that test (2) exercises is not known yet; find it with `rg -n '_is_stale_assignment\(\)' .agents/scripts`.

## Acceptance

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-stale-recovery-escalation.sh` reports 38/38.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-stale-no-worker.sh` reports 11/11.

title: perf(dep-unblock): ready dependants stay status:blocked for hours — event reconciler fails silently; stale sweep ready lane starved by full listing
body:
## What

Make dependency-chain unblocking near-immediate and observable. On a fleet running chained phase issues (each objective split into sequential issues joined by `Blocked by: #N` plus native blocked-by edges), dependants stay `status:blocked` for hours to days after their blockers close. The fleet then idles for lack of dispatchable work while capacity is free.

## Why

Observed 2026-11-13 on one managed product repo with 3 runners on v3.39.188 (target capacity 20 + 32 + 24 simultaneous workers):

- Running workers: 1 + 2 + 0 against 76 slots. Only about 10 issues were dispatchable. 360 of 472 open chained issues were `status:blocked`, and 283 of those were waiting only on a dependency (no terminal-blocker record).
- **33 of 301 dependency-blocked issues had every declared blocker already CLOSED.** Lag ranged from 1–2 h (several) to 18–24 h and 6–29 days (oldest). Most were legitimately held by a later `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked`. The rest had no hold and were never released.
- Replaying the existing guarded `reconcile_dependants_after_verified_closure` by hand for 30 closed blockers immediately unblocked **9 hold-free dependants** (`rc=0` for all; held ones correctly stayed blocked). Three had been missed within the previous hour. The unblock *decision* logic is correct; the two paths that should run it do not reliably reach it.
- Example: a blocker closed at 15:50Z by the worker's own `full-loop-helper` merge. Of its 4 dependants, 1 was unblocked, 1 correctly stayed blocked (another open blocker), and **2 with no hold and all blockers closed stayed blocked**. A read-only replay 90 min later classified both as ready (`_der_native_blockers_closed`=0, `_der_all_declared_blockers_closed`=0, `_der_has_hold`=no). Nothing was logged.

### Root cause 1: the event path fails silently and aborts on the first per-dependant error

`reconcile_dependants_after_verified_closure` (`.agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh:518-552`) has about 8 `return 1` exits: the live-closed check, the context fetch, GraphQL shape validation, candidate collection, and any `_der_try_unblock` status other than 0/`DER_NOT_READY`. That last exit skips every remaining sibling. `_der_try_unblock` (`:482-515`) makes 3–4 live calls per dependant (paginated comments, labels re-read, edit), so one transient failure is enough. All callers (`full-loop-helper-merge.sh` ~434, `pulse-merge-issue-closeout.sh` ~262/308, `issue-sync-helper-close.sh` ~575, `github-cli-helper.sh` ~364) wrap it in `|| true`, and the function itself prints nothing. Failures are invisible.

### Root cause 2: the stale-blocked sweep's ready lane exists but gets no time

`reconcile_stale_blocked_issues` (`dependency-event-reconciler.sh:705-802`) already prioritises a **ready lane**: issues whose native blockers are all CLOSED, up to `DER_STALE_BLOCKED_READY_MAX=10` per run. In practice it visits 0–1 per run:

```text
runner A: ... candidates=337 pending=189 visited=1 ... ready=13 ready_visited=1
runner B: ... candidates=389 pending=269 visited=0 ... ready=32 ready_visited=0
runner C: ... candidates=421 pending=234 visited=0 ... ready=32 ready_visited=0
```

The budget is spent before the first visit:

- `stale_blocked_reconcile` has a 60 s stage timeout minus a 15 s margin (`_pulse_stale_blocked_sweep_deadline`, `pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh:631`). Up to half of that goes to `_pdcu_sweep_expired_claims` (`:942-961`), and the rest is shared by every due repo (`:988-1021`).
- For this repo, the sweep first lists **all** `status:blocked` issues with full bodies over REST (`:724`, ~4 pages), then lists them again over paginated GraphQL with `blockedBy` (`_der_open_native_blocked_numbers`, `:601-629`, ~4 pages). By the time both finish, `DER_STALE_BLOCKED_STOP_EPOCH` has passed, and the loop breaks at `:740` before visiting anything, ready lane included.
- Held ready issues (terminal-blocker records) are not memoised in the ready lane (`:757` applies the memo only to `is_ready == false`), so the ~20 held ones are re-read every rotation and dilute the 10-slot lane.
- The stage is classed `deferrable` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-budget-priority.sh:190`.

The older cursor walk `refresh_blocked_status_from_graph` (`pulse-dep-graph.sh`) is similarly starved: 2–6 visits per 30 s run, deferred in 24/31, 132/207 and 9/10 cycles on the three runners.

Prior work on the same symptom, all closed: #33246, #34055, #34353, #36041, #38039. This is a recurrence at higher chain volume (300+ blocked issues in one repo).

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `rg -o 'stale sweep repo=[^ ]+ candidates=[0-9]+ .* visited=[0-9]+ .* ready=[0-9]+ ready_visited=[0-9]+' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | tail -n 3`

**Actual output:** `stale sweep repo=OWNER/REPO candidates=389 ... visited=0 ... ready=32 ready_visited=0` on consecutive runs, while the `Stage complete: stale_blocked_reconcile (0, 46s)` lines show the stage using its whole budget.

**Expected:** a hold-free ready dependant is unblocked within one cycle of its last blocker closing.

Full steps:

```bash
# 1. Ready lane starvation
rg -o 'stale sweep repo=[^ ]+ .*ready=[0-9]+ ready_visited=[0-9]+' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | tail -n 5
rg 'Stage (start|complete): stale_blocked_reconcile' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | tail -n 4
# 2. Event path is silent: no per-closure reconciler line exists to grep for
rg -c 'reconcile_dependants|dependants after' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log   # -> 0
# 3. Stale dependants: open status:blocked issues whose every blockedBy node is CLOSED and that
#    have no hold (_der_has_hold) -- run _der_try_unblock's predicates read-only per issue
```

## How

1. **Event path — never silent, never abort siblings.** In `reconcile_dependants_after_verified_closure` (`dependency-event-reconciler.sh:518-552`), log one line per closure (`[dependency-reconciler] closure repo=… closed=#N dependants=K unblocked=… not_ready=… held=… failed=…`) and one line for each early-exit reason. On a per-dependant failure, record it and `continue`, then return a distinct partial status. Append failed dependants, and closures that failed before candidate collection, to a device-local retry ledger (for example `~/.aidevops/cache/dep-unblock-retry/<owner>__<repo>.txt`). Write the log to stderr so callers' existing `2>>` capture keeps it. Callers keep `|| true`.
2. **Stale sweep — the ready lane must not pay for the full listing.** In `reconcile_stale_blocked_issues` (`:705-802`):
   - Run the cheap GraphQL `blockedBy` listing (`_der_open_native_blocked_numbers`) **first**. It already yields the `ready` set. Visit ready numbers plus retry-ledger entries before the full REST body listing, fetching each one's labels/body individually (one `gh issue view --json number,title,body,labels,updatedAt`). These visits are bounded only by the hard stop, not the per-repo share.
   - Fetch the full REST listing only if time remains for the ordinary lane.
   - Memoise held ready issues by `updated_at` the same way as the ordinary lane, so unchanged held issues stop consuming ready slots.
3. **Budget.** In `.agents/scripts/pulse-budget-priority.sh:190`, do not defer `stale_blocked_reconcile` when the last recorded run for any repo reported `ready>0` or the retry ledger is non-empty (the weight cache under `~/.aidevops/cache/stale-blocked-weight/` shows the pattern). In `pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh:929-1029`, cap the expired-claim sweep's share so the ready lane always gets a minimum, for example `PULSE_STALE_BLOCKED_READY_MIN_SECONDS=15`.
4. Keep every existing guard unchanged: `_der_has_hold`, the native and declared blocker checks, the upstream release gate, the live label re-read and `_der_has_active_status` before the edit. Unblock decisions must stay exactly those of `_der_try_unblock`.
5. Test: add `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler-partial.sh`, covering (a) one dependant failing while its siblings are still unblocked, with the failure logged and ledgered, and (b) a stale sweep under a near-expired deadline still visiting ready-lane and ledger issues before the REST listing. Run the existing `tests/test-pulse-stale-blocked-reconcile.sh`.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh:929-1029`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-budget-priority.sh`
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler-partial.sh`

## Acceptance

- [ ] A transient failure on one dependant no longer prevents unblocking its ready siblings, and every closure reconcile writes one summary line with failure reasons.
- [ ] On a repo with 300+ blocked issues, the stale sweep's `ready_visited` is greater than 0 whenever `ready>0`, and a hold-free ready dependant is unblocked within one pulse cycle.
- [ ] Held ready issues whose `updated_at` is unchanged are not re-read every run.
- [ ] `tests/test-pulse-stale-blocked-reconcile.sh` and the new test pass, and ShellCheck is clean.

title: bug(cleanup): capacity pass removes unproven worktrees with unmerged commits (test-worktree-capacity-recovery fails on main)
body:
## What

`.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-capacity-recovery.sh` fails on unmodified `main` (`c87f35c4`, macOS host). The async capacity pass removes fixture worktrees that the test requires to be **preserved** because they carry unmerged commits without PR proof:

- `unproven` (has a commit `unproven` that is not on `main`): expected preserved at `test-worktree-capacity-recovery.sh:134`, but it was removed
- `reused` (has a commit `reused` that is not on `main`): expected preserved at `test-worktree-capacity-recovery.sh:139`, but it was removed

Cleanup log from the fixture run:

```text
Checking for worktrees with merged branches...
Removing contained...
Removing reused...
[worktree-clean] deferred owner lease expired (lease-aged): <fixture>/squash owner_pid=<pid>
Removing squash...
Removing unproven...
Capacity pass: attempted=10 candidates=4 pr_proof_unknown=none open_query_failures=1
```

`pr_proof_unknown=none` while `open_query_failures=1` suggests that a failed open-PR query is being treated as proof that no PR exists, instead of leaving the tree unproven.

## Reproducer

```bash
# From a clean checkout of main (verified at c87f35c4 on macOS):
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-capacity-recovery.sh; echo "exit=$?"
# Observed: exit=1 after the async pass; [[ -d "$ROOT/unproven" ]] at line 134 fails.
```

## Why it matters

Capacity cleanup must never remove a worktree whose commits are not provably merged. If production behaves like the fixture, low-disk or worktree-cap pressure can delete unmerged work. That is a data-loss risk, so verify the fixture's premise before anything else.

## Likely cause (verify first)

9c7b194f86 `GH#37500: capacity cleanup uses local merge proof before GitHub reads (#37879)`, merged 2026-11-12. It is the most recent behavioural change to the capacity-pass merge proof. Check whether the local-proof path or the open-query failure handling now classifies `unproven` and `reused` as removable.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/worktree-clean-lib.sh`: capacity pass candidate selection and merge proof
- `.agents/scripts/cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh`: capacity-pressure invocation
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-capacity-recovery.sh`: existing regression fixture. Its expectations are the contract; do not weaken them.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/worktree-clean-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh`

Neither this test nor `test-codegraph-worktree-init-helper.sh` (which also fails locally on `main` with `FAIL: asynchronous init did not create the worktree index`) appears in a CI workflow. That is why the regression was not caught. Wiring them into CI is a separate, optional follow-up.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-capacity-recovery.sh` exits 0 and prints both PASS lines.
- `shellcheck` is clean on the touched scripts.
- A failed open-PR query leaves the tree preserved and counted as unproven in the `Capacity pass:` log line.

Found while verifying #38026 (PR #38113). That change does not touch this path; the failure reproduces identically on unmodified `main`.

title: full-loop-helper complete: point to finalize-receipt when no lifecycle state but a cleanup receipt exists
body:
## Observed

In an interactive full-loop on a maintained non-aidevops repo, the worktree was created with `worktree-helper.sh add` because `pre-edit-check.sh --loop-mode` hit a transient registry `database-locked` refusal. `full-loop-helper.sh start` was never run, and the PR was created with `gh-write-helper.sh pr create`. Then:

1. `full-loop-helper.sh merge 217 owner/repo` merged the PR, synced canonical and printed `LIFECYCLE_STATE=CLEANUP_DEFERRED; guarded cleanup ownership persisted outside the worktree`.
2. `full-loop-helper.sh record-deployment 217 <run> update-site-stats.yml <sha> owner/repo` recorded `release_status: published` in `~/.aidevops/state/full-loop-cleanup/<owner>_<repo>-217.json`.
3. `full-loop-helper.sh complete`, the step 9 finaliser that `scripts/commands/full-loop.md` names, failed with only: `[ERROR] Cannot complete full loop without persisted lifecycle state`.
4. `full-loop-helper.sh finalize-receipt 217 owner/repo` succeeded: `Cleanup receipt finalized for merged PR #217 (release:published)`.

## Problem

When no local lifecycle state exists but a matching cleanup receipt does, the `complete` error is a dead end. The command that works, `finalize-receipt`, appears only in `help`. `full-loop.md` step 9 names only `complete`.

## Suggested fix

- **Files:** `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-state-lifecycle-commands.sh` (the `complete` command path) and `.agents/scripts/commands/full-loop.md` (step 9 / 4.10).
- **Behaviour:** when lifecycle state is missing, look up a cleanup receipt for the current worktree with `full_loop_cleanup_receipt_for_worktree` from `full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh`. If one is found, either delegate to `finalize-receipt <PR> <REPO>` or print that exact command. If none is found, keep the current error.
- **Docs:** in `full-loop.md`, add one line saying that loops without `start` state finalize with `finalize-receipt <PR> [REPO]` after `merge`.

## Verification

1. Merge a PR with `full-loop-helper.sh merge` from a worktree that has no `start` state.
2. Run `full-loop-helper.sh complete` in that worktree. It should finalize the receipt or print the exact `finalize-receipt` command, and the receipt's `executor_completion_state` should change from `FINALIZATION_PENDING`.
3. Run `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh`. It should still pass.

title: perf(pulse): LLM supervisor starves 6–37 h — hourly drift-redeploy drains and incomplete prefetch skip it before blocker-recovery triggers; recovery queues at 75–79
body:
## What

The pulse LLM supervisor, the only owner of terminal-blocker recovery (`terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh pending`, t18514) and integration recovery, runs every 6–37 hours instead of when recovery is due. Its recovery queues grow, and every issue held as `Terminal blocker: reason=unknown owner=worker-triage` or `input_required ... the originating runner's recovery supervisor must publish one` stays `status:blocked` until the next run.

## Why

Observed 2026-11-13 on three runners at v3.39.188:

| Runner | Last supervisor attempt / success | Recent supervisor-phase outcomes | Recovery queue / decisions |
|---|---|---|---|
| macOS (20 slots) | 34.7 h / 37 h ago | 13.7 h log: **12 × `cooperative drain requested`**, 1 × budget deferral, **0 attempts** | (not sampled) |
| Linux A (32 slots) | 6 h / 6 h | last 400: **90 × `prefetch state incomplete`**, 12 × drain, 10 × not due, 25 attempts | 79 / 45 |
| Linux B (24 slots) | 1 h / 11 h | 13 × drain, 2 × not due, 9 attempts | 75 / 33 |

On one product repo, 22 dependency-free `status:blocked` issues are waiting on `reason=unknown owner=worker-triage` ("Interpret the protected dossier and record a known blocker class or repair the brief"), and several more on `input_required` with no sanitized question published. All of that is supervisor work.

### Root cause 1: every hourly drift redeploy drains the in-flight cycle, and a drained cycle skips the supervisor with no escape

`auto-update` redeploys runtime script drift between releases at most once per hour (`Script drift redeploy batched: last deploy Ns ago (< 3600s window)`). Each redeploy activates a new bundle (for example 6 activations in 4.5 h on the macOS runner) and asks the in-flight cycle to drain (#37907). `_pulse_run_supervisor_phase` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh:2135-2178`) then returns at line 2159 before any supervisor decision. Cycles on a loaded runner take 25–60 min, because the cycle joins post-dispatch housekeeping at `:2158` (`post_dispatch_housekeeping` up to 900 s). So most cycles that reach the supervisor phase are draining, and the supervisor never runs. The GH#34000 / #34524 starvation escape exists only for the prefetch branch.

### Root cause 2: incomplete prefetch skips the supervisor before the queue-driven triggers are evaluated

`:2167-2173` skips whenever `_PULSE_PREFETCH_DEGRADED=1` unless the 6 h escape (`_pulse_degraded_prefetch_supervisor_escape_due`, `pulse-dispatch-engine-supervisor.sh:57-68`) is due. The `blocker_recovery` trigger (`_should_run_llm_supervisor` step 1b, `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:829-833`) does not depend on `STATE_FILE`, because recovery entries come from the helper queue and live reads. It is still gated on a complete prefetch, which large repos rarely produce under cycle-budget pressure.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `rg -o 'Skipping LLM supervisor: [a-z ]+|LLM supervisor attempt started \(trigger=[a-z_]+' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | sort | uniq -c`, then read `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/supervisor/last_llm_attempt_epoch`.

**Actual output:** macOS runner: `12 Skipping LLM supervisor: cooperative drain requested`, no `attempt started`, and last attempt epoch 125,053 s old. Linux A: `90 Skipping LLM supervisor: prefetch state incomplete`.

**Expected:** when recovery entries are pending, the supervisor runs within roughly one redeploy interval, even across drains and degraded prefetch.

## How

1. EDIT `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh:2135-2178` (`_pulse_run_supervisor_phase`), drain branch: keep skipping by default, but when the latest supervisor attempt/success is older than `PULSE_LLM_DRAIN_ESCAPE_SECONDS` (new, default `7200`; `0` disables), run `_pulse_maybe_run_llm_supervisor` anyway. Its normal gates and failure cooldown still apply, and the lock is already released at `:2157`. Running one bundle-old supervisor is cheaper than starving it, and the drain's purpose (no new census or dispatch) is unaffected. Model the age check on `_pulse_degraded_prefetch_supervisor_escape_due`. Factor a shared `_pulse_supervisor_starved_for <seconds>` helper into `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine-supervisor.sh` and reuse it for both branches.
2. Same function, prefetch-incomplete branch: instead of skipping outright, call `_pulse_maybe_run_llm_supervisor` with `_PULSE_SUPERVISOR_STATE_INCOMPLETE=1` and a new `_PULSE_SUPERVISOR_QUEUE_TRIGGERS_ONLY=1`. In `_should_run_llm_supervisor` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:794-894`), that flag evaluates only the queue-driven step 1b (`_pulse_blocker_recovery_due`) and returns 1 for the daily-sweep and stall triggers. Do **not** probe `_pulse_blocker_recovery_due` separately first: it writes its 3 h stamp before counting (`pulse-dispatch-engine-supervisor.sh:115-116`), so a second call would see a fresh stamp and drop the trigger. The prompt already tells the model to treat state as hints and use live reads (`pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh:262-265`). Keep the 6 h escape for the snapshot-driven triggers.
3. Make starvation visible: append `last_attempt_age_s=<n>` to both `Skipping LLM supervisor:` log lines.
4. Do not change the redeploy cadence, the drain contract (#37907/#38048), or the prefetch reserve.
5. Test: NEW `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-supervisor-starvation-escape.sh`, stubbing `_pulse_drain_requested_bundle`, `_pulse_maybe_run_llm_supervisor`, `_pulse_blocker_recovery_due` and the epoch files, to assert: (a) a drain with a recent attempt skips; (b) a drain with a stale attempt runs; (c) degraded prefetch with recovery due runs with state marked incomplete; (d) degraded prefetch without recovery due and without a stale attempt skips. Also run the existing `tests/test-pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh` and `tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh` (drain coverage).

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh:2135-2178`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine-supervisor.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:794-894`
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-supervisor-starvation-escape.sh`

## Acceptance

- [ ] With hourly redeploys, a runner with pending terminal-blocker recovery entries runs the supervisor at least every `PULSE_LLM_DRAIN_ESCAPE_SECONDS`.
- [ ] Degraded prefetch no longer blocks a due `blocker_recovery` trigger.
- [ ] Skip lines report `last_attempt_age_s`.
- [ ] The new test and existing drain/lifecycle tests pass, and ShellCheck is clean.

title: Supervisor health dashboard stale: 2d2h (#23126)
body:
## Premise

The dashboard at #23126 last refreshed `2026-11-11T14:26:52Z` — **2d2h ago** (threshold: 2d0h). The `stats-wrapper.sh` scheduler is likely failing silently.

**Likely cause:** `stats.log` (last 20000 lines) retains 504 historical budget-stop records (`rc=124`) for this repo (stages: data-gather x39, body-publication x25; last logged timeout: 60s). These records are not time-bounded, so they do not confirm current scheduler health, and `rc=124` can come from either the per-repository budget or the shared aggregate deadline. Verify the scheduler is running; if recent stops are repository-budget stops, raise `STATS_HEALTH_REPO_TIMEOUT` / `STATS_HEALTH_RECOVERY_REPO_TIMEOUT` or investigate the slow stage.

## Why this matters

The supervisor health dashboard is the framework's primary single-glance health surface. When it stops refreshing, operators keep trusting green numbers that no longer reflect reality — every decision derived from "dashboard says green" becomes invalid.

## Triage

1. Inspect the stats scheduler status.

   macOS / launchd:

   ```bash
   launchctl list | grep -i aidevops-stats-wrapper
   tail -40 ~/.aidevops/logs/stats.log
   ls -la ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.aidevops.aidevops-stats-wrapper.plist
   ```

   Linux / systemd user timers:

   ```bash
   systemctl --user status aidevops-stats-wrapper.timer --no-pager
   systemctl --user status aidevops-stats-wrapper.service --no-pager
   systemctl --user list-timers --all --no-pager 'aidevops*'
   tail -40 ~/.aidevops/logs/stats.log
   ls -la ~/.config/systemd/user/aidevops-stats-wrapper.*
   ```

2. Run the refresh manually and capture the error:

   ```bash
   bash ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/stats-wrapper.sh 2>&1 | tail -40
   ```

3. Check the dashboard issue directly:

   ```bash
   gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/23126 --jq '{updated_at, body_length: (.body|length)}'
   ```

## Remediation

- **macOS missing plist:** re-run `setup.sh --non-interactive` (or `aidevops update`) with PULSE_ENABLED=true so `setup_stats_wrapper` reinstalls `com.aidevops.aidevops-stats-wrapper.plist`.
- **Linux missing or inactive systemd timer:** re-run `setup.sh --non-interactive` (or `aidevops update`) with PULSE_ENABLED=true so the Linux scheduler setup reinstalls and enables `aidevops-stats-wrapper.timer` and `aidevops-stats-wrapper.service` under `~/.config/systemd/user`.
- **`set -euo pipefail` fail:** the post-t2418 wrapper emits `HEALTH-DASHBOARD-FAIL exit=<N>` on error. Grep `stats.log` on that prefix.
- **Body size / API error:** inspect `stats.log` — look at `gh` HTTP errors and `_update_health_issue_for_repo` failures.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Root cause identified and documented on this issue.
- [ ] `gh issue view 23126 --repo marcusquinn/aidevops` shows an update within 24h of closing this alert.
- [ ] `last_refresh:` marker is present in the dashboard body.

title: fix(dispatch): has-open-pr still blocks drafts the shared checkpoint predicate rejects (ambiguous For targets, Ref-only related issues)
body:
## What

`has-open-pr` still decides "this draft is issue N's checkpoint" with its own regex, while continuation uses the shared predicate. When they disagree, the issue is blocked by dedup and rejected by continuation, and nothing ever moves it again.

- **Dedup:** `_has_open_pr_check_healthy_sibling` in `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh` (~L622–663) emits `WORKER_DRAFT_CHECKPOINT ... ordinary redispatch is blocked` for any unprotected `origin:worker`/`origin:worker-takeover` draft whose title/body has an explicit `for|refs?|close*|fix*|resolve* #N` or `GH#N`.
- **Continuation:** `_pr_checkpoint_nonclosing_draft_links_issue` / `checkpoint_draft_links` in `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-target-lib.sh` accepts a non-closing worker draft only when its `For` references (or, with no `For`, its `Ref(s)` references) name exactly issue N.

The plan in issue #37915 (step 1, "use one linkage predicate for both paths") was not implemented; its merged PR only widened the continuation regex. Issue #38111 restores `For` precedence in the shared predicate, so these two shapes remain mismatched:

1. **Ambiguous draft:** two or more `For` targets, e.g. `For #A ... For #B ... for #C`. Dedup blocks every named issue; continuation rejects all of them. Observed chain: `WORKER_DRAFT_CHECKPOINT` → `PR_CHECKPOINT_TARGET_REJECTED: reason=pr_metadata_ineligible` → `PR_CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_BLOCKED` → `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_TERMINAL_SKIPPED reason=pr_not_eligible`.
2. **Related-only reference:** the canonical checkpoint body (one standalone `For #A` plus `## Related` / `Ref #B`, per `scripts/commands/full-loop.md` "Worker checkpoint identity") links only A. Dedup still blocks B because `Ref #B` matches its body pattern. Parent issues are dispatch-blocked anyway, but a non-parent related issue stalls.

## Reproducer

On 2026-11-13, all 48 distinct `WORKER_DRAFT_CHECKPOINT` draft/issue pairs in one runner's production `pulse.log` were evaluated with both predicates. One open draft in a private managed repo carries three `For` targets and is rejected by the shared predicate (before and after #38111) while dedup blocks its issue. Every other open pair agreed after #38111.

Reproduce: collect pairs with `rg -o 'Dedup: WORKER_DRAFT_CHECKPOINT: draft PR #[0-9]+ is a durable checkpoint for issue #[0-9]+; ordinary redispatch is blocked issue=#[0-9]+ repo=[^ ]+' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`, fetch each PR with `gh pr view <pr> --repo <slug> --json state,isDraft,isCrossRepository,body,labels,closingIssuesReferences`, and run `bash -c 'source .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-target-lib.sh && _pr_checkpoint_nonclosing_draft_links_issue "$1" "$2"' _ "$json" <issue>`. Any open, unprotected, non-closing worker draft that dedup blocks but the predicate rejects is a stall.

## How

1. In `_ddpr_graphql_open_siblings` (`dispatch-dedup-pr.sh` ~L375), add `isCrossRepository`, `headRefName` and `closingIssuesReferences(first: 10) { nodes { number repository { name owner { login } } } }` to the PullRequest selection, and extend the jq shape validation. Normalise `closingIssuesReferences.nodes` into the `closingIssuesReferences` array shape the shared predicate expects.
2. In `_has_open_pr_check_healthy_sibling`, for an unprotected worker-owned draft with **no** closing references, emit `WORKER_DRAFT_CHECKPOINT` only when the shared predicate accepts it for N. Reuse `_PR_CHECKPOINT_FOR_LINK_JQ_DEFS` inside the existing jq program, which already has the PR objects, so no extra subprocess per PR is needed. Source `pr-checkpoint-target-lib.sh` the way other dispatch libs do. Drafts with closing references, protected drafts and seed drafts keep today's behaviour.
3. When the predicate rejects a worker draft that the regex matched:
   - **N is only a Ref/related target** (the draft's `For` set names other issues): the draft is context, not N's checkpoint. Do not block; log `WORKER_DRAFT_CHECKPOINT_UNLINKED issue=#N pr=#P reason=related_reference`.
   - **Ambiguous (N is one of several `For` targets):** disambiguate by dispatch identity. If `headRefName` names exactly one of the `For` targets with a numeric boundary (same convention as the `feature/auto-x-gh2905` vs `gh29050` matching in `dispatch-dedup-stale.sh`), normalise the body once through `gh-write-helper.sh pr edit`. Keep one standalone `For #<that issue>` line and move the others under `## Related` as `Ref #...`; the write wrapper already validates this shape. Then that issue continues and the others are no longer blocked. If identity cannot be proven, do not block, and log `WORKER_DRAFT_CHECKPOINT_UNLINKED reason=ambiguous`. A fresh worker costs less than a permanent stall, and the existing fuse and terminal actions retire the orphaned draft.
4. Keep the trust boundaries: same repository only, worker-origin labels only, no protective label, and a body edit only on `origin:worker`/`origin:worker-takeover` drafts. Mark the new decision point with `#aidevops:trust-boundary`.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-target-lib.sh` (only if a helper must be exported)
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-helper-has-open-pr.sh`

## Acceptance

- No path emits `WORKER_DRAFT_CHECKPOINT` for a draft that `_pr_checkpoint_nonclosing_draft_links_issue` rejects for the same issue (the issue #37915 acceptance criterion).
- A `For #A` + `## Related` / `Ref #B` worker draft blocks A, and B dispatches normally.
- An ambiguous draft whose head branch names one `For` target is normalised once, then that issue gets `PR_CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_DISPATCHED` within one cycle. Unprovable ambiguity no longer blocks.
- The GraphQL sibling query stays one request per issue; report its `rateLimit.cost` before and after in the PR.
- `shellcheck -x` is clean. `test-dispatch-dedup-helper-has-open-pr.sh`, `test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh` and `test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` pass. Add one has-open-pr case for each of the two shapes above, extending the existing inline-`For` case added by issue #37915.

title: consolidation-task: merge thread on #38119 into single spec
body:
## Consolidation target: #38119

**Parent issue:** #38119 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** perf(pulse): LLM supervisor starves 6–37 h — hourly drift-redeploy drains and incomplete prefetch skip it before blocker-recovery triggers; recovery queues at 75–79
**Parent labels:** `bug,status:available,auto-dispatch,priority:high,origin:interactive,tier:standard,consolidation-in-progress,fix-the-fixer`

> Sources are inlined below unless explicitly listed as omitted. Fetch omitted references before consolidating.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below, fetching any explicitly omitted sources first.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `### Files Scope` — the successor's write surface, one repo-relative path per line and nothing else on the line (`- EDIT: path/to/file` or `- NEW: path/to/file`). Carry over the parent's scope when present. Read-only references belong in `## How`, not here. The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.
     Preserve every wildcard scope entry verbatim from every superseded issue, including tool-generated paths such as `- NEW: todo/<area>/log/*/*/<slug>-*.jsonl`. Never invent a concrete machine, date, timestamp or filename in place of a pattern. Never change an existing `EDIT:` entry to `NEW:`.
     Check each path against the current default branch before copying its scope marker: use `git ls-files` in an up-to-date default-branch checkout or `gh api` for that branch's contents. Use `EDIT:` when the path already exists on the default branch; use `NEW:` only after confirming it is absent. A stale checkout or failed API lookup is not proof of absence.
   - **Runner prerequisites** — copy verbatim every line matching `^requires-secrets:` and its runner-prerequisite paragraph from every superseded issue. Keep all source lines (do not replace them with a summary): the runner capability gate unions comma/space-separated names across these lines. Never drop a prerequisite because this consolidation runner lacks the named secret; consolidation itself does not need those credentials.
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #38119 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`
   That marker must be a line by itself, exactly as shown (no extra text, no trailing whitespace); the dispatch gate refuses consolidated successors without it. Put any further lineage (for example "#38119 itself superseded #M") on a separate line, and add one exact marker line per additional superseded issue.

3. **Validate before filing the new consolidated issue.** Save the parent body (inlined or explicitly fetched) verbatim to a local file, plus a separate body file for each additional superseded issue. Validate the merged body against ALL sources; a failed check stops publication and parent closure until the merged body is repaired:

```bash
python3 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/consolidation-contract-validator.py \
  --parent 38119 \
  --source "<file containing the verbatim parent body>" \
  --successor "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
# Repeat --source for each additional superseded issue body.
# Repeat --parent for each additional superseded issue number.
```

The validator must pass before running the signed creation command below. It checks the exact marker line for every `--parent`, verbatim secret lines and prerequisite paragraphs, wildcard scope preservation, and EDIT-to-NEW regressions. Also run `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check` on the merged body for ordinary scope syntax validation.

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,status:available,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding all status:* labels, needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body-file "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Use the signed wrapper above rather than the raw GitHub CLI so the successor retains the managed signature and origin metadata.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` and `status:available` are also mandatory. Keep exactly one `status:*` label on the successor: `status:available` — never the parent's ownership status (`status:queued`, `status:claimed`, `status:in-progress`, `status:in-review`). Immediately before creating the successor, re-read the parent's labels; if it now carries `status:blocked`, use `status:blocked` instead, because that label records an unresolved dependency or hold rather than ownership. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch; the fill-floor enumerator also needs the available status, and the pre-claim gate holds a `status:blocked` successor until its blocker is released.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close every superseded parent and verify each handoff.** Run all five commands below for #38119, then repeat them for every additional issue passed as `--parent` in step 3, substituting that issue number in every command (including dependency repointing and the state check). Every command must succeed:

```bash
gh issue comment 38119 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 38119 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 38119 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
# Repoint open dependants' blockedBy edges and Blocked-by lines at the successor (GH#35130):
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dependency-supersession-repoint-helper.sh repoint "marcusquinn/aidevops" 38119 $NEW_NUM
# Re-read the parent (GH#37600); this must print exactly: closed not_planned
gh api "repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/38119" --jq '.state + " " + (.state_reason // "")'
```

   **Handoff verification (GH#37600):** a parent that still reads `open` keeps the `consolidated` label while the dispatch gate rejects it, so it consumes dispatch attempts every cycle. If any command above fails or refuses the write (for example a worker target-scope guard on a non-target issue), or any parent re-read is not `closed not_planned`, this task has FAILED: do not run step 5 and do not report success. Leave this consolidation task open, record the parent number, the failing command and its output in one comment here, and exit `BLOCKED`. Report a reopen observed after your close as evidence, with its event time; do not guess its cause.

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** only after every parent passed the step 4 verification, with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #38119 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- Read only explicitly omitted source references when the packet size limit prevents inlining them; otherwise do NOT re-read #38119.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Checkpoint recovery is never an unconditional requirement** (GH#35871). Name a checkpoint commit or branch as binding only after verifying it is reachable from a remote ref (`gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/commits/<sha>`), recording the full SHA and ref. Otherwise write: "Best-effort recovery: reuse if reachable; the functional spec is the source of truth; re-implement if unrecoverable." Never forbid re-implementing work that exists only as local commits on one runner.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn

## Parent body (verbatim)

## What

The pulse LLM supervisor, the only owner of terminal-blocker recovery (`terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh pending`, t18514) and integration recovery, runs every 6–37 hours instead of when recovery is due. Its recovery queues grow, and every issue held as `Terminal blocker: reason=unknown owner=worker-triage` or `input_required ... the originating runner's recovery supervisor must publish one` stays `status:blocked` until the next run.

## Why

Observed 2026-11-13 on three runners at v3.39.188:

| Runner | Last supervisor attempt / success | Recent supervisor-phase outcomes | Recovery queue / decisions |
|---|---|---|---|
| macOS (20 slots) | 34.7 h / 37 h ago | 13.7 h log: **12 × `cooperative drain requested`**, 1 × budget deferral, **0 attempts** | (not sampled) |
| Linux A (32 slots) | 6 h / 6 h | last 400: **90 × `prefetch state incomplete`**, 12 × drain, 10 × not due, 25 attempts | 79 / 45 |
| Linux B (24 slots) | 1 h / 11 h | 13 × drain, 2 × not due, 9 attempts | 75 / 33 |

On one product repo, 22 dependency-free `status:blocked` issues are waiting on `reason=unknown owner=worker-triage` ("Interpret the protected dossier and record a known blocker class or repair the brief"), and several more on `input_required` with no sanitized question published. All of that is supervisor work.

### Root cause 1: every hourly drift redeploy drains the in-flight cycle, and a drained cycle skips the supervisor with no escape

`auto-update` redeploys runtime script drift between releases at most once per hour (`Script drift redeploy batched: last deploy Ns ago (< 3600s window)`). Each redeploy activates a new bundle (for example 6 activations in 4.5 h on the macOS runner) and asks the in-flight cycle to drain (#37907). `_pulse_run_supervisor_phase` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh:2135-2178`) then returns at line 2159 before any supervisor decision. Cycles on a loaded runner take 25–60 min, because the cycle joins post-dispatch housekeeping at `:2158` (`post_dispatch_housekeeping` up to 900 s). So most cycles that reach the supervisor phase are draining, and the supervisor never runs. The GH#34000 / #34524 starvation escape exists only for the prefetch branch.

### Root cause 2: incomplete prefetch skips the supervisor before the queue-driven triggers are evaluated

`:2167-2173` skips whenever `_PULSE_PREFETCH_DEGRADED=1` unless the 6 h escape (`_pulse_degraded_prefetch_supervisor_escape_due`, `pulse-dispatch-engine-supervisor.sh:57-68`) is due. The `blocker_recovery` trigger (`_should_run_llm_supervisor` step 1b, `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:829-833`) does not depend on `STATE_FILE`, because recovery entries come from the helper queue and live reads. It is still gated on a complete prefetch, which large repos rarely produce under cycle-budget pressure.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `rg -o 'Skipping LLM supervisor: [a-z ]+|LLM supervisor attempt started \(trigger=[a-z_]+' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | sort | uniq -c`, then read `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/supervisor/last_llm_attempt_epoch`.

**Actual output:** macOS runner: `12 Skipping LLM supervisor: cooperative drain requested`, no `attempt started`, and last attempt epoch 125,053 s old. Linux A: `90 Skipping LLM supervisor: prefetch state incomplete`.

**Expected:** when recovery entries are pending, the supervisor runs within roughly one redeploy interval, even across drains and degraded prefetch.

## How

1. EDIT `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh:2135-2178` (`_pulse_run_supervisor_phase`), drain branch: keep skipping by default, but when the latest supervisor attempt/success is older than `PULSE_LLM_DRAIN_ESCAPE_SECONDS` (new, default `7200`; `0` disables), run `_pulse_maybe_run_llm_supervisor` anyway. Its normal gates and failure cooldown still apply, and the lock is already released at `:2157`. Running one bundle-old supervisor is cheaper than starving it, and the drain's purpose (no new census or dispatch) is unaffected. Model the age check on `_pulse_degraded_prefetch_supervisor_escape_due`. Factor a shared `_pulse_supervisor_starved_for <seconds>` helper into `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine-supervisor.sh` and reuse it for both branches.
2. Same function, prefetch-incomplete branch: instead of skipping outright, call `_pulse_maybe_run_llm_supervisor` with `_PULSE_SUPERVISOR_STATE_INCOMPLETE=1` and a new `_PULSE_SUPERVISOR_QUEUE_TRIGGERS_ONLY=1`. In `_should_run_llm_supervisor` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:794-894`), that flag evaluates only the queue-driven step 1b (`_pulse_blocker_recovery_due`) and returns 1 for the daily-sweep and stall triggers. Do **not** probe `_pulse_blocker_recovery_due` separately first: it writes its 3 h stamp before counting (`pulse-dispatch-engine-supervisor.sh:115-116`), so a second call would see a fresh stamp and drop the trigger. The prompt already tells the model to treat state as hints and use live reads (`pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh:262-265`). Keep the 6 h escape for the snapshot-driven triggers.
3. Make starvation visible: append `last_attempt_age_s=<n>` to both `Skipping LLM supervisor:` log lines.
4. Do not change the redeploy cadence, the drain contract (#37907/#38048), or the prefetch reserve.
5. Test: NEW `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-supervisor-starvation-escape.sh`, stubbing `_pulse_drain_requested_bundle`, `_pulse_maybe_run_llm_supervisor`, `_pulse_blocker_recovery_due` and the epoch files, to assert: (a) a drain with a recent attempt skips; (b) a drain with a stale attempt runs; (c) degraded prefetch with recovery due runs with state marked incomplete; (d) degraded prefetch without recovery due and without a stale attempt skips. Also run the existing `tests/test-pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh` and `tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh` (drain coverage).

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh:2135-2178`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine-supervisor.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:794-894`
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-supervisor-starvation-escape.sh`

## Acceptance

- [ ] With hourly redeploys, a runner with pending terminal-blocker recovery entries runs the supervisor at least every `PULSE_LLM_DRAIN_ESCAPE_SECONDS`.
- [ ] Degraded prefetch no longer blocks a due `blocker_recovery` trigger.
- [ ] Skip lines report `last_attempt_age_s`.
- [ ] The new test and existing drain/lifecycle tests pass, and ShellCheck is clean.

- **Brief-owner actionable from public evidence (13):** 4 transient conditions that had since cleared (a rate limit, a merged checkpoint, a deploy wait), 2 ended with work remaining and no hold, 1 had its dependency resolved, 1 needed policy already in the reference docs applied, 1 needed a sibling phase reopened, 1 had a maintainer-input request answerable under delegated authority, and 3 got bounded retries. That is model compliance with an existing contract (`headless-runtime-contract.sh`), not a parser defect. It is noted here because it inflates the `unknown` queue the supervisor must drain.

Implication for acceptance: when the supervisor phase is skipped repeatedly, an `unknown` hold with no public evidence never gets classified, because no other runner can read its dossier. title: test(dispatch): page-bounds guard rejects bounded commit-read GraphQL calls after GH#35888
body:
## What

`.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-graphql-page-bounds.sh` fails on `main` with two `hot-path GraphQL calls use bounded adapters` failures. Both flagged lines are in `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh` and already use the bounded adapter:

```
_ddpr_bounded_gh_read _ddpr_commit_read_attempt "$repo_slug" gh api graphql -f owner="$owner" -f name="$repo" ...
```

The guard regex (~line 208) only accepts `_<prefix>_gh_(read|call) [read|write] gh api graphql` with nothing between the adapter and `gh`. The commit-permission wrapper `_ddpr_commit_read_attempt "$repo_slug"`, added by GH#35888 (#35888, commit 2526cfc4b6), sits between them, so the guard reports bounded calls as unbounded. The production code is correct; the test guard drifted.

## Why

A suite that is always red on `main` hides real regressions. Any future unbounded GraphQL call added to a guarded hot-path file would be lost among these two known failures.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-graphql-page-bounds.sh` (from a current `main` checkout; observed 2026-11-13 on `4abe997e4a`)

**Actual output:**

```
FAIL hot-path GraphQL calls use bounded adapters: .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh: 		_ddpr_bounded_gh_read _ddpr_commit_read_attempt "$repo_slug" gh api graphql -f owner="$owner" -f name="$repo" \
FAIL hot-path GraphQL calls use bounded adapters: .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh: 		_ddpr_bounded_gh_read _ddpr_commit_read_attempt "$repo_slug" gh api graphql -f owner="$owner" -f name="$repo" -f query='
Ran 10 tests, 2 failed.
```

**Expected output:** `Ran 10 tests, 0 failed.`

## How

1. In `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-graphql-page-bounds.sh` (~L208), widen the accepted shape to allow exactly one optional `_<prefix>_attempt "$<var>"` wrapper between the adapter and `gh api graphql`, for example by inserting `([[:space:]]+_[a-z0-9_]+_attempt[[:space:]]+"\$[a-z_]+")?` before `[[:space:]]+gh[[:space:]]+api[[:space:]]+graphql`.
2. Keep the guard strict otherwise: a bare `gh api graphql`, or one wrapped only by a non-adapter function, must still fail.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-graphql-page-bounds.sh`

## Acceptance

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-graphql-page-bounds.sh` passes 10/10 on main.
- Temporarily changing one guarded call to a bare `gh api graphql` still makes the guard fail (verify locally, do not commit).

title: fix(checkpoints): per-PR fuse halts productive drafts that advance the head every release
body:
## Problem

Productive worker draft checkpoints are stopped by the per-PR continuation fuse, even when they advance the PR head with substantive commits on every release. `AIDEVOPS_PCC_MAX_PR_RELEASES` (default 6) counts every eligible release since the PR was created, whether or not that release made progress. When the fuse trips, a draft that is still delivering progress waits for one of two things:

- a maintainer posts a head-bound `CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_APPROVED` line for every new head, or
- the GH#37779 bounded terminal action runs, which happens at least `AIDEVOPS_PCC_TERMINAL_ACTION_SECONDS` (12h) after the newer of the attention record and the release. A trusted approval that is still unexpired postpones it again.

Long-archive enrichment work is legitimately multi-session. One release publishes one edition, so these drafts hit the fuse routinely and sit idle for 12h or more between sessions. The fuse exists to stop loops that make no progress (the same head, repeated stalls). Here it is stopping progress instead.

## Evidence (managed private repo, 2026-11-13)

- Draft PR #22810 (issue #22713) had 7 releases and 7 substantive commits. The head advanced on every release: September results spec, then publication, then August preparation, then August publication, and so on. Each continuation published one more edition to beta and passed its verification check. Pulse logged `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_REARM_BLOCKED ... head=5a52bebec6... reason=per_pr_fuse stalls=7 pr_releases=7` on every runner, and the issue was held with `stale_draft_checkpoint` / `worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked`. The source still lists more than 200 past monthly editions.
- The same fuse state appeared on three more productive drafts with advancing heads: #21779 (pr_releases=6), #21925 and #21972 (pr_releases=7). Each one needed a manual head-bound approval generated with `pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh approval-template` (posted 2026-11-13 around 17:55Z).
- Across both Linux runners' pulse logs, no `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_TERMINAL_*` line appeared for these PRs. The terminal action was not yet due, because each new release or approval reset its anchor. Each fused head therefore stayed idle until a person acted.

## Proposed fix (the worker decides the minimal design)

- Count only **non-progress** releases toward the per-PR fuse. A release counts as progress when it closes an attempt whose PR head advanced past the attempt's starting head by at least one new, non-merge commit authored on the PR branch. Base-integration merge commits alone do not count as progress. The existing per-head `stalls` counter already handles releases at an unchanged head.
- Keep a hard upper bound so a slowly advancing loop still stops. One option is a separate, larger total-release ceiling (for example `AIDEVOPS_PCC_MAX_PR_PROGRESS_RELEASES`, default 30) that posts the existing fuse attention record once.
- Report the counts the decision used: `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_REARM_BLOCKED ... progress_releases=<n> nonprogress_releases=<n>`. Then `rg` can tell a stuck fuse from a productive one.
- Keep everything else unchanged: exact-head fencing, approval binding, the 12h/fleet re-arm for unchanged heads, and the GH#37779 terminal action for drafts that are truly stalled.

### Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` — `_pcc_dispatch_stalled` (around line 1776; reads `pr_releases` from `_pcc_stall_release_evidence`), `_pcc_stalled_rearm_or_block` (around 1612), `_pcc_rearm_block_reason` (around 1587), and the `_PCC_MAX_PR_RELEASES` default (line 70).
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-target-lib.sh` or wherever `_pcc_stall_release_evidence` computes `pr_releases`. Derive per-release head advance from the release's attempt and the PR commit dates already fetched in `pr_json.commits`.
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md` — the "Non-blocked releases with an open draft" fuse paragraph (around lines 96-100).
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh` — add a fixture where 7 releases each advance the head (expect re-arm or continuation, not `per_pr_fuse`) and a fixture where 6 releases do not advance it (expect `per_pr_fuse`, as now).

Reference pattern: the per-head `stalls` computation and `_pcc_runner_tried_head` already compare release timing against `head_date`. Reuse that comparison instead of fetching extra data.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-target-lib.sh`
- `.agents/reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh`

### Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh` passes, including the two new fixtures.
- `shellcheck` reports zero violations on the touched scripts.
- Runtime, after deploy: for a draft whose head advances on every release, `rg 'STALLED_CHECKPOINT_REARM_BLOCKED.*per_pr_fuse' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` should not show that PR before the progress ceiling. Drafts with an unchanged head still show `per_pr_fuse` after 6 non-progress releases.

### Safety-stop recovery

The fuse remains a pause, not completion. Objective: productive checkpoints keep running without manual approvals, and loops that make no progress still stop. Resume condition: a new advancing head, a maintainer approval, or the GH#37779 terminal action.

Related: #37779 (terminal action), #37514 (fleet re-arm), #37926 (progress push path), #38103 (idle drafts after a failed launch). None of these changes how the fuse counts releases.

title: gh-audit: attribute protected-label-guard edits to the logical caller so trusted-author NMR normalization stays verified
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `gh audit anomaly scanner protected_label_removed` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 1 commit (176c16e5e7, GH#37906) / 0 open PRs touch target files in last 48h; it adds a separate permission-grant flag and does not touch caller attribution
- [x] File refs verified: 7 refs checked, all present at HEAD
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — the attribution approach is decided below; the existing live verification stays the trust authority
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — the fix is small and the worker must exercise the real call stack

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-13
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (maintainer review of GH audit alerts #38066, #38068, #38069)
- **Conversation context:** Three runners filed audit alerts at the same time after v3.39.187 (GH#37904) started scanning rotated logs. Alert #38066 shows the trusted-author `needs-maintainer-review` normalization is no longer recognised as an expected transition.

## What

Audit records for `gh_issue_edit_safe` calls made through `protected-label-guard.sh` must name the logical caller (for example `_nmr_edit_issue_labels` in `pulse-nmr-approval.sh`), not the guard's internal `_protected_label_raw_edit`. A verified trusted-author NMR normalization must again get `flags.trusted_author_nmr_verified == "v1-current-state"` and must not raise a GH audit anomaly alert.

## Why

GH#35793 (commit 7560fa00d2, 2026-10-28) routed `_nmr_edit_issue_labels` through `protected_label_edit` → `_protected_label_raw_edit` → `gh_issue_edit_safe`. The audit recorder takes `BASH_SOURCE[1]`/`FUNCNAME[1]`, so it now records `caller_function=_protected_label_raw_edit` and `caller_script=.../protected-label-guard.sh`. As a result:

- `_gh_audit_record_op` (`.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh:332-337`) never matches `_nmr_edit_issue_labels`, so the trusted-author verification never runs and no flag is written.
- `expected_trusted_author_nmr_transition` in `.agents/scripts/gh-audit-anomaly-filter.jq:77-91` can never match. Every trusted-author normalization after 2026-10-28 is reported as an anomaly.
- The tests did not catch this: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-audit-anomaly-expected-transitions.sh:269-293` calls `_gh_audit_record_op` with a hard-coded caller name instead of using the real call stack.

Evidence: #38066 reports `issue_edit #37890 protected_label_removed:needs-maintainer-review` with caller `_protected_label_raw_edit`. The issue timeline shows its write-authorized author removing NMR from their own issue, which is the case this normalization exists for.

## Reproducer

1. Observed in production: alert #38066 (scan at 2026-11-13T09:01:28Z) lists `2026-11-12T17:13:15Z issue_edit marcusquinn/aidevops #37890 protected_label_removed:needs-maintainer-review` with caller `_protected_label_raw_edit`.
2. GitHub confirms the expected case: `gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/collaborators/vladimirdulov/permission --jq .permission` returns `write`, and the issue #37890 timeline shows `github-actions[bot]` adding `needs-maintainer-review` at 11:23:21Z and the issue author removing it at 17:13:12Z.
3. Code path: `.agents/scripts/pulse-nmr-approval.sh:1559-1568` (`_nmr_edit_issue_labels` → `protected_label_edit`) → `.agents/scripts/protected-label-guard.sh:21-30` (`_protected_label_raw_edit` → `gh_issue_edit_safe`) → `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh:655-656`, which records `FUNCNAME[1]` = `_protected_label_raw_edit`. The check at `:332` then never matches.
4. Introduced by `git log -S"protected_label_edit" -- .agents/scripts/pulse-nmr-approval.sh` → 7560fa00d2 (GH#35793, 2026-10-28).

**Symptom command:** `rg -n '"\$\{FUNCNAME\[1\]:-\}"' .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh; rg -n 'gh_issue_edit_safe' .agents/scripts/protected-label-guard.sh`

**Actual output:** six recorder call sites (`:656`, `:836`, `:862`, `:882`, `:902`, `:922`) take `FUNCNAME[1]`, and `protected-label-guard.sh:25` calls `gh_issue_edit_safe` from `_protected_label_raw_edit`. As a result, alert #38066 records caller `_protected_label_raw_edit` with no `trusted_author_nmr_verified` flag.

**Expected output:** caller `_nmr_edit_issue_labels` (`pulse-nmr-approval.sh`) with `flags.trusted_author_nmr_verified == "v1-current-state"`, and no alert.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** a known frame-attribution pattern inside an already-decided trust boundary. The worker writes a stack walk and a real-stack test case, and the live re-verification remains authoritative.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh:656,836,862,882,902,922` — replace the six direct `"${BASH_SOURCE[1]:-}" "${FUNCNAME[1]:-}" "${BASH_LINENO[0]:-0}"` recorder arguments with a shared caller-frame helper that skips frames whose source is `protected-label-guard.sh`
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-audit-anomaly-expected-transitions.sh` — add one case that goes through the real stack: a function named `_nmr_edit_issue_labels`, defined in a file whose path ends in `/agents/scripts/pulse-nmr-approval.sh`, calls `protected_label_edit`; with `gh` stubbed, assert that the recorded caller and flag are correct

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `rg -n "protected_label_edit" .agents/scripts -g '!tests/**'` finds `pulse-nmr-approval.sh:1565`, `pulse-issue-reconcile-actions.sh:375,472`, `dispatch-single-issue-policy.sh:164`, and `full-loop-helper-state-lifecycle.sh:150`. All of them currently record the guard frame. Only the NMR normalization has a dependent exemption today. The others gain accurate attribution and keep their alert behaviour.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `_protected_label_raw_edit` (`.agents/scripts/protected-label-guard.sh:21-30`) is the only guard writer; when `gh_issue_edit_safe` is not defined it falls back to raw `gh issue edit`, which is not audited (unchanged).
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-audit-anomaly-expected-transitions.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-protected-label-guard.sh`.
- **Schemas/config:** the audit NDJSON fields `caller_script`, `caller_function`, and `caller_line` keep their names and types (`.agents/reference/gh-audit-log.md` "Schema Reference").
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** deployed copies under `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/` update on `setup.sh`/`aidevops update`; no generated files.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because `gh-audit.log` lines are immutable and the schema in `.agents/reference/gh-audit-log.md` is unchanged. Alerts already filed (#38066) are closed by review, not rewritten.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** reverting `_gh_audit_caller_frame` in `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh` restores the previous attribution; log format is unchanged.

### Implementation Steps

1. Add `_gh_audit_caller_frame` to `shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh`. It walks `FUNCNAME`/`BASH_SOURCE`/`BASH_LINENO` from the recorder's caller upward and returns the first frame whose `BASH_SOURCE` does not end in `/protected-label-guard.sh`. It prints script, function, and line, and with no guard frame it falls back to the current index-1 behaviour. Keep it Bash 3.2 compatible and end it with an explicit `return 0`.
2. Use the helper at all six recorder call sites. The line number must belong to the selected frame (`BASH_LINENO[i-1]` for frame `i`).
3. Leave the verification at `:332-337` unchanged. Attribution only selects the candidate. `_gh_audit_verify_trusted_author_nmr_transition` stays the authority.
4. Add the real-stack test case and a negative case: a function with a different name in the guard path must not acquire the flag.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** none. This is pure in-process stack inspection, and record appends are unchanged.
- **Migration/rollback:** none. The log schema is unchanged, so the revert is a single commit.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** older runners keep logging the guard frame until they update. The filter still fails closed for them, which is today's behaviour.
- **Idempotency/retry:** the attribution is deterministic for a given stack.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** if the stack walk finds nothing, it falls back to index 1 and never emits an empty caller.
- **Trust boundary:** skipping frames must match exactly the guard's absolute script suffix, never a function name alone. Otherwise any script could hide behind a function called `_protected_label_raw_edit`. Mark the helper `#aidevops:trust-boundary`.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-audit-anomaly-expected-transitions.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-protected-label-guard.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-audit-anomaly-expected-transitions.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** the first test proves attribution and flag behaviour for the real stack, plus the negative case. The guard test proves the guard behaviour is unchanged. ShellCheck and the changed-file lint cover the edited files.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required. The change touches one shared wrapper file, and its existing test suite covers it.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-audit-anomaly-expected-transitions.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] When a trusted-author NMR removal goes through `_nmr_edit_issue_labels` → `protected_label_edit`, the record has `caller_function == "_nmr_edit_issue_labels"`, a `caller_script` ending in `/pulse-nmr-approval.sh`, and `flags.trusted_author_nmr_verified == "v1-current-state"`, and the scanner does not report it.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-audit-anomaly-expected-transitions.sh"
  ```

- [ ] Negative: an external-author NMR removal, a read-only actor, or a non-framework script that defines a function named like the guard's still gets `flags == {}` and is still reported.
- [ ] ShellCheck reports zero violations on the changed files.

## Context & Decisions

- Chosen: skip guard frames in the recorder rather than adding a caller-override variable to the guard. The override approach would let any caller claim another identity.
- Non-goal: reclassifying generic `gh-write-helper.sh` status-label edits. That is a separate design decision with its own issue.
