title: gh-audit: separate verified lifecycle status transitions from trust-gate anomalies to cut alert noise
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `gh audit anomaly scanner protected_label_removed` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 2 commits (52d343295c GH#37904, 176c16e5e7 GH#37906) / 0 open PRs touch target files in last 48h. Neither classifies lifecycle status edits.
- [x] File refs verified: 6 refs checked, all present at HEAD
- [x] Tier: `tier:thinking` — this changes what the audit trust boundary reports, and the policy choice is still open
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — the policy decision comes before any code

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-13
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (maintainer review of GH audit alerts #38066, #38068, #38069)
- **Conversation context:** After v3.39.187 (GH#37904) the scanner caught up on rotated logs, and one runner reported 117 anomalies from about 2.5 months of backlog. Most of them were normal lifecycle status changes, not trust-gate removals.

## What

Decide which protected-label removals count as security anomalies and which are expected lifecycle transitions, then implement that decision. When finished, a GH audit alert should list only changes a maintainer actually needs to review: trust-gate removals (`needs-maintainer-review`, `needs-maintainer-permissions`, `no-auto-dispatch`, `origin:interactive`), content wipes, and unverified status removals. Status transitions made through sanctioned, attributable paths should no longer produce alerts.

## Why

Evidence comes from the backlog on one runner (2026-08-26 to 2026-11-13). The filter (`.agents/scripts/gh-audit-anomaly-filter.jq`) let through 142 suspicious entries. About 100 of them are `status:*` lifecycle swaps made through `gh-write-helper.sh issue edit` (caller `main`, and since 2026-11-11 `_issue_edit_signed`):

| Count | Transition |
|---|---|
| 17 | `status:in-review` → `status:done` |
| 13 | `status:in-progress` → `status:in-review` |
| 11 | `status:in-progress` → `status:blocked` |
| 10 | `status:in-review` → `status:available` |
| 7 | `status:claimed` → `status:in-review` |
| 6 | `status:in-progress` → `status:available` |

Ad-hoc scripts in agent workspaces (`.edit-issue-NNNNN.sh`, `finalize-*-pr.sh`, `update-*-pr.sh`, `issue-edit.sh`) add a few more. Because of this noise, real trust-gate removals are hard to spot. In this backlog, external-author NMR removals by raw edit at issue close were correctly reverted by the label-protection Action, but they were buried among routine entries. The sanctioned `gh-write-helper.sh issue status` path (`set_issue_status`, `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-status.sh:793`) left no audit records with that caller on this runner since 2026-11-11. That needs confirming.

## Reproducer

1. Production alert #38069 (117 entries): most rows are `status:*` removals with caller `main` (from `gh-write-helper.sh`).
2. On any runner, group the suspicious entries that pass the filter by caller and transition:
   `jq -c --arg nmr needs-maintainer-review --arg permission needs-maintainer-permissions --arg issue_edit issue_edit --arg approval_script approval-helper.sh --arg permission_script worker-permission-helper.sh --arg nmr_script pulse-nmr-approval.sh --arg full_loop_commit_script full-loop-helper-commit.sh --arg full_loop_script full-loop-helper.sh -f .agents/scripts/gh-audit-anomaly-filter.jq ~/.aidevops/logs/gh-audit.log | jq -sc 'group_by([(.caller_script|split("/")|last), .caller_function, (.delta.labels_removed|tostring), (.delta.labels_added|tostring)]) | map({n:length, script:(.[0].caller_script|split("/")|last), fn:.[0].caller_function, removed:.[0].delta.labels_removed, added:.[0].delta.labels_added}) | sort_by(-.n)'`
3. Expected today: the largest groups are `gh-write-helper.sh` `main`/`_issue_edit_signed` lifecycle swaps.

**Symptom command:** the step 2 grouping over this runner's rotated logs for 2026-08-26 to 2026-11-13 (`gh-audit.20260826T011108Z.log`, `gh-audit.20260929T084844Z.log`, `gh-audit.20261111T043333Z.log`, `gh-audit.log`).

**Actual output:** 142 entries pass the filter. The top groups are `gh-write-helper.sh main` `status:in-review→status:done` (15), `status:in-progress→status:in-review` (13), `status:in-progress→status:blocked` (11), `status:in-review→status:available` (10), and `status:claimed→status:in-review` (7), plus `_issue_edit_signed` lifecycle swaps from 2026-11-11 onward.

**Expected output:** sanctioned lifecycle swaps with verified provenance stay out of alert-grade output, while trust-gate removals stay in it.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking`

**Tier rationale:** this changes which mutations the security audit reports, and the policy between severity tiers, provenance flags, and steering edits to sanctioned subcommands is not decided yet.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/gh-audit-log-helper.sh:72-80` — `GH_AUDIT_PROTECTED_LABELS` treats lifecycle `status:*` removals the same as trust-gate removals
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/gh-audit-anomaly-filter.jq` — add expected-transition rules or a severity split for the chosen policy
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh:314-360` — `_gh_audit_record_op` provenance flags for any newly sanctioned transition
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh:204-260` — generic `issue edit`; decide whether pure core-status swaps should be redirected to `issue status`
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh` — report layout if alerts are split into alert and digest sections
- `EDIT: .agents/reference/gh-audit-log.md` — "Anomaly Taxonomy" documents the decision

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh scan` (daily routine `r-gh-audit-scan`) reads the log through `gh-audit-anomaly-filter.jq`; `.agents/reference/gh-audit-log.md` "Forensics Workflow" is the human reader.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `gh_issue_edit_safe` and five other recorders in `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh` (lines 656, 836, 862, 882, 902, 922); `set_issue_status` in `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-status.sh:793` (check whether it is audited).
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-audit-anomaly-expected-transitions.sh` encodes each expected-transition rule.
- **Schemas/config:** the audit NDJSON `flags` object (`.agents/reference/gh-audit-log.md` "Schema Reference"); any new flag needs a versioned value like the existing `v1-current-state`.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** deployed copies under `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/` update via `setup.sh`; no generated artefacts.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because historical log lines are immutable. New rules apply only to records with new flags, and legacy records keep failing closed.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the filter rules in `.agents/scripts/gh-audit-anomaly-filter.jq` to restore today's reporting.

### Implementation Steps

1. Decide the policy and record it in `.agents/reference/gh-audit-log.md`. Options to weigh:
   a. Keep `status:*` protected, but add verified-provenance flags for sanctioned transitions (`issue status`, review-handoff, close-as-done after a merged PR) in the same way as the existing `pr_review_handoff_verified`.
   b. Split the report into "Trust-gate anomalies" (an alert issue) and "Lifecycle removals without verified provenance" (a digest section or a count only).
   c. Make generic `issue edit` refuse pure core-status swaps and point callers to `issue status`, so lifecycle changes all go through one attributable path.
   Claim theft (one runner removing another's `status:in-progress`/`status:claimed`) is the threat that status protection covers. Any option must keep detecting it.
2. Implement the chosen option and give each new exemption both a positive and a negative test case in the existing transitions test.
3. Run a dry-run scan over a representative backlog (`gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh scan --all --dry-run`) and record the before/after counts in the PR.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** none added. Record appends and the filter run are unchanged.
- **Migration/rollback:** the change is rule-only, so a revert restores current reporting.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** older runners emit records without new flags, and those must keep failing closed (reported).
- **Idempotency/retry:** the filter is a pure function over records, so rescans give the same output.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** if provenance verification fails, the record is still reported (fail closed), as with `approval_verified`.
- **Trust boundary:** never exempt a removal on caller name alone. Exemptions need live state verification, and trust-gate labels stay alert-grade.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-audit-anomaly-expected-transitions.sh
.agents/scripts/gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh scan --all --dry-run
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** the transitions test proves each new rule and its negative case. The dry-run scan shows the reduction in reported noise and that trust-gate entries are still reported. The changed-file lint covers the edited shell and jq.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required. The change is limited to audit scripts that already have a focused test.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/gh-audit-log-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/gh-audit-anomaly-filter.jq`
- `.agents/scripts/gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-audit-anomaly-expected-transitions.sh`
- `.agents/reference/gh-audit-log.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Status transitions made through the sanctioned path, with verified provenance, no longer appear as alert-grade anomalies. A dry-run scan of a backlog like the one above reports at least 70% fewer alert entries.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-audit-anomaly-expected-transitions.sh"
  ```

- [ ] Negative: removing `needs-maintainer-review`, `needs-maintainer-permissions`, `no-auto-dispatch`, or `origin:interactive` without verified provenance is still alert-grade, and a `status:in-progress` removal by a different runner without verified provenance is still reported.
- [ ] `.agents/reference/gh-audit-log.md` "Anomaly Taxonomy" documents the chosen policy.

## Context & Decisions

- Related: #38134 (guard-frame caller attribution, `_protected_label_raw_edit`) fixes the trusted-author NMR false positive. This issue covers lifecycle noise only.
- Prior art: GH#37906 (permission-grant flag), GH#35881 (timeline-proven self-reversals), `_issue_review_handoff` (`v2-owned-pr-current-state`).

title: perf(gh): expire orphaned single-flight lease.reclaim markers (10 s waits on ~3.8k gh calls/day)
body:
## What

`_ghrs_reclaim_lease` (`.agents/scripts/shared-gh-request-state.sh`) uses a `lease.reclaim` directory as a short mutex but never expires it. If a process is killed between `mkdir lease.reclaim` and `rmdir lease.reclaim` (gh timeouts and worker kills make this routine), every later reclaim fails, so every caller of that single-flight key spins for the full `AIDEVOPS_GH_SINGLEFLIGHT_WAIT_SECONDS` (10 s), records `timeout`, then fetches directly anyway.

## Reproducer

Maintainer host, 2026-11-13.

**Symptom command:** `rg gh_request_singleflight ~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls.log | awk -F'\t' '$1 >= 1794509000 {n[$6]++} END {for (k in n) print n[k], k}'`

**Actual output:** `3834 timeout`, `2437 leader`, `2371 leader-success`, `36 leader-failure`, `20 takeover`, `5 follower-success` — about 3.8k ten-second waits per day (~10.6 h of blocked wall-clock across pulse dedup/claim and worker `gh` calls).

- The production rate-limit projection key (`gh_request_state_request_key global rate-limit resources/v1 all default`) had an empty `lease/` (no `owner.json`) and an empty `lease.reclaim/`, both with mtime 2026-11-03 23:08 — 10 days stale.
- Profiling one wrapped `gh issue view`: 10.51 s of 11.28 s spent at `shared-gh-wrappers-rest-fallback.sh:360` (`gh_request_state_rate_json normal 20 _rest_rate_limit_json_fetch`), i.e. `_rest_should_fallback` waiting on the leaked lease.
- Isolated repro (same library, fresh state dir, 6 concurrent callers): all complete in < 1 s, so the waiting comes from the leaked state, not normal contention.
- Runtime remediation already applied on the maintainer host (empty dirs removed with `rmdir`); this issue is the durable code fix.

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-request-state.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-request-singleflight.sh`

- **File:** `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-request-state.sh` — `_ghrs_reclaim_lease` (around line 311).
- When `mkdir "$reclaim_dir"` fails, treat a reclaim marker whose mtime is older than a short grace (new knob `AIDEVOPS_GH_SINGLEFLIGHT_RECLAIM_GRACE_SECONDS`, default 10 s; the critical section is a few file operations) as orphaned: `rmdir` it and retry `mkdir` once. Reuse `_file_mtime_epoch` exactly as `_ghrs_owner_is_stale` does for orphan leases. Create the marker with `umask 077` like the lease.
- Keep fail-safe semantics: any error returns 1 (caller keeps waiting/times out), never a second leader by force.
- **Test:** extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-request-singleflight.sh` with one case: pre-create an empty `lease/` and a back-dated `lease.reclaim/`, then assert `gh_request_state_singleflight_begin` returns role `leader` well under the wait timeout.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-request-singleflight.sh` passes, including the new leaked-marker case.
- `shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/shared-gh-request-state.sh` clean.
- After deploy: the `timeout` share of `gh_request_singleflight` decisions in `~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls.log` falls from ~60% to near zero.

title: chore(gh): garbage-collect stale github-request-state request dirs and temp files
body:
## What

Nothing prunes the GitHub request-coordination state under `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/work/github-request-state/requests/`. Every distinct single-flight key creates a directory that is never removed, and killed processes leave `.outcome.*` / `.owner.*` temp files and ownerless `lease/` dirs behind. Found while diagnosing GH#38138 (leaked `lease.reclaim` on the shared rate-limit key).

## Reproducer

Maintainer host, 2026-11-13.

**Symptom command:** `fd -H -t d -d 1 --changed-before 7d . ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/work/github-request-state/requests | wc -l`

**Actual output:** `34157` (of 41,711 request dirs; 81 MB total). 147 ownerless `lease/` dirs (oldest 2026-11-11), 10 orphaned zero-byte `.outcome.*` temp files (oldest 2026-09-12).

No measured throughput impact yet (GH#38138 was the throughput defect); this is bounded-growth hygiene so the state root cannot grow without limit on long-lived runners.

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-request-state.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-request-singleflight.sh`

- Add `gh_request_state_gc` to `shared-gh-request-state.sh`: remove request dirs whose mtime and every entry mtime are older than `AIDEVOPS_GH_REQUEST_STATE_GC_DAYS` (default 7) **and** that hold no live lease (no `lease/`, or a lease that `_ghrs_owner_is_stale` judges stale); remove `.outcome.*` / `.owner.*` temp files older than 1 hour. Use `_file_mtime_epoch` (portable-stat.sh), never GNU-only `find -mtime` flags; never follow symlinks; only operate under `_ghrs_base_dir`.
- Rate-limit it with a stamp file (at most once per 24 h) and call it from `_preflight_cleanup_and_ledger` in `pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh` via `run_stage_with_timeout` (pattern: the `cleanup_stale_session_locks` guarded call at that function), so the pulse amortises it and it can never block dispatch.
- Test: one case in `test-gh-request-singleflight.sh` — a back-dated idle request dir is removed; a back-dated dir with a live lease (current shell PID, future `expires_at`) and a fresh dir are kept.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-request-singleflight.sh` passes.
- `shellcheck -x` clean on changed scripts; `/bin/bash -n` parses (Bash 3.2).
- After deploy: the `fd ... --changed-before 7d` count above drops to near zero within a day, and pulse stage timings show the GC stage well under `PRE_RUN_STAGE_TIMEOUT`.

title: perf(dispatch): cache layer-4 PR-evidence blocks across rounds instead of mislabelling them dedup_active_claim (~5,400 s/16 h)
body:
## What

Every dispatch round re-runs the full 50–120 s pre-launch ceremony for candidates that layer 4 (`_dedup_layer4_pr_evidence`) already blocked because an open, merged or draft PR exists for the issue. The block is never cached across rounds, so it consumes dispatch-round budget that should reach launchable candidates.

## Root cause

1. For non-worker PR evidence, `_dedup_layer4_pr_evidence` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-dedup-layers.sh`) logs `Dedup: <evidence>` but prints nothing to stdout. `_dispatch_dedup_check_layers` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh:530-538`) therefore falls back to `reason=dedup_active_claim signal=dedup_guard_blocked`. It is a PR block, not a claim.
2. `dedup_active_claim` hints are deliberately not honoured on an empty local worker pool when this runner owns the assignment (`_dispatch_negative_cache_reason`, GH#37780). `_dispatch_recheck_zero_worker_active_claims` also strips them from the per-cycle benign ledger. Both rules exist to recover orphaned self-owned claims. They are wrong for PR evidence, which does not depend on local worker liveness.
3. The cache record also requires an assignee and a status label, so unassigned issues blocked by an existing draft (for example `status:available` plus a draft) are never cached.

The result is self-reinforcing: an empty pool forces a recheck of every self-owned PR block, the round budget runs out before launchable candidates are reached, and the pool stays empty.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `rg -o 'Dedup: draft PR #[0-9]+ is a durable checkpoint for issue #[0-9]+|DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=dedup_active_claim signal=dedup_guard_blocked issue=#[0-9]+ repo=[^ ]+' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head`

**Actual output (abridged):** `12 ... issue=#NNNNN repo=<private-repo>`, `8 ... #105`, `7 ... #32`, `6 ... issue=#240 repo=marcusquinn/cloudron-netbird-app`. The same unchanged PR-held issues are blocked again every round.

Maintainer host, `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`, 2026-11-13 02:59–19:12Z (16.2 h). Every `DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=dedup_active_claim` was joined to its preceding `Dedup:` line and the candidate `elapsed_ms`:

| layer-4 evidence (mislabelled `dedup_active_claim`) | n | total s | mean s | unique issues |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| open PR is approved or mergeable | 37 | 1832 | 49.5 | 17 |
| open PR has commits targeting issue | 29 | 1512 | 52.1 | 26 |
| open PR closes issue via keyword in body | 17 | 1232 | 72.5 | 16 |
| draft PR is a durable checkpoint (non-worker draft) | 12 | 664 | 55.3 | 1 |
| merged PR references issue via keyword | 3 | 139 | 46.2 | 3 |

That is about 5,400 s of candidate-slot time in 16 h, and none of it was an actual claim. Example: `marcusquinn/cloudron-netbird-app#240` is held by PR #241 (`hold-for-review`, `release-approval-required`, unchanged since 04:09Z). It was re-ceremonied every round for 58–70 s. Its negative-cache record (`dedup_active_claim`, matching `updatedAt`) was ignored because the assignee is this runner and the local pool was empty. The last three rounds processed 30–72 candidates each and launched 0–1 workers, with the pool at 1/20.

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-dedup-layers.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-diagnose-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons.sh`

1. In `_dedup_layer4_pr_evidence`, when the helper blocks (rc 0) with output that is not `WORKER_DRAFT_CHECKPOINT:` and names a PR, print `pr_evidence_block: <output>` to stdout. Leave the uncertainty and worker-draft paths unchanged.
2. `classify_dispatch_blocker_reason`: map the `pr_evidence_block:` prefix to a new reason, `dedup_pr_evidence`, before the structural chain runs.
3. Register `dedup_pr_evidence` as a benign block and stats reason in `pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh`.
4. In `_dispatch_cache_confirmed_block`, record `dedup_pr_evidence` with the PR number parsed from the candidate's attempt lines. The fingerprint comes from one bounded REST read of the exact PR: `state`, `merged_at`, `draft`, `updated_at`, `head.sha`.
5. `_dispatch_negative_cache_reason`: honour `dedup_pr_evidence` only if the issue `updatedAt` is unchanged, the record is within the existing 1800 s TTL, and the live PR fingerprint still matches. Skip the owner-label requirement and the GH#37780 empty-pool rule; neither applies to PR evidence. Any read failure falls through to the full ceremony.

## Safety

The fingerprint covers every PR change that can lift a layer-4 block (close, merge, draft toggle, body or title edit, labels, commits; GitHub bumps `updated_at` for each). Any issue change, including an approval comment that would route `_dispatch_revised_checkpoint`, bumps the issue's `updatedAt` and invalidates the record. The only gap is a mergeability change without `updated_at`, and the 30-minute TTL bounds it. Worker drafts keep their existing `worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked` path.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons.sh`, `test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh`, `test-dispatch-dedup-stale-no-worker.sh` pass.
- `shellcheck` clean; `/bin/bash -n` parses (Bash 3.2).
- After deploy: `rg -c 'cross-cycle ownership block:dedup_pr_evidence' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` grows, and repeat `DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON` lines for the same unchanged PR-held issue stop within one TTL.

title: fix(pulse): checkpoint-claim ledger sweep is skipped whenever the deferrable stale_blocked_reconcile stage is budget-deferred
body:
## Problem

GH#38104 / PR #38116 added a device-local ledger so the pulse releases this device's own expired revision-checkpoint prelaunch claims every cycle. The ledger sweep (`_pulse_sweep_checkpoint_ledger`) is called inside `_pulse_reconcile_stale_blocked_if_due`. That function runs as the `stale_blocked_reconcile` stage, and `_pulse_stage_priority_class` puts that stage in the `deferrable` class. When the REST-core or GraphQL budget policy defers deferrable stages, the ledger sweep is skipped too, even though it makes no GitHub reads when nothing has expired.

The pre-dispatch stage runs once per pulse cycle, and cycles currently take about 45 minutes. So one deferral leaves an expired own claim open for at least 1.5 hours. During that time the issue stays `status:in-progress` and assigned, and continuation stays blocked.

## Evidence (v3.39.189, macOS runner, 2026-11-13)

- A revision-checkpoint `DISPATCH_CLAIM` was posted at 18:35:28Z for a private managed-repo issue. Its prelaunch `expires_at` was 18:37:19Z. The continuation launch then failed (`rc=13`). The ledger held exactly this one entry.
- In `pulse.log`, `Stage start: stale_blocked_reconcile` last ran at about 18:20Z, before the claim was posted. The fallback cursor `~/.aidevops/cache/checkpoint-claim-next-repo` was last written at 18:19:46.
- In the next cycle, at about 19:05Z: `budget-priority: deferred deferrable stage 'stale_blocked_reconcile' (graphql=normal:4961/5000@1188, rest=normal:226/5000@35 ...)`. In the visible log window this stage was deferred 4 times and started 13 times.
- At 19:27Z, running `dispatch-claim-helper.sh sweep-pr-checkpoint-claim <issue> <repo>` by hand released the claim at once (`CLAIM_RELEASED reason=claim_only_no_worker`) and pruned the ledger entry. The sweep logic works; only its scheduling is wrong.

## Fix

- Run `_pulse_sweep_checkpoint_ledger` as its own stage before dispatch. Classify it as `critical`, or as `progress` gated only by the REST hard floor, so a deferrable-stage deferral does not suppress it. With nothing expired it costs no reads. Each expired own claim costs one marker read, one fresh re-read and one write.
- Keep the fallback repo rotation (`_pdcu_sweep_expired_claims`) inside the deferrable stage. It scans repositories and is legitimately deferrable.
- Log one line when the ledger sweep releases a claim or retains one after a failed release. Today a successful or skipped sweep writes nothing to `pulse.log`, so a stranded claim cannot be diagnosed from the logs.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh`: `_pulse_reconcile_stale_blocked_if_due` (about line 951) and `_pulse_sweep_checkpoint_ledger` (about line 933).
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`: `_pulse_run_pre_dispatch_stages` (about line 1529). Add the new stage before `stale_blocked_reconcile`.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-budget-priority.sh`: `_pulse_stage_priority_class`. Add the new stage name to the chosen class.
- Reference pattern: `evaluate_routines` is `critical` because it spends no quota.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-budget-priority.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-checkpoint.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-graphql-budget-priority.sh`

`dispatch-claim-checkpoint.sh` (`cmd_sweep_checkpoint_ledger`) is the only place that knows whether a ledger entry was released or retained, so the one-line log required by the Fix section lands there; its stdout already goes to `pulse.log`. The regression case lands in the existing budget-priority test.

## Verification

- `tests/test-dispatch-claim-ledger.sh`, `tests/test-pulse-stale-blocked-reconcile.sh` and `tests/test-pulse-graphql-budget-priority.sh` pass.
- Add one regression case: with `stale_blocked_reconcile` deferred (REST class `reserve`), the ledger sweep still runs and releases an expired own entry.
- `shellcheck` reports zero violations on the touched scripts.

Related: #38104 (ledger), #38103 (stranded claims after a failed continuation launch), #38014.

title: fix(checkpoints): revision continuation prelaunch lease (120s) expires during transfer/worktree prep, failing launch rc=13 and stranding approvals
body:
## Problem

An approved revision-checkpoint continuation can fail with `launch failed rc=13` because its own prelaunch lease expires before launch. `claim-pr-checkpoint` posts a `DISPATCH_CLAIM` whose prelaunch `expires_at` is about 120 s away (`DISPATCH_CLAIM_ORPHAN_GRACE=120`). Nothing renews that lease before the worker starts. The launch path then runs these steps in order:

1. the claim consensus window and a snapshot re-read
2. the ownership transfer (assignee and status writes)
3. `verify-pr-checkpoint-target` (post-transfer)
4. review worktree preparation
5. `_prrts_final_dispatch_fence`, which calls `verify-pr-checkpoint-target` again

On loaded hosts these steps take more than 120 s. Both verifications pass the lease to `pr-checkpoint-revision.py`. `successors_valid()` in `pr_checkpoint_events.py` returns False once `claim.expires_at <= now`, so the launch fails as `checkpoint_post_transfer_verification_failed` or `checkpoint_final_target_verification_failed`.

Each failure:

- consumes the maintainer's approval; a new approval is needed.
- leaves the issue assigned and `status:in-progress`, because the restore is skipped with `checkpoint claim or target no longer valid` (see #38103).
- leaves an expired open claim until a sweep releases it (see #38144).

## Evidence (v3.39.188–189, 2026-11-13)

- Linux runner A: claim posted at 19:25:52Z with prelaunch expiry at 19:27:55Z. The transfer finished at 19:27:01Z. The final fence ran after worktree preparation and the state recorded `completed_at` 19:28:10Z, 15 s after expiry: `checkpoint_final_target_verification_failed`, `launch failed rc=13`.
- macOS runner: claim at 18:35:08Z, expiry at 18:37:19Z, transfer at 18:36:26–48Z. The state recorded `completed_at` exactly at the expiry epoch: `checkpoint_post_transfer_verification_failed`, `launch failed rc=13`. A direct `verify-pr-checkpoint-target` then returned `reason=eligibility_changed`.
- Across both Linux runners, the per-PR state files hold 4 more failures of this class, each 214–258 s from `dispatched_at` to `completed_at`: final-target (221 s, 228 s) and post-transfer (258 s, plus 214 s locally). Short failures of other kinds (`checkpoint_claim_failed`, 30–98 s) are not part of this issue.
- Counts of `launch failed rc=13` lines in scanner and pulse logs: 36 on runner A (against 87 continuation launches) and 17 on runner B (against 64). Not every rc=13 is a lease expiry. Please instrument the reason (see Verification).

## Fix

- Use the existing manual-dispatch pattern: `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` (around line 1350) renews the prelaunch lease with `dispatch-claim-helper.sh transition prelaunch <issue> <repo> <lease> <session> <ttl>`, where the TTL covers preparation (`_DSI_PRELAUNCH_PREPARATION_SECONDS=600`).
- In `pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` `_pcc_claim_checkpoint` (around lines 165–211), renew the prelaunch lease right after the claim is acquired and before the ownership transfer. Use a preparation TTL (for example 600 s). The phase stays `prelaunch`, so the existing comment about not pre-transitioning to `ready` still holds. `successors_valid()` already merges own prelaunch renewals into the claim (`own_renewal_matches`), and the `require_prelaunch` check accepts `phase=prelaunch`.
- Before `_prrts_prelaunch_target_fence` in `pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh` `_prrts_final_dispatch_fence` (around line 1337), renew again when less than a safety margin remains (for example 90 s).
- When a verification fails, log whether the lease had expired, for example `reason=prelaunch_lease_expired` against other eligibility changes. The two causes need different responses and cannot be told apart today.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`: `_pcc_claim_checkpoint`, and `_prrts_prelaunch_target_fence` (around line 242).
- `.agents/scripts/pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh`: `_prrts_final_dispatch_fence`.
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-helper.sh`: `transition` (already supports prelaunch renewal), and `cmd_verify_pr_checkpoint_target` (diagnostic reason).
- Reference pattern: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` prelaunch renewal.

## Verification

- The existing checkpoint-continuation and dispatch-claim tests pass (`tests/test-dispatch-claim-helper.sh`, and the `tests/test-pr-checkpoint-*.sh` and `tests/test-pr-review-thread-response-*.sh` suites that cover `_pcc_claim_checkpoint`).
- Add one regression case: stub the clock so more than 120 s pass between claim and final fence. With renewal, the fence passes and the launch proceeds. Without renewal, it fails with the new diagnostic reason.
- `shellcheck` reports zero violations on the touched scripts.

Related: #38103 (restore after failed launch), #38144 (ledger sweep deferral), #36771 (consensus-window expiry, closed), #37735 (closed).

title: perf(worktree): precreate.verify_generation p50 45 s even on small repos — receipt reconciliation parses 5,134 receipts 3x under the global receipt lock
body:
## What

Worker pre-creation spends 20–120 s in `precreate.verify_generation` on every launch, even for small repositories whose `git worktree add` takes 1–3 s. The full pre-launch ceremony (`dedup.ceremony_total`) grew from p50 117 s at 12Z to about 390 s at 17–18Z on the maintainer host, which directly limits how many workers the pulse can start per hour.

## Evidence

Maintainer host, `~/.aidevops/logs/dispatch-stages.tsv`, 2026-11-13 12:00–19:40Z:

| stage | n | p50 s | p90 s | max s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `precreate.helper_add` | 16 | 91.4 | 152.8 | 214.2 |
| `precreate.verify_generation` | 16 | 44.6 | 110.6 | 117.2 |
| `precreate.create_worktree` | 21 | 39.1 | 115.7 | 130.3 |
| `precreate.git_worktree_add` | 22 | 26.1 | 69.4 | 77.1 |

Per repository, `git_worktree_add` is 0.8–3.3 s for eight small repositories but about 36 s for one large private repository, so it scales with repository size. `verify_generation` does not: it is 22–56 s for small repositories where `git worktree add` took 1–3 s (for example 3.0 s vs 50.2 s, and 1.7 s vs 22.2 s). The cost is shared, not per repository.

`_cmd_add_verify_created_generation` (`.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh`) runs three steps and none of them is timed separately:

1. `register_worktree` (`.agents/scripts/shared-worktree-registry.sh`, Python registry write)
2. `_cmd_add_created_registration_contract` (`check_worktree_owner` read-back)
3. `_cmd_add_reconcile_cleanup_generation` → `full_loop_supersede_cleaned_receipts_for_recreated_worktree` (`.agents/scripts/full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh`)

Step 3 is the likely dominant cost (hypothesis; confirm with step 1 below):

- The receipt directory `~/.aidevops/state/full-loop-cleanup` holds **5,134** receipt files (20 MB). **4,480** are terminal `CLEANED`, 639 `CLEANUP_DEFERRED`, 15 `CLEANUP_LEASED`.
- One full-set `jq` pass over the directory takes 1.4 s on the loaded host (load average 14–25 on 16 cores).
- Under the global `mkdir` lock (`.mutation.lock.d`), reconciliation runs three full-set passes: `_full_loop_valid_receipt_file_count`, `_full_loop_cleanup_receipt_for_worktree_unlocked` and `_full_loop_active_recreated_receipts_are_cleaned`. It does this even when no receipt names the new path, which is the normal case for a fresh worktree slug.
- `_full_loop_receipt_lock_acquire` retries 200 times with `sleep 0.05` plus an owner-liveness probe per attempt. Cleanup passes in `worktree-clean-lib.sh` and `worktree-helper-cmds.sh` take the same lock per lookup, each running a full-set pass. Concurrent launches and cleanup therefore serialize on one lock whose hold time scales with the total receipt count.

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh` (existing suite; extend only if a changed contract requires it)

1. **Measure first.** Wrap the three steps of `_cmd_add_verify_created_generation` with `_ds_substage_run` (pattern: the existing `precreate.verify_generation` call at `_cmd_add_register_created_generation`), for example `precreate.verify.register`, `precreate.verify.contract` and `precreate.verify.reconcile`. Inside `full_loop_supersede_cleaned_receipts_for_recreated_worktree`, record the lock wait separately from the scan if the stage recorder is available (guard with `declare -F`).
2. **Collapse the three passes into one.** Under the lock, one `jq` invocation can return the valid-set count, the selected receipt for the worktree and whether every matching non-superseded receipt is `CLEANED`. It must keep the fail-closed behaviour: a symlink, malformed JSON, non-object or empty file still refuses. This is behaviour-preserving and cuts lock hold time by about two-thirds.
3. **Shrink the hot set (only after a consumer audit).** Terminal `CLEANED` receipts older than a bounded age (for example 14 days) could move to `${receipt_dir}/archive/`, outside the scanned `*.json` glob, and stay preserved. Before doing this, audit every reader of `_full_loop_cleanup_receipt_path` and of the receipt directory glob (`finalize-receipt`, `record-no-release`, `adopt-merged-receipt`, release reconcile/inclusion transitions, cleanup supervisors). Add an archive fallback for exact PR-path reads. If any consumer needs hot-directory presence of old `CLEANED` receipts for correctness, skip this step and record why in the PR.

Choose what to ship from the step 1 measurements. If registry or contract dominates instead, fix that step and say so in the PR.

## Safety

Receipts are lifecycle evidence for worktree cleanup and release state, so a wrong read can delete or strand work. Keep every fail-closed path. Never delete receipts. Keep the lock for any read that leads to a mutation. Do not add a lock-free fast path unless it is proven that no concurrent writer can create a receipt for the same new path.

## Verification

title: fix(github-app-auth): request actions:read by default so App-routed workflow/run reads stop returning 403
body:
## What

Request `actions: read` in the default repository-scoped GitHub App read set used by Pulse and inherited worker `gh` reads, capped by what the installation grants.

## Why

Repository App reads route supported workflow/run reads (`gh run list`, `gh run view`, `/repos/OWNER/REPO/actions/...`, and GraphQL `statusCheckRollup ... checkSuite.workflowRun`) to the App. `.agents/reference/github-app-auth.md` lists **Actions: Read when enabled** in the permission matrix. Default and migrated profiles never request it:

- `.agents/scripts/github_app_auth.py:167`: `REQUIRED_PULSE_PERMISSIONS = ("contents", "pull_requests", "issues", "metadata", "checks", "statuses")` has no `actions`.
- `.agents/scripts/github_app_auth.py:177-181`: `cached_token()` falls back to that tuple. It also rewrites the historical generated default `{"metadata","issues","pull_requests"}` to the same tuple, so `actions` is never requested.
- `.agents/scripts/github_auth_profiles.py:38`: new profiles use the same tuple.

The installation can grant `actions: read` while the default profile omits it. In that case, every App-routed Actions read returns `HTTP 403 Resource not accessible by integration`. GraphQL check rollups return partial `Resource not accessible by integration` errors on `checkSuite.workflowRun`. Routing does not retry with personal auth on 403, so these reads always fail.

### Observed evidence (2026-11-13)

- A managed-repo checkpoint continuation worker on a Linux runner stopped with `CONTINUATION_BLOCKER_FINDING blocked_by=infrastructure reason=deployment_verification_access`. Its deployment-verification step ran `gh run list` for the deploy workflow and got `HTTP 403 Resource not accessible by integration`. The worker log also contains GraphQL `Resource not accessible by integration (repository.pullRequest.statusCheckRollup...checkSuite.workflowRun)`.
- That runner's profile was the historical default (`issues`, `metadata`, `pull_requests`). Its installation grants `actions`, `administration`, `checks`, `contents`, `issues`, `members`, `metadata`, `pull_requests` and `statuses` at read level.
- A second runner whose profile explicitly lists `actions` did not hit this.
- Operational mitigation on the affected runner: adding `actions` (plus the required set) to its profile let the next minted token carry `actions: read`. The deploy-workflow runs endpoint then returned 200. Operators who have not hand-edited their profile still get the failing default.

## How

1. `.agents/scripts/github_app_auth.py`: add an optional-read tuple, for example `OPTIONAL_PULSE_PERMISSIONS = ("actions",)`, and a default request set `DEFAULT_PULSE_READ_PERMISSIONS = REQUIRED_PULSE_PERMISSIONS + OPTIONAL_PULSE_PERMISSIONS`.
   - Use it in `cached_token()`, both as the missing-`permissions` fallback and as the historical-default migration target.
   - Also migrate the previous generated default (exactly the six `REQUIRED_PULSE_PERMISSIONS` at `read`) to the new default, so profiles created by `github_auth_profiles.py` gain `actions` in memory without hand edits. Keep any other explicit map unchanged.
   - Keep `missing_permissions()` on `REQUIRED_PULSE_PERMISSIONS` only, so installations without Actions still pass `check`.
   - `exchange()` already intersects requested permissions with installation grants (`github_app_auth.py:125-131`). Installations without `actions` keep minting tokens; do not change that.
2. `.agents/scripts/github_auth_profiles.py:38`: generate new profiles with the default request set.
3. Optional but preferred: `aidevops github auth check` reports when the installation grants `actions` but the minted token lacks it. Do not fail; it is optional.
4. `.agents/reference/github-app-auth.md`: in the permission matrix and profile example, say Actions read is requested by default when the installation grants it. Without it, workflow/run reads and check-rollup `workflowRun` fields fail with 403 and are not retried with personal auth.

Do not route Actions reads to personal auth on 403. The read/write boundary forbids a personal-auth fallback (`github-app-auth.md` "Read/write boundary").

## Acceptance criteria

- With no `permissions` key, the historical three-permission default, or the previous six-permission generated default, `cached_token()` requests `actions: read` whenever the installation grants it.
- An installation that does not grant `actions` still mints a token, and `check` still passes when the required set is granted.
- An explicit custom permissions map is never widened.
- Existing tests pass: `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test_pulse_repo_auth.py` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-github-app-auth-helper.sh`. Extend the existing cached-token/migration tests in `test_pulse_repo_auth.py` for the new default. No new harness.
- `shellcheck` is unaffected (Python-only change); `python3 -m py_compile` passes on the touched modules.

## Reproducer

On a host whose repository App read profile is the generated default (no `permissions` key, or `metadata`/`issues`/`pull_requests` only) and whose installation grants `actions: read`:

1. `aidevops github auth check OWNER/REPO --consumer pulse` passes (the required set is granted).
2. Mint a scoped token through `cached_token()` and list its permissions: `actions` is absent.
3. From a Pulse-routed process (`AIDEVOPS_PULSE_REPO=OWNER/REPO`), run `gh run list --repo OWNER/REPO --workflow <deploy>.yml --limit 1`. Result: `HTTP 403 Resource not accessible by integration`.
4. Add `"actions": "read"` to the profile and repeat step 3. Result: 200 with run metadata. This was confirmed on 2026-11-13 against `/repos/OWNER/REPO/actions/workflows/<deploy>.yml/runs`.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/github_app_auth.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/github_auth_profiles.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/github_auth_runtime.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test_pulse_repo_auth.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/github-app-auth.md`

Notes: `github_app_auth.py` holds `REQUIRED_PULSE_PERMISSIONS` and `cached_token()`. `github_auth_profiles.py:38` is the new-profile default. `github_auth_runtime.py` lines 109-120 are where the optional `check` note goes. In `github-app-auth.md`, update the permission matrix and the profile example.

title: perf(routines): actions-event-policy status spends ~1,500 REST core requests per run and exhausts the shared rate limit
body:
## What

Each `r-event-policy` routine run (`actions-event-policy-routine.sh` → `actions-event-policy-helper.sh status --all-managed`) spends about 1,500 REST core requests within 15–30 minutes. The maintainer account already averages about 74% of its 5,000/h core budget from pulse, merge and worker traffic, so this burst exhausts it. While the account is in `gh-cooldown`, issue creation, PR checks, dispatch and merges all stall for every session on the host.

## Evidence

Maintainer host, `~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls.log` (per-request ledger):

- Over the last 43.8 h: 161,734 REST core attempts (about 3,690/h average). `actions-event-policy-helper.sh` made 5,971 of them across 4 routine runs (about 1,490 per run).
- 2026-11-13 19:40–19:56Z: 266 `actions-event-policy-helper.sh` requests in 16 minutes (6–34/min) on top of normal load. At 19:56Z the shim reported `primary-core active=true reason=github-core-primary-exhausted`, and an interactive `gh-write-helper.sh issue create` hit HTTP 403 rate limit.

## Root cause

`_policy_scan` in `.agents/scripts/actions-event-policy-helper.sh` makes, per managed repository:

1. `GET repos/{slug}` (default branch and visibility)
2. `GET repos/{slug}/contents/.github/workflows?ref=…` (listing)
3. one `GET repos/{slug}/contents/{path}?ref=…` **for every `.yml`/`.yaml` workflow file**, then a local `grep` for the event

Two avoidable costs follow:

- **Non-public repositories** always end in `OK …: not applicable (non-public repository)`, but `_policy_cmd_status` checks `.public` only after `_policy_scan` has downloaded every workflow file.
- **Unchanged files are re-downloaded every run.** The directory listing already returns each file's blob `sha`, and blob content is immutable for a given SHA.

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/actions-event-policy-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-actions-event-policy-helper.sh` (existing suite; extend only where a changed contract requires it)

1. **Gate on visibility before listing.** In `_policy_scan`, read visibility from the first `repos/{slug}` response. For `status`, return the non-public result before listing or fetching any workflow. Keep `plan`/`apply` behaviour explicit: the routine already refuses non-public repositories before `apply`.
2. **Cache workflow content by blob SHA.** Keep the listing call (it is the change detector) and use each entry's `sha`. Store fetched content (or only the derived `{mentions_event, events, parsed}` result) in a local cache keyed by `sha`, for example under `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/cache/actions-event-policy/<sha>`, with 600 permissions. Fetch a file only on a cache miss. A blob SHA cannot go stale, so no TTL is needed; bound cache size with a simple age prune.
3. Optional, if cheap: reuse the existing conditional-request cache (`.agents/scripts/pulse-batch-conditional-cache.py`, ETag/`If-None-Match`; 304 responses do not count against the primary rate limit) for the `repos/{slug}` and listing reads.

## Safety

The routine reports repositories whose `pull_request_target` workflows will be blocked by default from 2026-12-02, and can apply policies to public repositories. Correctness must not regress:

- Any API error must still fail the repository (never a silent `OK`).
- A 404 listing remains an empty set.
- A cache-read or parse failure must fall back to a live fetch.
- `apply` must still scan live content for the repository it mutates. Using the cache there is acceptable only if keyed by the exact blob SHA from a live listing taken in the same run.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-actions-event-policy-helper.sh` passes; ShellCheck clean; `/bin/bash -n` parses (Bash 3.2).
- Manual: run `actions-event-policy-helper.sh status --all-managed` twice. Count `actions-event-policy-helper.sh` attempts added to `~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls.log` by each run: the second run should be at most about 2 requests per managed repository plus policy reads for public repositories with matching workflows. The `OK`/`UNCOVERED` output must be identical between runs.

title: fix(workers): decide reversible in-scope choices instead of parking drafts as decision blockers; publish full option sets
body:
## What

Stop workers from parking resolvable design choices as `decision` blockers that wait for a human. Two prompt rules tell workers to stop on any choice the brief does not make, and neither mentions the existing decision-only consultation (`reference/agent-routing.md`, "When current-model uncertainty is the only reason...") that is meant to run before a decision is exported to a person. When a worker does stop, the published finding truncates the options at 700 characters, so whoever decides cannot see them all.

## Why

Observed 2026-11-13 on #38103: the checkpoint continuation worker implemented criteria 1–4 on draft PR #38133, then stopped with `CONTINUATION_BLOCKER_FINDING ... blocked_by=decision reason=ttl_hold_design_choice`. The choice was internal and reversible: whether a dispatch hold should be a new label or rely on the existing negative cache. Repository code answered it (`_dispatch_negative_cache_reason` in `pulse-dispatch-lib.sh` already keys that hold to `updatedAt`). The draft sat idle for about 2 hours until an interactive session revised the brief and published an approval. The published finding ended mid-option (`2. Clear the label ...`) because of the 700-character cap.

#38103 also records 7 `blocked` (worker-decision) drafts on one managed product repo that each got one attention record and then nothing. Every such stop costs maintainer attention that the framework's purpose says should go to seeding new needs, not to answering choices AI can make.

Sources of the stop rule:

- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` continuation prompt, step 7 (around lines 496–502): "a draft whose remaining acceptance needs a human choice the brief does not make (`decision`, naming the exact choice)".
- `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md` Headless Dispatch Rules item 5 (around line 209): "EXIT for API breaks, obsolete task, missing credentials/external services, architectural decisions."
- `.agents/scripts/pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh` lines 943 and 1027 cap finding details at 700 characters.

## How

1. In the continuation prompt step 7, state that a choice the brief does not make is not by itself a blocker. If it is in scope and reversible, the worker chooses the option that best preserves the brief's stated outcome and the repository's existing patterns, using the decision-only consultation first when uncertain. It records the choice under the PR body's decisions and continues. `decision` remains for choices that need authority, consent, taste or values, inaccessible context, unknown secrets, an irreversible commitment, or that contradict the brief's explicit text. The details file must list every option and the worker's recommendation.
2. In `full-loop.md` item 5, narrow "architectural decisions" in the same way and point to the decision-only consultation, so implementation workers follow the same rule.
3. Raise the finding-details cap at both `_prrts_state_value_line ... 700` call sites to 2000 characters so the full option set is published.

Edit only the continuation prompt step 7, `full-loop.md` item 5, and the two details caps.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh`

## Acceptance

- [ ] The continuation prompt no longer instructs a `decision` stop for every choice the brief does not make; it names the escalation set, the decision-only consultation, and requires every option and a recommendation in the details.
- [ ] `full-loop.md` item 5 matches that rule.
- [ ] Finding details publish up to 2000 characters.
- [ ] ShellCheck is clean on changed scripts; the existing continuation prompt and review-thread scanner tests pass.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh .agents/scripts/pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-dispatch.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-review-thread-response-scanner-lifecycle.sh
```

title: feat(checkpoints): AI brief-owner pass resolves decision-blocked worker drafts instead of waiting for a maintainer
body:
## What

When a worker draft checkpoint is parked by a `decision` blocker, run one bounded thinking-tier "brief owner" pass. The pass either decides, by appending a decision record to the brief and publishing a `CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_APPROVED` through the existing approval path, or escalates with a classified reason. A maintainer then sees only genuine escalations, each with its reason, instead of every choice a worker declined to make.

## Why

A `blocked` release or `CONTINUATION_BLOCKER_FINDING ... blocked_by=decision` currently gets one attention record and then waits for a human indefinitely (#38103 root cause D: 7 such drafts on one managed product repo, idle for hours to days). The dispatch negative cache bounds the polling cost but not the wait.

Worked example, resolved by hand on 2026-11-13: draft PR #38133 (#38103) stopped with `reason=ttl_hold_design_choice`. An interactive session read the finding and the relevant code (`_dispatch_negative_cache_reason` in `pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`), appended a "Decision record" to the brief, generated `pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh approval-template marcusquinn/aidevops 38133 38103 <release-id> attempt:<id>` and published the line. That took about 10 minutes of model work, but the draft had already waited 2 hours for it. Nothing in that sequence needed human authority; it needed only reading and judgment.

#38153 cuts new decision stops at the worker. This issue handles the decision stops that still happen, including existing parked drafts, so that "blocked" always carries a why and is revisited by AI before it costs a person time.

## Reproducer

1. For an issue with a draft worker PR, list its decision findings: `gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/issues/ISSUE/comments --paginate --jq '.[] | select(.body | test("CONTINUATION_BLOCKER_FINDING .*blocked_by=decision")) | .created_at'`. Alternatively, look for `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION` records older than 24 h.
2. Observed: the draft stays idle; `blocked-attention` posts once and does nothing further; no approval or escalation follows.
3. Expected: within one dispatch cycle of the finding, either a decision record plus approval appears, or one classified escalation record appears.

## How

Reference patterns to follow:

- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-unknown-digest.sh` `_pcc_unknown_pending_work`: opt-in repos.json `checkpoint_policy`, write-permission checks for `configured_by`, the publishing login and the runner, `_pcc_approval_template` bound to the exact head and brief SHA, and publication through `gh-write-helper.sh issue comment`.
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` `_terminal_blocker_triage_unknown`: one bounded `ai-research-helper.sh --stdin` inference with a timeout and an allowlisted JSON result; anything else keeps the hold.

Steps:

1. **Trigger.** In `_pcc_blocked_attention` (`pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`), after its existing eligibility checks, detect that the newest blocker for the current head is decision-class: a trusted `CONTINUATION_BLOCKER_FINDING ... blocked_by=decision` comment, or a `blocked` release whose terminal-blocker class is a decision. Exclude `already_landed`.
2. **Policy.** Add `checkpoint_policy.auto_resolve_decisions: true` beside `auto_continue_unknown_pending_work`, with the same `configured_by` rule. With the policy off, keep today's behaviour exactly.
3. **Inference.** Make one call: `ai-research-helper.sh --stdin --model thinking` under a timeout of at most 180 s. Pass the issue body, the finding's full details, the PR title, the diff stat, and a bounded diff excerpt of the files the finding names. The prompt treats all of it as untrusted evidence. Accept only:
   - `{"action":"decide","confidence":"high","decision_record":"<markdown, at most 2500 chars>"}`, or
   - `{"action":"escalate","class":"authority|consent|taste|inaccessible_context|secret|irreversible|contradicts_brief|insufficient_evidence","why":"<at most 400 chars>"}`.
   Anything else, including `medium` confidence, counts as `escalate` with class `insufficient_evidence`.
4. **Decide.** Append `### Decision record (AI brief owner, <UTC date>)` to the issue body through `gh-write-helper.sh issue edit --body-file`. Edits are append-only: verify that the new body equals the old body plus the section. Then generate and publish the approval as `_pcc_unknown_pending_work` does, bound to the new brief SHA. Factor the shared permission-and-publish tail into one function rather than copying it.
5. **Escalate.** Post one deduplicated `DECISION_ESCALATION head=<sha> class=<class>` record (inside `ops:start`/`ops:end` markers) with the reason and the options. Add no label.
6. **Bounds and dedup.** Allow one resolver run per (issue, PR head, finding comment ID) and at most 2 per issue. Before inference, look for an existing decision record or escalation marker for that finding, so other runners and later cycles skip it. Mark every new trust check with `#aidevops:trust-boundary`. Never auto-resolve when the issue author or the finding's poster lacks write permission, or when any hold label from the `_pcc_unknown_pending_work` filter is present.

Put the new logic in a sourced file such as `pr-checkpoint-decision-resolver.sh`. `pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` is about 1,900 lines, and #38105 recently split it to stay under 2,000.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-decision-resolver.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-unknown-digest.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-dispatch.sh`

The dispatch test file is sourced by `test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`; run the parent. Its unknown-policy fixtures (search for `auto_continue_unknown_pending_work`) are the model for the new cases.

## Acceptance

- [ ] With the policy off, behaviour is unchanged: no inference, no brief edit, no approval.
- [ ] With the policy on, a decision finding on an eligible draft plus a high-confidence `decide` produces exactly one appended decision record and one approval bound to the new brief SHA, which `dispatch-approved` accepts.
- [ ] `escalate`, low or medium confidence, invalid JSON, or a timeout produces exactly one classified `DECISION_ESCALATION` record and no approval.
- [ ] Repeated cycles or a second runner produce no second inference or publication for the same finding.
- [ ] Trust filters match `_pcc_unknown_pending_work` (hold labels, write permission for every actor); the brief edit is verified append-only.
- [ ] ShellCheck is clean; `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` passes.

title: test(codegraph): resolve macOS temp root so lifecycle enrollment accepts the fixture state dir
body:
## What

`.agents/scripts/tests/test-codegraph-worktree-init-helper.sh` fails on macOS at current `main` (`5bed6c307f`):

```
FAIL: asynchronous init did not create the worktree index
```

This is test-fixture drift, not a production defect. Production CodeGraph init still runs.

## Reproducer

On macOS, at `main` `5bed6c307f`:

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-codegraph-worktree-init-helper.sh
# FAIL: asynchronous init did not create the worktree index   (exit 1)
```

Rerunning step 1 with logs retained shows `$AIDEVOPS_CODEGRAPH_LOG_FILE` contains only:

```
status=skipped reason=lifecycle-context-unavailable issue=30661
```

The fake `codegraph` is never called (no `calls.log`).

## Root cause (verified)

- The test sets `TEST_ROOT=$(mktemp -d)` (line 9) and exports `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_STATE_DIR="${TEST_ROOT}/lifecycle"` (line 93).
- On macOS, `mktemp -d` returns `/var/folders/...`, and `/var` is a symlink to `/private/var`.
- Since GH#35996 (`5596d7e677`), `codegraph-worktree-init-helper.sh` `_codegraph_new_lifecycle_context()` enrolls the worktree via `worker-registry.py enroll --initialize`. `LifecycleRegistry.initialize()` (`.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/storage.py:70-71`) deliberately rejects a non-canonical state parent with `state-parent-must-be-canonical`. That check is a symlink guard and must stay.
- Enrollment therefore fails, and the helper logs `status=skipped reason=lifecycle-context-unavailable issue=30661` and never launches init. The test then times out waiting for `codegraph.db`.
- Linux CI is unaffected because `/tmp` is already canonical, which is why this only reproduces on macOS.

Evidence: calling `worker-registry.py --state-dir <mktemp>/lifecycle enroll --initialize --path <linked>` directly returns `{"detail": "state-parent-must-be-canonical", "status": "unavailable"}` (rc 2). With the root resolved through `pwd -P` it returns a `generation_id` (rc 0).

## Fix

Resolve the temp root in the fixture, using the existing repo pattern from `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh:12` and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-scratch-worktree-helper.sh:13`:

```bash
TEST_ROOT="$(cd "$(mktemp -d)" && pwd -P)"
```

Do **not** relax the `state-parent-must-be-canonical` check in `storage.py`.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-codegraph-worktree-init-helper.sh`

Only line 9 (`TEST_ROOT=`) changes.

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-codegraph-worktree-init-helper.sh
# expect: PASS: CodeGraph init is asynchronous, admitted, generation-bound, singleflight, queued, optional, and bounded
shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/tests/test-codegraph-worktree-init-helper.sh
```

This was pre-verified on macOS: a copy of the test with only this change prints the PASS line and exits 0.

## Context

Found while verifying the release scope for GH#38026 / GH#38115. It is the same class of macOS fixture-path drift fixed for `test-worktree-capacity-recovery.sh` in `e6f3d6445d`.

title: fix(worker-lifecycle): legacy cleanup holds the registry writer across 300 s native worktree removal, refusing interactive bounded operations (database-locked)
body:
## What

Interactive sessions are refused with `database-locked` when they start a bounded operation in a linked worktree, because the observation-era legacy cleanup holds the worker-lifecycle registry write lock for the whole of a native `git worktree remove`. That removal has a 300 s limit. Interactive admission gives up after about 7 s, while worker launch admission waits 30 s. Two changes are needed:

1. Do not hold the registry writer across native removal in legacy cleanup.
2. Let bounded-operation admission wait out writer contention under the same 30 s bound that worker launches already use.

## Why

Every refusal forces a human-attended session to stop and retry, and gates such as `full-loop-helper.sh wait-checks` or `merge` cannot start at all. Today one macOS host logged 17 `database-locked` admission refusals, spread between 07:00 and 20:00 UTC. #37900 fixed the minutes-long hold during source inspection. Its PR #37902 recorded "finish()/reconstructible removal still hold the writer by design", and that remaining hold is what is now observed.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `aidevops_bounded_operation start` with any argv (here `full-loop-helper.sh wait-checks 38156 --repo marcusquinn/aidevops`), using a cwd inside a linked aidevops worktree, while `worker-legacy-cleanup.py --apply` runs from `pulse-cleanup-worktree-removal.sh`.

**Actual output** (twice, 2026-11-13 20:42 and 20:43 UTC, aidevops 3.39.189, OpenCode 1.19.5, macOS; elapsed 44 s and 10 s, exit 75, command never started):

```text
BLOCKED: bounded-operation lifecycle admission unavailable: lifecycle owner admission is unavailable (database-locked); no write authorized
```

Evidence collected at the time:

- `pgrep -fl worker-legacy-cleanup` showed one process, `worker-legacy-cleanup.py --state-dir <state> --repos-config <repos.json> --output-root <archives> --apply --budget-seconds 300`, with `ps` elapsed `09:58`, about twice its budget. `lsof registry.sqlite3 registry.sqlite3-wal` listed only that PID.
- The previous observation-era pass in `~/.aidevops/logs/cleanup_worktrees.log` reported, for a `managed-by-current-cleanup` worktree, `"operation":"subprocess","reason":"TimeoutExpired","status":"retained","timeout_seconds":300`. 300 s is `REMOVAL_TIMEOUT` (`interrupted_removal.py:27`), which `native_timeout` applies only to `git ... worktree remove`.
- A bounded `["true"]` started a few minutes later in the same worktree was admitted in 2.8 s, so the hold is intermittent, one native removal at a time.
- `jq 'select(.outcome=="refused")' ~/.aidevops/logs/lifecycle-admission/2026-11-13.jsonl` listed 17 `database-locked` refusals across the day.

## Root cause

- `legacy_cleanup.py` `process_reconstructible` holds `store.connection(write=True)` from plan through `_git(..., "worktree", "remove", plan["source"])` and `verify_reconstructible`. `finish()` holds the writer through `_git(..., "worktree", "remove", "--force", target)`. Both removals can each take up to 300 s.
- `worker-lifecycle-session-helper.py` `admit_targets_with_retry` retries contention twice (`STORE_CONTENTION_RETRY_DELAYS = (0.25, 0.75)`) with 2 s SQLite busy timeouts, a total of about 7 s, sized to fit the plugin's 10 s helper timeout. Worker launch admission waits up to 30 s (`AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_ADMISSION_WAIT_SECONDS`, see `worker-lifecycle/REGISTRY.md` around line 313).
- `legacy_runner.py` `run` computes `deadline` only after `inventory`, `discover` and `queue`, and checks it only between items, so `--budget-seconds` bounds neither discovery nor a single item.

## How

1. **Release the writer during native removal** (`legacy_cleanup.py`). Follow the pattern `finish()` already uses for the "removing" checkpoint (GH#37326). Journal the removal start and commit, run the native `git worktree remove` under `writer_released(connection)`, then reacquire the writer, verify, and journal "retired". The interrupted-removal resume path (`interrupted_removal.py`: `removal_started`, `require_deletion_only`, `restore_git_link`) already handles a crash between start and retire; reuse it for the reconstructible path rather than adding a parallel one. Keep every pre-removal guard (`unchanged()`, `same_tree`, `current != plan`) under the writer immediately before the removal starts.
2. **Bounded-operation admission wait** (`bounded-operation-supervisor.mjs` `runSupervisor`). The supervisor is its own detached process, so waiting does not block the session. On a refusal whose reason is `database-locked`, retry `admitToolOwner` with backoff (for example 0.5 s doubling to 4 s) until `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_ADMISSION_WAIT_SECONDS` (default 30, valid 0 to 300, invalid values deny) has elapsed. Any other reason refuses immediately, as today. Log each retry through the existing `recordAdmission` diagnostic. Leave synchronous in-hook admission for Bash/Edit/Write unchanged.
3. **Budget covers the pass** (`legacy_runner.py`). Start `deadline` before `inventory`/`discover`, and return an incomplete report if discovery exhausts it. `pulse-cleanup-worktree-removal.sh` already passes `--budget-seconds`.

Out of scope: the reclaim redesign in #38051. This is a targeted fix to the current path and must not pre-empt that parent's design.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/legacy_cleanup.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/legacy_runner.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-supervisor.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/REGISTRY.md` (one sentence: bounded operations share the admission wait)
- EDIT: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/LEGACY-CLEANUP.md` (removal no longer holds the writer)
- EDIT tests next to the existing cases: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_legacy_cleanup.py`, `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_reconstructible.py`, and `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-bounded-worktree-ownership.mjs`, which already exercises `admitToolOwner` for bounded operations (run with `node`).

## Acceptance

- [ ] During a native `git worktree remove` in either legacy path, another connection can take the registry writer (a test can hold removal open with a stub `_git` and assert `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` succeeds from a second connection).
- [ ] A crash between removal start and "retired" resumes through the existing interrupted-removal path, with no forced removal of a changed tree.
- [ ] A bounded operation whose admission first sees `database-locked` and is admitted within `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_ADMISSION_WAIT_SECONDS` starts its command; past the deadline it exits 75 with the same message as today. Non-contention reasons are not retried.
- [ ] A `--budget-seconds` pass ends within its budget plus at most one item's work, discovery included.
- [ ] `python3 -m unittest` for the touched worker-lifecycle tests passes, the supervisor test passes, and ShellCheck, ruff and mypy are clean on touched files where the repo already runs them.
