title: consolidation-task: merge thread on #38200 into single spec
body:
## Consolidation target: #38200

**Parent issue:** #38200 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** perf(pulse): new product-repo arrivals wait for round-robin after the #38024 backlog lead is consumed — 20-slot runner idles at 4/20
**Parent labels:** `bug,status:available,auto-dispatch,priority:high,tier:thinking,origin:worker,source:conflict-feedback,consolidation-in-progress,fix-the-fixer`

> Sources are inlined below unless explicitly listed as omitted. Fetch omitted references before consolidating.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below, fetching any explicitly omitted sources first.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `### Files Scope` — the successor's write surface, one repo-relative path per line and nothing else on the line (`- EDIT: path/to/file` or `- NEW: path/to/file`). Carry over the parent's scope when present. Read-only references belong in `## How`, not here. The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.
     Preserve every wildcard scope entry verbatim from every superseded issue, including tool-generated paths such as `- NEW: todo/<area>/log/*/*/<slug>-*.jsonl`. Never invent a concrete machine, date, timestamp or filename in place of a pattern. Never change an existing `EDIT:` entry to `NEW:`.
     Check each path against the current default branch before copying its scope marker: use `git ls-files` in an up-to-date default-branch checkout or `gh api` for that branch's contents. Use `EDIT:` when the path already exists on the default branch; use `NEW:` only after confirming it is absent. A stale checkout or failed API lookup is not proof of absence.
   - **Runner prerequisites** — copy verbatim every line matching `^requires-secrets:` and its runner-prerequisite paragraph from every superseded issue. Keep all source lines (do not replace them with a summary): the runner capability gate unions comma/space-separated names across these lines. Never drop a prerequisite because this consolidation runner lacks the named secret; consolidation itself does not need those credentials.
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #38200 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`
   That marker must be a line by itself, exactly as shown (no extra text, no trailing whitespace); the dispatch gate refuses consolidated successors without it. Put any further lineage (for example "#38200 itself superseded #M") on a separate line, and add one exact marker line per additional superseded issue.

3. **Validate before filing the new consolidated issue.** Save the parent body (inlined or explicitly fetched) verbatim to a local file, plus a separate body file for each additional superseded issue. Validate the merged body against ALL sources; a failed check stops publication and parent closure until the merged body is repaired:

```bash
python3 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/consolidation-contract-validator.py \
  --parent 38200 \
  --source "<file containing the verbatim parent body>" \
  --successor "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
# Repeat --source for each additional superseded issue body.
# Repeat --parent for each additional superseded issue number.
```

The validator must pass before running the signed creation command below. It checks the exact marker line for every `--parent`, verbatim secret lines and prerequisite paragraphs, wildcard scope preservation, and EDIT-to-NEW regressions. Also run `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check` on the merged body for ordinary scope syntax validation.

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,status:available,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding all status:* labels, needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body-file "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Use the signed wrapper above rather than the raw GitHub CLI so the successor retains the managed signature and origin metadata.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` and `status:available` are also mandatory. Keep exactly one `status:*` label on the successor: `status:available` — never the parent's ownership status (`status:queued`, `status:claimed`, `status:in-progress`, `status:in-review`). Immediately before creating the successor, re-read the parent's labels; if it now carries `status:blocked`, use `status:blocked` instead, because that label records an unresolved dependency or hold rather than ownership. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch; the fill-floor enumerator also needs the available status, and the pre-claim gate holds a `status:blocked` successor until its blocker is released.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close every superseded parent and verify each handoff.** Run all five commands below for #38200, then repeat them for every additional issue passed as `--parent` in step 3, substituting that issue number in every command (including dependency repointing and the state check). Every command must succeed:

```bash
gh issue comment 38200 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 38200 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 38200 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
# Repoint open dependants' blockedBy edges and Blocked-by lines at the successor (GH#35130):
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dependency-supersession-repoint-helper.sh repoint "marcusquinn/aidevops" 38200 $NEW_NUM
# Re-read the parent (GH#37600); this must print exactly: closed not_planned
gh api "repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/38200" --jq '.state + " " + (.state_reason // "")'
```

   **Handoff verification (GH#37600):** a parent that still reads `open` keeps the `consolidated` label while the dispatch gate rejects it, so it consumes dispatch attempts every cycle. If any command above fails or refuses the write (for example a worker target-scope guard on a non-target issue), or any parent re-read is not `closed not_planned`, this task has FAILED: do not run step 5 and do not report success. Leave this consolidation task open, record the parent number, the failing command and its output in one comment here, and exit `BLOCKED`. Report a reopen observed after your close as evidence, with its event time; do not guess its cause.

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** only after every parent passed the step 4 verification, with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #38200 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn @vladimirdulov."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- Read only explicitly omitted source references when the packet size limit prevents inlining them; otherwise do NOT re-read #38200.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Checkpoint recovery is never an unconditional requirement** (GH#35871). Name a checkpoint commit or branch as binding only after verifying it is reachable from a remote ref (`gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/commits/<sha>`), recording the full SHA and ref. Otherwise write: "Best-effort recovery: reuse if reachable; the functional spec is the source of truth; re-implement if unrecoverable." Never forbid re-implementing work that exists only as local commits on one runner.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn @vladimirdulov

## Parent body (verbatim)

## Observed

This is a follow-up to #38022 / PR #38024. The same 20-slot runner (70 pulse-enabled repositories, deployed v3.39.189 with #38024) is again running at `workers=4/20` (2026-11-14 01:30–01:55 UTC). The product repository at registry index 4 has **15 clean launchable issues**: `auto-dispatch`, `status:available`, no assignee, no claim comment, closed native blockers. `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh issue <N>` on one of them showed no backoff, no blockers and no attempts. The issues arrived between 00:55 and 01:44 UTC: a batch publication added new cores, and phases became unblocked when their cores closed.

Pulse log (local host):

```text
Dispatch_max: available=20, candidates=105     # earlier census reached the product repo
...
candidate enumeration timing census=full outcome=ok elapsed=739s sample=recorded
Dispatch_max: available=16, candidates=1
candidate enumeration timing census=full outcome=ok elapsed=554s sample=snapshot_hit
Dispatch_max: available=18, candidates=1       # wpallstars/seoprocookieconsent#207 only
Dispatch_max: #207 (...) blocked:dedup_pr_evidence benign dispatch block
Minimum worker floor refill stopped: dispatch_max returned 0 (no eligible candidates or hard gate exhausted)
pulse-health.json written: workers=4/20 (x5 consecutive)
```

`~/.aidevops/cache/pulse-first-wave-cursor` = `wpallstars/seoprocookieconsent` (index 61 of 70). In the meantime the other fleet runners claim the product repository's new issues. This host contributes 3–4 workers out of a 20-worker target.

## Root cause

#38024 lets a repository lead the first-wave rotation only while the first-wave snapshot still has **unconsumed** candidates for it (`_dispatch_first_wave_backlog_repos`, `pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh:230-239`; consumed via `${snapshot}.consumed`). Two gaps remain:

1. **New arrivals have no lead signal.** Once every candidate known from the last census is attempted, the repository drops back into plain rotation (`_dispatch_repository_rows`, `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:318-349`). Candidates are consumed on every attempt, including `rc=3` / `dedup_active_claim_durable_launch` losses to other runners. Work that appears afterwards — new issues, or phases unblocked by a closed core — is invisible until the cursor comes back round. With 70 repositories and 3–12 minute censuses, that takes about one wave in three.
2. **A snapshot hit can still take a full census duration.** The 554 s `sample=snapshot_hit` round served a snapshot captured before the call started (`_dispatch_enumeration_served_snapshot`, `pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh:940-955`). Freshness is `max(ttl, census_seconds)` (`_dispatch_candidate_snapshot_is_fresh`, `pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh:52-58`), so a 739 s census keeps a mostly consumed snapshot "fresh" for more than 12 minutes. Confirm where the 554 s went before changing anything. It may have been lock wait or prepass work rather than the read.

## Proposed fix

- Add a zero-API lead hint from data the cycle already holds. The issue prefetch (`_prefetch_repo_issues`, `pulse-prefetch-fetch.sh:498-523`, "using cycle canonical snapshot") has each repository's open issues with labels and assignees. Count `auto-dispatch` + `status:available` + unassigned issues per repository, minus attempt-recency keys, and put repositories with a non-zero count ahead of the plain rotation. Keep this stable partition next to the existing #38024 backlog partition. Repositories with no launchable work keep GH#33647 rotation fairness.
- Treat a snapshot whose unconsumed remainder is smaller than the free slots as stale for the first wave, while the prefetch-hint repositories hold launchable issues the snapshot does not contain. Re-enumerate those repositories first, instead of serving the remainder for a census-length window.
- Add a stat, for example `first_wave_new_arrival_lead`, to `pulse-health.json` so the effect is visible.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch-fetch.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-logging.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-candidate-snapshot.sh`

Integration scope recovery (worker, 2026-11-14): added `.agents/scripts/pulse-logging.sh`. The `pulse-health.json` document is written only by `write_pulse_health_file` there, and dispatch runs inside command substitutions, so the requested `first_wave_new_arrival_lead` field must be derived in that writer from the cycle's `pulse-stats.json` counter events (the same pattern as `_pulse_cycle_index_budget_skips`). Verification: the two tests above plus `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-cycle-state-contract.sh` (exercises `write_pulse_health_file`) and ShellCheck on the edited file.

## Verification

- Extend `test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh`: 70 repositories, cursor past the product repository, the first-wave snapshot fully consumed for it, and the prefetch fixture listing 15 fresh launchable issues there. Assert that the product repository is scanned in the next first wave. Add the inverse case: a repository with no prefetch-visible launchable issues keeps its rotation position.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-candidate-snapshot.sh` pass, with ShellCheck clean.
- Live: on a many-repository runner, within two cycles of new `status:available` issues appearing in one repository, `Dispatch_max: available=N, candidates=M` shows M ≥ min(N, new issues), and `pulse-health.json` `workers=` approaches the target.

## Related

#38022 / PR #38024 (unattempted backlog lead), GH#33647 / GH#34331 (first-wave fairness and bounded census), GH#37623 (census timing), #37874 (ranked-list reuse), #37888 (REST budget; `gh api user` per round at `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:712` is part of that).

title: t18987: fix(task-id-guard): name the malformed token and its source in block diagnostics
body:
**Task ID:** `t18987` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `auto-dispatch` `bug` `fix-the-fixer` `priority:medium`

## Outcome

fix(task-id-guard): name the malformed token and its source in block diagnostics

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief


## What

When `task-id-collision-guard.sh` blocks on a malformed task identity, print the offending token and its source (commit subject, commit body, PR title or PR body). Today the report shows only the subject line and the sentinel `__malformed__ — malformed task identity`.

## Why

The `__malformed__` sentinel drops the token that tripped `task_identity_has_malformed_candidate` (`.agents/scripts/task-identity-lib.sh`). `_report_violations` then prints `Subject: <subject or PR title>` under the header "Commit subject references invented or unclaimed task ID(s)". That points the author at a valid subject.

Observed on 2026-11-14, PR #38218. The commit body and later the PR body contained the prose placeholder `tNNN: plan: ...`. The guard reported the valid subject `t18986: fix(dispatch): ...` as the violation. The author rewrote a valid subject twice locally, and CI failed (`Task-ID Collision Guard`, run 43558546885). Removing `tNNN` from the body fixed it. Fail-closed matching of `t[A-Z]...` placeholders is intended. Only the diagnostic is wrong. Every agent that writes a `tNNN`/`tXXX` placeholder in a commit or PR body pays this cost.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/task-identity-lib.sh`: add `task_identity_first_malformed_candidate <text>`. It prints the first candidate that `task_identity_has_malformed_candidate` would reject, using the same brief-path exclusion and trailing-dot rule. Factor the shared loop so the two cannot drift. Keep the `has_` return contract unchanged; `pulse-dep-graph.sh` and its tests consume it.
- `.agents/hooks/task-id-collision-guard.sh`:
  - Keep the `__malformed__` sentinel in `_extract_tids`. Do not change its grammar; pulse-dep-graph uses the same sentinel.
  - Where `_check_tid` handles the sentinel, look up the offending token with the new function. Report an indented line reading `malformed task identity token '<token>' (in <source>); write <task-id> for placeholders`.
  - In check-pr mode, say whether the token is in the PR title or PR body. `_check_pr_title_body` (around `pr_combined=`) already has both. For commits, say subject or body.
  - Reword the `_report_violations` header so it does not say "Commit subject" when the scanned text was a body or PR text.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/task-identity-lib.sh
- .agents/hooks/task-id-collision-guard.sh

## Acceptance

- A commit or PR body containing `tNNN: plan: ...` is still blocked. The report names `tNNN` and `body`.
- Valid IDs, padded legacy IDs (`t001` → `use t1`), brief paths and trailing-period IDs behave as before.
- `shellcheck -x` is clean on both files. These pass: `.agents/tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-blocked-by.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-prose-dependencies.sh`, and the existing `task-id-collision-guard` tests (`git ls-files '*task-id*guard*test*' '*test*task-id*'`).

title: label-sync-helper.sh docs say admin access is needed; write access is enough
body:
`label-sync-helper.sh` says it needs admin access, but the code and GitHub only need write access:

- Header comment, line 8: "Syncs labels across all repos in repos.json (non-local, admin-accessible)."
- `cmd_sync`, line 583: "Check if we have admin access (can create labels)", followed by `gh label list --repo "$repo" --limit 1`, which only proves read access.
- `_get_admin_repos` selects non-local, non-contributed repos; it does not check admin rights.

GitHub lets anyone with write access create, edit and delete labels (https://docs.github.com/en/issues/using-labels-and-milestones-to-track-work/managing-labels). So a machine account with Write, the setup the docs recommend for the pulse, can run `label-sync-helper.sh sync --repo owner/repo` itself. Reading "admin-accessible" led us to plan creating the labels by hand with an admin login.

Suggested fix:
- Line 8: "Syncs labels across all repos in repos.json that are not local-only or contributed; creating labels needs write access."
- Line 583: "Skip a repo we cannot read; creating labels below needs write access."
- Rename `_get_admin_repos` to `_get_managed_repos`.

Seen at 81d5070c (VERSION 3.39.189).

title: consolidated: perf(pulse): lead first waves with prefetch-visible new arrivals and bound census latency
body:
_Supersedes #38200 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Make the pulse first wave lead with repositories that have prefetch-visible launchable new arrivals, stop serving a mostly consumed candidate snapshot for a census-length window, and treat candidate-enumeration `elapsed` as a first-class latency target. Expose the effect as a `first_wave_new_arrival_lead` stat in `pulse-health.json`.

## Why

Follow-up to #38022 / PR #38024. A 20-slot runner (70 pulse-enabled repositories, deployed v3.39.189 with #38024) again ran at `workers=4/20` (2026-11-14 01:30–01:55 UTC). The product repository at registry index 4 had **15 clean launchable issues**: `auto-dispatch`, `status:available`, no assignee, no claim comment, closed native blockers. `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh issue <N>` on one of them showed no backoff, no blockers and no attempts. The issues arrived between 00:55 and 01:44 UTC: a batch publication added new cores, and phases became unblocked when their cores closed.

Pulse log (local host):

```text
Dispatch_max: available=20, candidates=105     # earlier census reached the product repo
...
candidate enumeration timing census=full outcome=ok elapsed=739s sample=recorded
Dispatch_max: available=16, candidates=1
candidate enumeration timing census=full outcome=ok elapsed=554s sample=snapshot_hit
Dispatch_max: available=18, candidates=1       # wpallstars/seoprocookieconsent#207 only
Dispatch_max: #207 (...) blocked:dedup_pr_evidence benign dispatch block
Minimum worker floor refill stopped: dispatch_max returned 0 (no eligible candidates or hard gate exhausted)
pulse-health.json written: workers=4/20 (x5 consecutive)
```

`~/.aidevops/cache/pulse-first-wave-cursor` = `wpallstars/seoprocookieconsent` (index 61 of 70). In the meantime the other fleet runners claim the product repository's new issues. This host contributes 3–4 workers out of a 20-worker target.

Later evidence from the same runner, about 25 minutes after a cursor nudge (per @marcusquinn):

```text
Substage: preflight_early_dispatch (0, 2678s)
Dispatch_max: candidate enumeration timing census=full outcome=ok elapsed=2079s sample=recorded estimate=300s->745s (GH#37623)
Dispatch_max: available=18, candidates=107
Dispatch_max stopping early: cooperative drain requested for activated bundle 3.39.190-... during parallel loop (GH#37907)
Dispatch path=max complete: implementation_dispatched=0 ... processed=0/107 simultaneous_worker_slots_targeted=18
pulse-health.json written: workers=1/20
```

- With the cursor nudged, the census reached the product repository and found 107 candidates. The nudge fixes reachability, so the ordering diagnosis holds.
- The census itself took **2079 s**, and the cycle's early-dispatch substage took 2678 s. The v3.39.190 bundle activated during that window, so its cooperative drain stopped the loop before any launch. The runner sat at 1–2 of 20 workers for the whole time.
- So the second gap (enumeration latency) matters as much as the ordering. A census that takes longer than the release cadence can be pre-empted by every bundle activation.

### Root cause

#38024 lets a repository lead the first-wave rotation only while the first-wave snapshot still has **unconsumed** candidates for it (`_dispatch_first_wave_backlog_repos`, `pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh:230-239`; consumed via `${snapshot}.consumed`). Two gaps remain:

1. **New arrivals have no lead signal.** Once every candidate known from the last census is attempted, the repository drops back into plain rotation (`_dispatch_repository_rows`, `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:318-349`). Candidates are consumed on every attempt, including `rc=3` / `dedup_active_claim_durable_launch` losses to other runners. Work that appears afterwards — new issues, or phases unblocked by a closed core — is invisible until the cursor comes back round. With 70 repositories and 3–12 minute censuses, that takes about one wave in three.
2. **A snapshot hit can still take a full census duration.** The 554 s `sample=snapshot_hit` round served a snapshot captured before the call started (`_dispatch_enumeration_served_snapshot`, `pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh:940-955`). Freshness is `max(ttl, census_seconds)` (`_dispatch_candidate_snapshot_is_fresh`, `pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh:52-58`), so a 739 s census keeps a mostly consumed snapshot "fresh" for more than 12 minutes. Confirm where the 554 s went before changing anything. It may have been lock wait or prepass work rather than the read.

Line references are from the v3.39.189 parent brief; re-locate the functions by name on current `main` before editing.

## How

1. **Prior implementation (best-effort recovery).** PR #38208 (`GH#38200: perf(pulse): lead first waves with prefetch-visible new arrivals`) was closed with merge conflicts against `main` that `gh pr update-branch` could not resolve; the conflicts are semantic (same files modified on both branches, 6 files touched: `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`, `pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh`, `pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh`, `pulse-logging.sh`, `tests/test-pulse-dispatch-candidate-snapshot.sh`, `tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh`). Its reviews contain no `CHANGES_REQUESTED`, so the approach was not rejected. Both of its commits were verified reachable from the remote ref `refs/pull/38208/head` on 2026-11-14 via `gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/commits/<sha>`:
   - `ef40d7b714543019029e159d9a690da29e31595c` — `GH#38200: perf(pulse): lead first waves with prefetch-visible new arrivals`
   - `0f01f51fe70c5d978ffca3d4f382a5372d2cc502` (PR head) — `GH#38200: fix(pulse): exclude expired snapshots from arrival hints`

   The conflict-feedback guidance names only the head commit; cherry-pick **both** commits, in order, onto a fresh branch off current `origin/main` (never the old PR branch, never canonical HEAD per t2802):

   ```bash
   git fetch origin pull/38208/head:recovered-38208
   git cherry-pick ef40d7b714543019029e159d9a690da29e31595c 0f01f51fe70c5d978ffca3d4f382a5372d2cc502
   ```

   If the cherry-pick surfaces conflicts, resolve those specific hunks — the conflict surface IS the semantic overlap — rather than rewriting untouched logic. Best-effort recovery: reuse if reachable; the functional spec is the source of truth; re-implement if unrecoverable.

2. **Zero-API new-arrival lead hint.** The issue prefetch (`_prefetch_repo_issues`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch-fetch.sh:498-523`, "using cycle canonical snapshot") has each repository's open issues with labels and assignees. Count `auto-dispatch` + `status:available` + unassigned issues per repository, minus attempt-recency keys, and put repositories with a non-zero count ahead of the plain rotation. Keep this stable partition next to the existing #38024 backlog partition (`_dispatch_first_wave_backlog_repos` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh`, consumed by `_dispatch_repository_rows` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`). Repositories with no launchable work keep GH#33647 rotation fairness. The prior PR's follow-up commit also excludes expired snapshots from arrival hints; keep that behaviour.

3. **Stale-for-first-wave snapshot rule.** Treat a snapshot whose unconsumed remainder is smaller than the free slots as stale for the first wave, while the prefetch-hint repositories hold launchable issues the snapshot does not contain. Re-enumerate those repositories first, instead of serving the remainder for a census-length window (`_dispatch_enumeration_served_snapshot` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh`; `_dispatch_candidate_snapshot_is_fresh` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh`). First confirm where the 554 s `snapshot_hit` round went (lock wait, prepass work, or the read).

4. **Enumeration latency as a first-class target** (per @marcusquinn). Treat census `elapsed` as a target: a per-repository time budget, or concurrent enumeration of the repositories that have launchable work, so a census cannot outlast the release cadence and be pre-empted by every bundle activation's cooperative drain (GH#37907). Verify that #38024's remainder retention launches the (107) already-enumerated candidates in the next cycle without re-enumerating.

5. **Health stat.** Add `first_wave_new_arrival_lead` to `pulse-health.json`. Integration scope recovery (worker, 2026-11-14): `.agents/scripts/pulse-logging.sh` is in scope. The `pulse-health.json` document is written only by `write_pulse_health_file` there, and dispatch runs inside command substitutions, so the requested `first_wave_new_arrival_lead` field must be derived in that writer from the cycle's `pulse-stats.json` counter events (the same pattern as `_pulse_cycle_index_budget_skips`). Verification: the two tests below plus `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-cycle-state-contract.sh` (exercises `write_pulse_health_file`) and ShellCheck on the edited file.

Read-only reference: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-cycle-state-contract.sh` (verification of `write_pulse_health_file`; not in the write surface).

Fix-the-fixer: this work touches the worker dispatch path (`fix-the-fixer`, `tier:thinking`). Workers dispatched on it run through the code being fixed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh` covers 70 repositories, cursor past the product repository, the first-wave snapshot fully consumed for it, and the prefetch fixture listing 15 fresh launchable issues there, and asserts that the product repository is scanned in the next first wave.
- [ ] Inverse case: a repository with no prefetch-visible launchable issues keeps its rotation position (GH#33647 fairness preserved).
- [ ] A snapshot whose unconsumed remainder is smaller than the free slots is treated as stale for the first wave while prefetch-hint repositories hold launchable issues it does not contain; those repositories are re-enumerated first.
- [ ] The source of the 554 s `snapshot_hit` latency is identified (lock wait, prepass, or read) before the freshness change, and recorded in the PR.
- [ ] Census `elapsed` is bounded (per-repository time budget or concurrent enumeration of repositories with launchable work), and #38024's remainder retention is verified to launch already-enumerated candidates in the next cycle without re-enumerating.
- [ ] `pulse-health.json` contains `first_wave_new_arrival_lead`, derived in `write_pulse_health_file` from the cycle's `pulse-stats.json` counter events.
- [ ] `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh`, `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-candidate-snapshot.sh` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-cycle-state-contract.sh` pass; ShellCheck is clean on every edited file.
- [ ] Live: on a many-repository runner, within two cycles of new `status:available` issues appearing in one repository, `Dispatch_max: available=N, candidates=M` shows M ≥ min(N, new issues), and `pulse-health.json` `workers=` approaches the target.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch-fetch.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-logging.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-candidate-snapshot.sh

## Context & Decisions

- Original problem, root cause, proposed fix, verification and the `pulse-logging.sh` integration scope recovery: #38200 (interactive brief; scope recovery added by a worker on 2026-11-14).
- per @marcusquinn: the cursor nudge fixes reachability, confirming the ordering diagnosis; enumeration latency (2079 s census, 2678 s early-dispatch substage pre-empted by the v3.39.190 cooperative drain) matters as much as ordering, so `elapsed` is a first-class target (per-repository time budget or concurrent enumeration), and #38024's remainder retention must launch the enumerated candidates next cycle without re-enumerating.
- per @alex-solovyev (automated self-hosting detector): `tier:thinking` applied because the body matches `pulse-dispatch-`; workers fixing the dispatch path run through it. Bypass: `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_SELF_HOSTING_DETECTOR=1`.
- per @vladimirdulov (automated fix-the-fixer detector, t3077): `fix-the-fixer` classification — workers run with `AIDEVOPS_VERBOSE_LIFECYCLE=1`, `WORKER_STALL_TIMEOUT=180`, `AIDEVOPS_WORKER_PREFLIGHT_SENTINEL=1`. Remove the label to dispatch with default settings if the classification is wrong.
- Conflict feedback (pulse-merge.sh, PR #38208): prior implementation was correct-but-stale against `main`; recover by cherry-pick onto a fresh `origin/main` branch, resolve only the overlapping hunks, do not reuse the old branch. No scope-leak warning applies (6 files). Consolidation note: the PR has two commits, so both must be picked.

## Related

#38022 / PR #38024 (unattempted backlog lead), GH#33647 / GH#34331 (first-wave fairness and bounded census), GH#37623 (census timing), GH#37907 (cooperative drain on bundle activation), #37874 (ranked-list reuse), #37888 (REST budget; `gh api user` per round at `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:712` is part of that), PR #38208 (prior conflicting implementation).

title: privacy guard: public vendor domain already in the target public repo is blocked as a private repo/client name
body:
## Observed

`privacy-guard-helper.sh` (pre-push and `gh-write-helper.sh` public-write scans) blocks any new line containing a public vendor domain when a private repo in `repos.json` is named after that domain (repo basename `example.com`, the site's own repo) and the site inventory lists the same host as a client site. The block fires as `[private-repo]` (bare basename match) and `[private-client]`.

The domain is the public shop of the public plugin repo being pushed: the same string is already on dozens of lines in that public repo (credits, update server, links). Changing one constant from `https://www.<domain>/` to `https://www.<domain>/?page_id=N` is blocked, though nothing new is disclosed. The only exits are `PRIVACY_GUARD_DISABLE=1` / `--no-verify` (needs owner authorization each time) or code that splits the string (guard evasion).

## Expected

A private entity that already occurs in the target public repo's tracked content at the base commit (or is declared public for that repo) is not a new disclosure. Options:

1. Skip an entity when `git grep -F` finds it in the target repo's base tree (cheap, per push), or
2. A per-repo public-allow list (for example `.aidevops/privacy-public-terms.txt` in the target repo, or a `public_terms` field on the repos.json entry), checked in `privacy_scan_public_text()`.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/privacy-guard-helper.sh`: `privacy_scan_public_text()` (entity loop, bare-basename branch), the diff scanner at the end of the file.
- `.agents/scripts/test-privacy-guard.sh`: regression case (entity present in base tree → allowed; new private name → still blocked).
- `reference/pre-push-guards.md`: document the rule.

## Verification

`test-privacy-guard.sh` passes, with a case where a private repo basename equals a domain already in the public repo's base tree (allowed) and one where it is not (blocked).

title: gh-audit scanner: one torn NDJSON line permanently blocks anomaly scanning
body:
# Problem

A single torn write in `~/.aidevops/logs/gh-audit.log` permanently disables GH audit
anomaly scanning on the affected runner. `gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh scan` fails closed
on any unparsable line in the scan window, refuses to advance its checkpoint, and so
replays the same corrupt window forever. Audit anomaly detection is silently blind from
the moment of the first torn line.

## Observed

Runner `alex-solovyev`, verified 2026-11-14:

```text
$ gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh status
Log lines:  12471
Last scan:  2026-10-31T09:03:28Z
Last line:  9511
Unscanned:  2960 entries

$ gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh scan --dry-run
[GH-ANOMALY] Scanning 2960 entries (Lines 9512–12471 of `gh-audit.log`)
[GH-ANOMALY WARN] Malformed audit NDJSON detected — checkpoint not advanced
[GH-ANOMALY WARN] Audit scan aborted without updating state
```

The checkpoint has not advanced for 14 days. Cause is line 9605 of the live log: a
truncated record (`{"ts":"2026-10-31T18`) with no trailing newline, immediately followed
on the same physical line by a complete later record. One partial append plus the
missing newline merged two events into one unparsable line.

## Root causes

1. `gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh` `_cmd_scan_collect_anomalies()` treats a jq parse failure
   anywhere in the window as a reason to abort and preserve the checkpoint. Fail-closed is
   correct for *suppression* decisions, but applying it to *checkpoint progress* converts
   one corrupt line into indefinite loss of detection.
2. `gh-audit-log-helper.sh` appends with a bare `printf '%s\n' "$event" >>"$log_file"`
   with no newline-termination check and no `flock`, so an interrupted or short write
   leaves the file without a trailing newline and the next event concatenates onto it.

## Fix

Files to modify:

- `.agents/scripts/gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh`
  - In `_cmd_scan_collect_anomalies()`: partition the window into parsable NDJSON and
    malformed lines before running `gh-audit-anomaly-filter.jq`. Count malformed lines in
    a caller-scoped `_sc_malformed_count`, run the expected-transition filter on the
    parsable subset only, and keep `return 1` only when the filter program itself fails on
    valid JSON (genuine fail-closed).
  - In `cmd_scan()` / `_cmd_scan_build_issue_body()`: report malformed lines as a
    first-class log-integrity finding, and file the alert when `malformed > 0` even if no
    `suspicious[]` anomalies were found. Malformed lines must never be silently dropped —
    corruption of an append-only audit log is itself the alert.
- `.agents/scripts/gh-audit-log-helper.sh`
  - Make the append newline-safe and serialized: when the log's last byte is not `\n`,
    prefix the record with `\n` so a prior partial write cannot swallow the next event;
    wrap the append in `flock` when available.
- `.agents/reference/gh-audit-log.md`: document malformed-line reporting and the recovery
  expectation (the log stays immutable; the corrupt physical line is reported, not edited).

Reference pattern: the existing fail-closed boundary and `# aidevops:trust-boundary`
comments in `_cmd_scan_collect_anomalies()`; expected-transition suppression lives in
`gh-audit-anomaly-filter.jq` and must stay unchanged.

Tests: extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-audit-anomaly-expected-transitions.sh` or add
a sibling test that feeds a window containing one torn line plus one real anomaly, and
asserts the scan reports both, exits 0, and advances the checkpoint.

## Verification

1. `shellcheck .agents/scripts/gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh .agents/scripts/gh-audit-log-helper.sh`
2. New/extended test passes.
3. On the affected runner: `gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh scan --dry-run` reports the
   malformed line count and the real anomalies instead of aborting; after a non-dry-run
   scan, `status` shows `Last line: 12471` and `Unscanned: 0`.

## Context

Found while reviewing #38068 (GH audit anomaly alert). The five anomalies in that alert
were benign `status:in-progress` → `status:in-review` lifecycle transitions already
suppressed by #38161; this scanner blindness is the real defect behind it.

title: fix(blocker-recovery): seed cursor resumes after the interrupted repo, starving the slow repo's seed and the unclassified-hold intake
body:
## What

Fix a resume livelock in `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh` seed intake. Today, a repo whose seed pass does not fit the stage cap is retried behind the repos that do fit, so it never completes. As a side effect, the GH#37978 unclassified-hold stage is starved on every `pending` run.

## Why

Observed on one supervisor runner on 2026-11-14 across 8 consecutive `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh pending` runs (each ~45 s):

```
blocker-recovery: checking stage=seed_policy repo=marcusquinn/aidevops
blocker-recovery: checking stage=seed_candidates repo=marcusquinn/aidevops
blocker-recovery: checking stage=seed_comments repo=marcusquinn/aidevops issue=35359
blocker-recovery: checking stage=seed_policy repo=<private-product-repo>
blocker-recovery: checking stage=seed_candidates repo=<private-product-repo>
blocker-recovery: incomplete stage=seed rc=124
blocker-recovery: incomplete stage=unclassified reason=budget_exhausted
```

The order was the same every run, and the seed never completed. Mechanism, read from the deployed script:

- `tbr_seed` saves `seed_repo_cursor` as the slug it is **about to start** (`.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh:309`).
- The next run calls `_tbr_rotate "$repos" "$repo_cursor"` (`:297-298`). `_tbr_rotate` (`:162-166`) puts entries strictly **greater** than the cursor first: `map(select(. > $cursor)) + map(select(. <= $cursor))`.
- The interrupted repo therefore moves to the back. A repo that completes quickly (here `marcusquinn/aidevops`, 3 searches + 1 issue) always runs first and uses most of the seed cap: `reserve = min(BUDGET/2, TBR_STAGE_SECONDS)`, which is 8 s by default (`:79`, `:1385-1387`). The larger repo then times out in `_tbr_seed_candidates`, which runs 3 GitHub searches (`:340-351`).
- Because the seed returns incomplete, `last_seed_epoch` is never written (`:332-334`), so `TBR_SEED_INTERVAL` never throttles it. It runs, and fails, on every pass.
- `unclassified` runs after the seed against the same overall deadline (`:1437-1445`). The seed has already used up the remaining time, so unclassified holds (GH#37978) are never discovered on a runner with a non-empty queue.

The same "save the item being started, then resume after it" pattern applies to the per-repo issue cursor (`:320-326`) and to the call at `:461`. There, an issue that cannot finish in the remaining time is skipped forward rather than retried. That is less harmful but has the same root cause.

## How

- Resume **at** the interrupted entry, not after it. Either save the cursor only after an entry or repo completes (save the last *completed* item, which keeps today's `_tbr_rotate` semantics correct), or add an inclusive rotate variant (`>=`) for the start-of-work cursors. Pick one convention and apply it to `seed_repo_cursor` (`:297-309`), the per-repo seed issue cursor (`:320-326`) and the `:461` caller. Check that the queue cursor (`:1397-1423`) still advances as intended. It deliberately advances past a timed-out entry so one slow entry cannot block the lap, so do not change it unless you confirm the same livelock there.
- Make sure the seed cannot use up the unclassified stage's share. For example, give `unclassified` its own reserve, or run it before the seed when the seed did not complete on the previous run. Keep the GH#36114 / GH#37978 constraints in the comments at `:113-133` and `:1389-1391`.
- Keep the existing guarantees: a timeout is never evidence that a hold resolved (`:107-108`), and the overall deadline and stage caps still bound each run.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: .agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With two pulse repos, where the alphabetically later one completes within the cap and the earlier one does not, consecutive `pending` runs start with the repo that was interrupted last time, and that repo eventually completes its seed.
- [ ] After a seed completes, `last_seed_epoch` is written and `TBR_SEED_INTERVAL` throttles the next seed as before.
- [ ] The `unclassified` stage gets a non-zero budget at least on runs where the seed is throttled or completed, so `intake: unclassified_hold` entries can appear on a runner with a large queue.
- [ ] Existing terminal-blocker tests still pass: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit*.sh`.
- [ ] ShellCheck reports zero violations for the edited script.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit-discovery.sh`
- Production check: on a runner with a non-empty queue, run `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh pending` three times. The stderr `seed_policy repo=` order should start with the previously interrupted repo, and one run should either complete the seed or record progress past `seed_candidates` for that repo.

title: fix(pulse-merge): treat check runs with conclusion+completed_at as terminal in pre-merge snapshot
body:
## What

The pulse pre-merge snapshot treats a check run as active when GitHub reports `status: in_progress` even though the same check run already has a `conclusion` and a `completed_at` time. GitHub sometimes leaves a check run in this state after an Actions incident. The workflow run is `completed/success`, and GitHub itself reports the PR as `mergeStateStatus: CLEAN`. The pulse still logs `not ready (active=1, blocking_failures=0, ...)` on every pass, so approved, green PRs never merge.

## Evidence (2026-11-14)

- PRs in a private managed repo with `reviewDecision=APPROVED` and `mergeStateStatus=CLEAN` stayed open for 12+ hours. Two examples: one check run was `Core Gate Summary` and the other was `E2E Shard 1/4`. Both check runs returned `{"status":"in_progress","conclusion":"success","completed_at":"2026-11-13T17:42:57Z"}` from `GET repos/{owner}/{repo}/check-runs/{id}`. Both started at the same second (17:42:51Z), which points to a single GitHub-side incident.
- Their parent workflow runs returned `status: completed, conclusion: success`.
- `pulse.log`: `pre-merge snapshot: PR #N ... not ready (active=1, blocking_failures=0, advisory_failures=0) (GH#27137)` repeated each cycle.

## Why it matters

Every runner shares this code. One stuck status blocks an otherwise mergeable PR indefinitely. The only way out is a person noticing and merging by hand, which is the user-time cost aidevops exists to remove.

## Fix

In `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-required-checks.sh` `_pmrc_normalize_snapshot_checks_json`, normalize a check run's status to `completed` when it has both a non-empty `conclusion` and a non-null `completed_at`. GitHub's API contract sets a conclusion only once a check run is complete (supplying a conclusion forces `status: completed`), so both fields together are terminal evidence. Genuinely active runs have neither field, so they stay pending. Failure conclusions keep blocking as before, because the conclusion is still evaluated.

## Files

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-required-checks.sh` (`_pmrc_normalize_snapshot_checks_json`, check_run mapping near `status: ((.status // "") | ascii_downcase)`)

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-required-checks.sh`
- Run the existing pre-merge snapshot tests (`rg -l '_pmrc_normalize_snapshot_checks_json\|pre-merge snapshot' .agents/scripts/tests`).
- Pipe the live check-run JSON shape into the normalizer and confirm the result is `status: completed, conclusion: success`. An `in_progress` run with a null conclusion must stay `in_progress`.

title: fix(checkpoints): draft checkpoint stranded when issue is unassigned with no release comment (orphaned terminal lease)
body:
## What

A worker draft checkpoint gets stranded for good when the issue ends up unassigned and back at `status:available` with no worker release comment. Every runner then logs this on each pass:

`STALLED_CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_SKIPPED: PR #N in <repo> has no current stall release issue=#M`

and reports `DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked`. Nothing continues the draft, nothing redispatches the issue, and nothing raises attention. The objective stalls until a person notices.

## Reproducer (live, 2026-11-14)

Issue #38112 with draft PR #38132, as recorded in the issue comments and events:

1. 18:03:50Z `DISPATCH_CLAIM` → 18:05:25Z `Dispatching worker` → 18:05:29Z `DISPATCH_LEASE phase=ready`. All of these came from the authoring runner.
2. 18:07:13Z: the worker opened draft PR #38132. Its checks are green and it has no failing contexts.
3. 18:08:09Z `DISPATCH_LEASE phase=terminal`. **No release comment was ever posted.**
4. 20:48:56Z: the same runner removed the assignee and moved the issue to `status:available`, again with no release comment.
5. Since then, every pass on this runner logs `WORKER_DRAFT_CHECKPOINT ... ordinary redispatch is blocked` followed by `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_SKIPPED ... has no current stall release`.

Scale: one runner's `pulse.log` shows **24 distinct draft PRs** in this state (20 in one private repo, 2 in this repo, 2 elsewhere), with 69 skip lines. Those re-evaluations also take a large share of dispatch time: `dedup.7_layers` and `dedup.dedup_check` add up to about 21.7 hours of serial work per 24 hours, and the most re-evaluated candidates are draft-checkpoint holds.

## Why

`_pcc_dispatch_stalled` (`.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`, around lines 1787-1831) continues a draft only when `_pcc_stall_release_evidence` (around line 1361) finds a trusted, unedited release comment whose reason matches `_PCC_STALL_RELEASE_PATTERN`. If the release comment is missing (a silent unassign, or a terminal lease with no release), the last ownership event never passes `stall_release`. `_pcc_dispatch_expired_recovery_draft` then returns 3 (not applicable), and the helper prints SKIPPED.

This family has come up before: #33839 (own terminal lease blocks the draft), #35363 (`stale_assignment_reset` strands the draft) and #38103 (failed continuation launch). Each fix covered one specific release reason. The remaining case is **no release comment at all**.

## Fix

Treat an orphaned draft checkpoint as stall-equivalent, keeping the existing bounded continuation and fuse:

- Conditions: the PR is an open draft by a trusted runner; the issue has no assignees; the latest trusted ownership event after the PR was created is a `DISPATCH_LEASE phase=terminal` (or there is no later claim or ready lease); no release comment follows it; and it is older than a grace window. Reuse an existing TTL such as the stale-assignment threshold rather than adding a new knob.
- When all of these hold, synthesize the release reason `orphaned_terminal_lease`, add it to `_PCC_STALL_RELEASE_PATTERN`, and use the lease's comment id and time as the release boundary. Per-head stall counts, the PR release fuse and attention keep working unchanged, so a draft that keeps stalling still escalates to attention instead of looping.
- Optional, as a separate small change: find the path that unassigns without posting a release (likely stale-assignment recovery or worker cleanup on the authoring runner) and make it post its release reason. The continuation-side fix is still needed for drafts that are already stranded and for releases lost on other devices.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`

Targets: `_pcc_stall_release_evidence`, `_pcc_dispatch_stalled` and `_PCC_STALL_RELEASE_PATTERN`. If `_PCC_JQ_RELEASE_DEFS` lives in a sourced file (`rg -n '_PCC_JQ_RELEASE_DEFS=' .agents/scripts`), that file is in scope too.

Coordination: #38105 (file-size split of this helper, assigned to another runner). If it merges first, rebase on it, and keep this change local to the evidence and dispatch functions.

## Verification

- Existing tests: `rg -l 'dispatch-stalled|_pcc_stall_release_evidence' .agents/scripts/tests` and run each one.
- Use the live #38112/#38132 comment JSON (`gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/38112/comments`) as the case: `_pcc_stall_release_evidence` should return a release row with reason `orphaned_terminal_lease`, and `dispatch-stalled` should launch one exact-head continuation, not SKIPPED.
- Negative cases: an assigned issue still SKIPs; a terminal lease younger than the grace window still SKIPs; a later claim or ready lease from any runner still fences.
- After deploy, `rg -c 'has no current stall release' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` should stop growing for the stranded PRs, which should get continuations or attention records instead.

title: perf(dispatch): negative cache self-invalidates on runner coordination comments — 23h/day of ceremony on non-launch outcomes
body:
## What

The cross-cycle dispatch negative cache (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`: `_dispatch_negative_cache_record`, `_dispatch_negative_cache_reason`, `_dispatch_prefilter_owned_candidate`) is meant to let the pulse skip blocked candidates without re-running the dedup ceremony. Each record is keyed on the issue's `updatedAt`. Runners post coordination comments (`DISPATCH_CLAIM`, `DISPATCH_LEASE`, `CLAIM_RELEASED`, `CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_APPROVED`) to the same issue, and every one of those comments bumps `updatedAt`. Busy issues therefore invalidate their own cache records almost immediately, and the pulse pays the full ceremony every time.

## Reproducer

Data: one runner, about 27 h of `pulse.log` from 2026-11-13T03:00Z.

**Symptom command:** `rg -o 'dispatch_with_dedup returned rc=[0-9]+ for #[0-9]+ elapsed_ms=[0-9]+' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | awk '{split($3,a,"="); split($6,b,"="); n[a[2]]++; s[a[2]]+=b[2]} END {for (k in n) printf "rc=%s n=%d avg_s=%.0f total_h=%.1f\n", k, n[k], s[k]/n[k]/1000, s[k]/3600000}'` and `rg -o 'cross-cycle ownership block:[a-z_]+' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | sort | uniq -c`

**Actual output:** see the first two bullets below. The cache produced 15 hits against 740 blocked ceremonies.

**Root cause (confirmed by reading):** `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:493` in `_dispatch_negative_cache_reason` returns a miss unless `cached == updated`. The only exception is `$_DISPATCH_LIVE_OWNER_HOLD_REASON`. Its comment at `:491-492` already names this failure mode for that one reason: "The refused attempt's own claim comment bumps updatedAt". `_dispatch_negative_cache_record` (`:393`) stores the candidate's prefetched `updatedAt`, so the ceremony's own coordination comments can invalidate the record it just wrote.

- `dispatch_with_dedup` outcomes: rc=0 (launched) n=49, avg 389 s, 5.3 h total. rc=1 (blocked) n=541, avg 73 s, 11.0 h. rc=3 (durable block) n=199, avg 85 s, 4.7 h. rc=2 (pre-launch failure) n=50, avg 327 s, 4.5 h. rc=124 n=17, avg 630 s, 3.0 h. **About 23 h of ceremony time went to outcomes that launched nothing.**
- Negative-cache hits (`cross-cycle ownership block:`) numbered **15** in the same window, against 740 rc=1 plus rc=3 ceremonies.
- `~/.aidevops/logs/dispatch-negative-cache/` holds 1,706 records. Most are older than 6 h (`dedup_active_claim` 780, `dedup_active_claim_durable_launch` 347, `worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked` 104, ...), so they no longer match the current `updatedAt`.
- Example: one issue in a private managed repo received **47 comments in 24 h**, all from runners: 13x `DISPATCH_LEASE phase=prelaunch`, 4x `phase=ready`, 5x `CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_APPROVED`, 3x `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=worker_complete`, 2x `claim_only_no_worker`, and others. Its cache record was keyed on an `updatedAt` from four days earlier. Every pass re-ran the ceremony, which re-posted coordination comments, which bumped `updatedAt` again.

## Why it matters

The ceremony takes 73-85 s even when it ends in a block. With 20 slots, this runner averaged about 1.2 concurrent workers, because its dispatch time went into re-proving known blocks. The coordination comments also wake every other runner, so the cost repeats across the fleet.

## Fix

Key the invalidation on material changes and ignore coordination noise:

1. At write time (`_dispatch_negative_cache_record`), also store a material fingerprint built from data already in the candidate JSON: sorted labels, sorted assignee logins, and a body hash when `.body` is present. Reuse `_dispatch_capability_fingerprint` (`pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh`) rather than adding a new hasher. Records without the new field keep today's exact-`updatedAt` behaviour.
2. At read time (`_dispatch_negative_cache_reason`, `:493`), when the only mismatch is `updatedAt`, accept the record only if (a) the material fingerprint still matches, and (b) one bounded REST read, `issues/{n}/comments?since=<recorded updatedAt>&per_page=100`, returns only ops/audit comments. Ops comments are the ones with an `<!-- ops:start` marker, or a first token of `DISPATCH_CLAIM`, `DISPATCH_LEASE`, `CLAIM_RELEASED`, `CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_APPROVED` or `Dispatching worker`. Use the existing ops-marker classifier if there is one (`rg -n 'ops:start' .agents/scripts`); do not write a parallel list. If the read fails, returns 100 comments, or the body hash is unavailable while the issue body may have changed, treat it as a miss (fail closed, as today). On a hit, rewrite the record's `updatedAt` so the next pass needs no read. One read is far cheaper than a 73 s ceremony.
3. Leave the TTLs, reason allowlists, the claimed-owner snapshot check (`:494-500`) and the fresh final gates before claim and launch unchanged. Cache hits stay advisory: they only skip the ceremony.
4. Keep the GH#37780 rule: an empty local pool still re-checks claims this runner could own.

**Reference pattern:** the live-owner hold exception at `pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:491-493`, which already decouples one reason from `updatedAt`, and the fingerprint helpers `_dispatch_checkpoint_fingerprint` / `_dispatch_capability_fingerprint` in `pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh:1234-1255`.

Out of scope: the separate draft-checkpoint stranding (#38236) and multi-runner claim contention.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`

## Verification

- Run the existing tests: `test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh`, `test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh`, and any other file `rg -l '_dispatch_negative_cache' .agents/scripts/tests` returns.
- Unit probe with fixture comments: a record whose `updatedAt` changed only because of ops comments returns the cached reason. A human or maintainer comment, a body edit or a label change after the stamp invalidates it.
- After deploy, `rg -c 'cross-cycle ownership block:' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` should grow by hundreds per day, and the summed rc=1/rc=3 `elapsed_ms` from `rg -o 'dispatch_with_dedup returned rc=[13] for #[0-9]+ elapsed_ms=[0-9]+'` should fall substantially.

title: perf(worktree): archive terminal cleanup receipts — reconcile_scan opens 5,181 files under the receipt lock (18-55 s per launch under vnode churn)
body:
## What

Every worker launch runs `precreate.verify.reconcile_scan` (`_full_loop_recreated_receipt_scan`, `.agents/scripts/full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh:889-944`) while holding the global receipt lock. The scan opens every file in `~/.aidevops/state/full-loop-cleanup/*.json`, which is currently **5,181 files**. **4,481** of them are terminal `CLEANED` receipts and **4,450** are older than 7 days. GH#38149 / PR #38177 reduced this to one jq pass, which takes 0.37 s interactively. In the pulse it still takes **18-55 s** on most launches, and because the receipt lock is held throughout, every concurrent launch waits behind it (`precreate.verify.reconcile_lock` max 40 s).

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `awk -F'\t' '$1>="2026-11-14T02:10" && $4=="precreate.verify.reconcile_scan" {print $1, $3, $5}' ~/.aidevops/logs/dispatch-stages.tsv`

**Actual output** (ms, one runner, after v3.39.190 deployed #38177):

```text
2026-11-14T03:11:15Z <large repo> 27671
2026-11-14T03:15:18Z <large repo> 21601
2026-11-14T03:28:23Z <large repo> 55472
2026-11-14T04:34:56Z <large repo> 29140
2026-11-14T06:47:40Z <large repo> 22408
2026-11-14T06:47:40Z <small repo> 360
2026-11-14T06:49:55Z <small repo> 364
2026-11-14T06:56:06Z <large repo> 18676
2026-11-14T06:56:07Z <small repo> 379
```

Pattern: a scan that follows another within about 2 minutes is fast; one after a gap of 4 minutes or more is slow.

## Root cause (measured)

1. **Not path- or repo-dependent.** A read-only probe that sources the helper and calls `_full_loop_recreated_receipt_scan` on both worktree paths takes 0.37-0.38 s for each.
2. **Not plain load, writeback or metadata contention.** The probe stays at 0.40-0.60 s at load average 28 on 16 cores, alongside a concurrent 16 GB sequential write, and alongside 8 concurrent extractions of about 76k small files.
3. **Throttled I/O reproduces it.** `taskpolicy -b` on the same probe gives **14-56 s**, which matches production. The pulse runs as `com.aidevops.aidevops-supervisor-pulse` with no `ProcessType`. launchd.plist(5) describes that default as "light resource limits ... throttling its CPU usage and I/O bandwidth". A one-shot LaunchAgent with identical keys measured 0.8-1.2 s, 2-3x slower than interactive, with warm vnodes.
4. **The vnode cache is saturated.** `sysctl kern.num_vnodes kern.maxvnodes` reports `263168 263168`, and `kern.num_recycledvnodes` reports 1.2 billion over 5.5 days of uptime. That is about 2,540 recycles/s on average, so the whole table turns over roughly every 100 s, driven by worktree churn. The 5,181 receipt vnodes are evicted between launches, so each slow scan re-resolves 5,181 files through throttled-tier metadata I/O. A scan right after another hits warm vnodes, which explains the fast-after-slow pairs.

The cost scales with the number of files opened under the lock, and 86% of those files are terminal history.

## Fix

Archive terminal receipts out of the hot glob so the scan opens about 730 files instead of 5,181:

1. Under the receipt lock, move receipts whose `resource_cleanup_state == "CLEANED"` and whose newest timestamp is older than `AIDEVOPS_CLEANUP_RECEIPT_ARCHIVE_DAYS` (default 7, 0 = off) into `~/.aidevops/state/full-loop-cleanup/archive/YYYY-MM/`. Use atomic `mv` on the same filesystem and preserve file mode. That subdirectory is outside `"$receipt_dir"/*.json`, so no glob changes are needed.
2. Run the archival as a bounded, rate-limited housekeeping step (at most once per hour per runner), not in the launch path. The existing reconciliation sweep near `full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh:1199-1203`, or the routine that calls `:1841`, is the natural host; pick the one already outside dispatch.
3. **Consumer audit (required before archiving):** every whole-set reader is in `full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh` (`:725-727`, `:758-791`, `:808-840`, `:862-871`, `:889-942`, `:1054`, `:1841-1843`). For each one, confirm that a missing `CLEANED` receipt older than 7 days is safe. For example, `full_loop_supersede_cleaned_receipts_for_recreated_worktree` treats "no history for path" as status 2 and proceeds, which is correct for a terminal receipt. Fixed-path producers (GH#37706) recreate paths within minutes, not after 7 days. If any reader needs archived history, have it consult `archive/` only on its miss path; never widen the hot glob.
4. Leave `CLEANUP_DEFERRED` and `CLEANUP_LEASED` receipts and every validator's fail-closed behaviour unchanged.

Optional, needs host owner action, not in this PR: raise `kern.maxvnodes` on worker hosts. That reduces churn everywhere, but it needs sudo and does not survive a reboot without a LaunchDaemon. Mention it in the PR body only.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh`

## Verification

- Existing tests: `rg -l 'full-loop-cleanup-receipt|cleanup_receipt' .agents/scripts/tests` and run each, especially the recreated-worktree and reconciliation suites.
- Probe: archive in a fixture directory with old `CLEANED`, recent `CLEANED`, `DEFERRED` and `LEASED` receipts. Only old `CLEANED` receipts move, and a recreated-path reconciliation for an archived path still returns its no-history status.
- After deploy: the `fd -t f -e json . ~/.aidevops/state/full-loop-cleanup --max-depth 1 | wc -l` count drops to about the 7-day volume. The symptom command shows `reconcile_scan` mostly under 5 s, and `precreate.verify.reconcile_lock` max under 10 s.

title: perf(pulse-merge): cache immutable commit-by-SHA, /user and per-process permission reads — 36% of merge-routine REST; merges deferred 60-85% of starts
body:
## What

The pulse merge routine defers as "optional" whenever core REST remaining is at or below the GH#37278 worker reserve (20%). On this runner, **60-85% of merge-routine starts each hour** log `Worker REST reserve reached; deferring optional merge routine` (`~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-merge-routine.log`). Finished worker PRs therefore sit unmerged: at 2026-11-14T07:15Z there were **16 open, non-draft, checks-green PRs** across managed repos, all idle for more than 40 minutes. The reserve is correct, because it stops the merge routine starving workers (GH#37278). What needs to change is the merge routine's cost, which is mostly reads whose answer cannot change or changes rarely.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `awk -F'\t' -v s=<window_start> -v e=<window_end> '$1>=s && $1<e && $2=="pulse-merge-routine.sh" && $9=="attempt" {split($25,p,"?"); c[$23" "p[1]]++} END {for (k in c) printf "%5d %s\n", c[k], k}' ~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls.log | sort -rn`

**Actual output** (one full hourly window ending 2026-11-14T07:11Z, 742 merge-routine attempts in total):

```text
  357 unknown unknown
  157 GET repos/:o/:r/pulls/:id
  133 GET repos/:o/:r/commits/:id
  101 GET repos/:o/:r/collaborators/:u/permission
   79 GET repos-other
   77 GET repos/:o/:r/pulls/:id/reviews
   36 GET repos/:o/:r/issues/:id
   30 GET user
```

Deferral rate: `rg -n 'deferring optional merge routine' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-merge-routine.log | rg -o '2026-11-1[34]T[0-9]{2}' | sort | uniq -c` against the same count for `Starting merge routine`. For example, at 03Z it was 27 of 31 starts and at 04Z 15 of 20.

## Fix

Cache the reads that are immutable or slow-changing. **264 of 742 calls/hour (36%)** need no network:

1. **Commit by SHA (133/h), immutable.** There are three readers: `pulse-merge-rest-state.sh:536` (`_pmrs_head_commit_age_seconds`, `.commit.committer.date`), `pulse-merge-conflict.sh:340` (activity time) and `pulse-merge-conflict.sh:552` (`.files`). Add one helper, for example `gh_commit_by_sha_cached <repo> <sha>`, that stores the raw REST response under `~/.aidevops/cache/gh-commit/<owner>--<repo>/<sha>.json` (mode 600, atomic tmp+mv). It is valid forever for a 40/64-hex SHA, and should be pruned by mtime after 7 days in existing pulse cleanup. Never cache an error or empty body. Callers keep their own `--jq` by running jq on the cached file.
2. **Authenticated login (`GET /user`, 30/h).** It is constant for a process. Memoize it per process in `pulse-merge-gates.sh:930` and `pulse-merge-feedback-ci-repair.sh:1349`. First check whether `shared-gh-wrappers-session.sh:331-337` or another shared helper already exposes a cached login, and reuse it if so (`rg -n 'api user' .agents/scripts`).
3. **Collaborator permission (101/h).** This is a `#aidevops:trust-boundary` path (`shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh`, `_gh_collaborator_permission_lookup`). Memoize per process only, keyed on `repo|login`, and cache only successful lookups. Do not add a cross-process TTL cache in this issue: that would delay revocation and needs a separate decision.
4. Leave the GH#37278 worker reserve and every merge gate unchanged.

Out of scope: the `unknown` attribution bucket (GH#37888 / PR #37889 owns attribution) and the review-page cache from GH#37278 item 4, unless it is already absent. If it is absent, note it in the PR body as a follow-up.

title: perf(cloudron): skip unchanged pending approval requests in r924 — 3,769 REST calls/day polling human-gated releases
body:
## What

Routine r924 (`.agents/scripts/routines/core-routines.sh:42`, `cron(*/30 * * * *)`) runs `cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh process --apply` across all 10 maintained `cloudron-package` repos. While releases wait for a human-signed approval, every run re-does the full authority resolution for each unchanged pending request. That costs **3,769 core REST calls/day** (about 157/h, about 3% of every hourly window) on this runner, and nothing changes until a human signs.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `awk -F'\t' -v s=<epoch_24h_ago> '$1>=s && $2=="cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh" && $5=="rest-core" && $9=="attempt"' ~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls.log | wc -l`

**Actual output:** `3769` for the 24 h ending 2026-11-14T08:53Z. One hourly window broke down as `issues` list 56, `repos-other` 47, `contents/:id` 32, `issues/:id` 30, `pulls/:id` 27, unattributed 76 (199 total).

## Fix

In `release_process_issue` (`cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh:581-668`), when `release_resolve_authority` returns 3 (`NO_APPROVAL`/`STALE_APPROVAL`), record a per-request fingerprint at `~/.aidevops/cache/cloudron-release-approval/<owner>--<repo>-<issue>`. The fingerprint is the request issue's `updated_at`, the bound `head` from `release_metadata`, the repo's standing-policy issue `updated_at` (from the list `release_policy_issue` already fetches), and the epoch. On the next run, after the single `before` GET (`:586`), skip the issue entirely when the fingerprint matches and is younger than `AIDEVOPS_CLOUDRON_APPROVAL_RECHECK_SECONDS` (default 21600, 0 = off). A signature or any comment bumps `updated_at`, so a new approval is picked up on the next run. Never skip when the verdict was anything other than rc=3, and never skip the post-merge publication-resume path (`:641-667`).

Optional, same PR: skip `release_reconcile_held` / `release_retry_interrupted` for a repo when its approval-issue list and held-PR list are identical to the previous run's (compare a hash of the numbers plus `updated_at`).

`#aidevops:trust-boundary`: the skip only avoids re-reading. It never grants authority, and every merge still re-verifies at the exact head (`:625-631`).

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh`

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-release-approval.sh` passes.
- Probe with a stubbed `gh`: a pending, unchanged request is evaluated once, then skipped on the second run (1 call instead of 15+). Bumping `updated_at` or the policy issue re-evaluates it, and a recorded rc=1 failure is never skipped.
- After deploy, the symptom command's 24 h count drops by at least 70% while approvals are pending.

title: perf(pulse-merge): human-gated retry hints and draft enrichment starve merge-ready PRs
body:
## Problem

Merge-ready worker PRs in `marcusquinn/aidevops` wait hours for the deterministic merge pass. The repo is visited about once per hour, and each visit processes only one or two PRs. That PR is often a human-gated draft or `hold-for-review` PR, not a merge-ready one.

## Reproducer

Observed on 2026-11-14 with runtime 3.39.191. To reproduce, check `pulse.log` for `PR backlog marcusquinn/aidevops:` lines and the `Merge pass:` lines that follow them. Then compare with `gh pr checks 38231 --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --required`.

- PR #38231 (GH#38228) and PR #38233 (GH#38229): `MERGEABLE`, all required checks passing, `review-bot-gate` passing, `maintainer-gate` passing. The merge pass did not evaluate either PR across several hourly visits.
- `pulse.log` visit at about 07:57Z: `PR backlog marcusquinn/aidevops: total=15, merge-ready=4, ... human-approval-needed=9`. The only PR processed was #37768, which was skipped with `PR is draft or has hold-for-review`. After that: `graceful time budget exhausted ... pausing at PR cursor index=1 next_pr=38244`. Timing row: `total_s=206 enrichment_s=103 pr_s=22 other_s=76 slowest_pr=#37768:22s`.
- Visit at about 07:00Z: `merge-ready=1` at sorted index 0, followed by `resuming marcusquinn/aidevops at PR cursor index=6 last_pr=37889 next_pr=37733`. The walk then evaluated only three draft PRs at the tail and finished. The merge-ready PR was never visited.
- Dirty queue `~/.aidevops/state/pulse-merge-dirty/work.sqlite3`: the row for `marcusquinn/aidevops|37768` has a non-empty generation, `durable=1`, and `updated` from 2026-11-11. This is a deferred feedback-route retry hint. The PR is now draft/hold-for-review, so the evaluator returns 1 every time, `_pulse_merge_queue_finish 1` keeps the generation, and the hint lasts until the 7-day retention expires.

## Root causes

1. `_pmp_sort_prs_by_backlog_priority` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-backlog.sh:158-193`) puts the retry key first. A durable retry hint on a draft or `hold-for-review` PR therefore outranks every merge-ready PR on every visit.
2. `_process_single_ready_pr` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh:1699-1731`) finishes the queue lease as unhandled when a human gate rejects the PR: the draft check in `_pmp_stage_parse_and_validate` (`pulse-merge.sh:1283-1286`) or the live draft/hold check in `_pm_gate_origin_authority` (`pulse-merge.sh:618-631`). The durable hint cannot be satisfied until a human acts. Until it expires, it also makes the repo unfingerprintable for the GH#33569 unchanged-skip (`pulse-merge-unchanged-skip.sh:56`), so every visit pays for full backlog enrichment.
3. Draft PRs are enriched twice per visit. The advisory backlog snapshot does it in `_pmp_prepare_enriched_pr_backlog` (`pulse-merge-pass.sh:520-592`). The authoritative per-cursor step does it again in `_pmp_prepare_pr_at_cursor` (`pulse-merge-backlog.sh:268-324`). Each pass makes three REST reads per draft (mergeability, checks, reviews), but the evaluator rejects drafts from list fields before it reads any enriched field. Backlog classification also maps drafts to `human-approval-needed` before it looks at enrichment.
4. On resume, `_pmp_prepare_merge_pr_cursor_resume` (`pulse-merge-pass.sh:190-229`) starts at the saved `next_pr`. A PR that became merge-ready since the last walk, and that sorts before the cursor, is skipped until the walk wraps.

## Proposed fix

- Sorting: grant `retry_priority=0` only when the listed PR is neither draft nor labelled `hold-for-review`. This changes ordering only; every gate still runs.
- Queue lifecycle: when the draft gate or the live draft/hold gate rejects the PR, acknowledge the claimed hint as handled. Polling stays authoritative, and a later ready/unhold event creates a new generation.
- Enrichment: skip advisory and authoritative enrichment for PRs whose fresh list object has `isDraft == true`. Fill in `UNKNOWN` placeholders so the evaluator's draft rejection behaves exactly as before.
- Resume lane: on a resumed walk, move up to `PULSE_MERGE_RESUME_PRIORITY_LIMIT` (default 2) merge-ready PRs from before the cursor to just ahead of it. Newly ready work is then evaluated first, while the cursor still guarantees forward progress through the tail.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-backlog.sh`: sort retry key, draft enrichment skip, resume lane helper.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-pass.sh`: draft skip in `_pmp_prepare_enriched_pr_backlog`.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh`: apply the resume lane after `_pmp_prepare_merge_pr_cursor_resume`.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`: human-gate flag and queue acknowledgement.
- Existing tests: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-pr-backlog-priority.sh`, `test-pulse-merge-pr-cursor-resume.sh`, `test-pulse-merge-dirty-queue.py`.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-pr-backlog-priority.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-pr-cursor-resume.sh`
- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-dirty-queue.py`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-unchanged-skip.sh`
- ShellCheck on the modified scripts.
- Runtime: after deploy, the next `marcusquinn/aidevops` visit processes merge-ready PRs before #37768, the #37768 hint row is deleted, and the timing row shows lower `enrichment_s`.
